For males, a full-time mission is two years in length, and for females it lasts 18 months.
rewrite: Approximately 97% of male and 32% of female graduates of Brigham Young University (BYU) have historically interrupted their undergraduate studies to serve as missionaries for The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints (LDS). A significant policy shift was announced during the October 2012 LDS General Conference, lowering the eligible age for missionary service. Young men may now begin service at age 18 following high school graduation, rather than at 19, potentially altering the traditional composition of BYU’s incoming freshman class, as many previously enrolled briefly in higher education first. For young women, the eligible age was reduced from 21 to 19. The standard duration of full-time missionary service is two years for men and eighteen months for women.

input: A district of Himachal Pradesh is an administrative geographical unit, headed by a Deputy Commissioner or District Magistrate, an officer belonging to the Indian Administrative Service. The district magistrate or the deputy commissioner is assisted by a number of officers belonging to Himachal Administrative Service and other Himachal state services. Each district is subdivided into Sub-Divisions, governed by a sub-divisional magistrate, and again into Blocks. Blocks consists of panchayats (village councils) and town municipalities. A Superintendent of Police, an officer belonging to the Indian Police Service is entrusted with the responsibility of maintaining law and order and related issues of the district. He is assisted by the officers of the Himachal Police Service and other Himachal Police officials.
rewrite: Within the administrative framework of Himachal Pradesh, a district constitutes a primary geographical and governmental division. It is administered by a District Magistrate or Deputy Commissioner, a senior officer of the Indian Administrative Service. This official is supported by subordinate officers from the Himachal Administrative Service and other state civil services. Each district is further segmented into Sub-Divisions, overseen by a Sub-Divisional Magistrate, and subsequently into Blocks. These Blocks encompass both panchayats (village councils) and municipal towns. Law enforcement and public order within the district fall under the purview of a Superintendent of Police, an officer of the Indian Police Service, who is assisted by personnel from the Himachal Police Service and other state police ranks.

input: As federal judge Alex Kozinski has pointed out, binding precedent as we know it today simply did not exist at the time the Constitution was framed. Judicial decisions were not consistently, accurately, and faithfully reported on both sides of the Atlantic (reporters often simply rewrote or failed to publish decisions which they disliked), and the United Kingdom lacked a coherent court hierarchy prior to the end of the 19th century. Furthermore, English judges in the eighteenth century subscribed to now-obsolete natural law theories of law, by which law was believed to have an existence independent of what individual judges said. Judges saw themselves as merely declaring the law which had always theoretically existed, and not as making the law. Therefore, a judge could reject another judge's opinion as simply an incorrect statement of the law, in the way that scientists regularly reject each other's conclusions as incorrect statements of the laws of science.
rewrite: As noted by federal judge Alex Kozinski, the contemporary doctrine of binding precedent was absent at the nation's founding. During the constitutional era, judicial decisions were not reliably documented in either Britain or America, as reporters frequently altered or omitted opinions they disfavored. Moreover, the United Kingdom lacked a unified judicial hierarchy until the late nineteenth century. Additionally, eighteenth-century English jurisprudence was guided by natural law theories, now largely obsolete, which posited law as an independent entity discoverable by judges. Within this framework, judges viewed their role as declaratory, merely identifying preexisting legal principles rather than creating law. Consequently, a judge could dismiss a prior judicial opinion as an erroneous declaration of law, analogous to a scientist rejecting a colleague's conclusion for misstating a scientific law.

input: There are hundreds of distinct neighborhoods throughout the five boroughs of New York City, many with a definable history and character to call their own. If the boroughs were each independent cities, four of the boroughs (Brooklyn, Queens, Manhattan, and the Bronx) would be among the ten most populous cities in the United States.
rewrite: New York City's five boroughs contain hundreds of distinct neighborhoods, each possessing its own historical character. Were they independent cities, four boroughs—Brooklyn, Queens, Manhattan, and the Bronx—would rank among the ten most populous in the United States.

input: In the 1990s, protesters criticised the company's environmental record, particularly the possible pollution caused by the proposed disposal of the Brent Spar platform into the North Sea. Despite support from the UK government, Shell reversed the decision under public pressure but maintained that sinking the platform would have been environmentally better. Shell subsequently published an unequivocal commitment to sustainable development, supported by executive speeches reinforcing this commitment.
rewrite: During the 1990s, the company faced significant public criticism over its environmental practices, notably concerning the proposed deep-sea disposal of the Brent Spar platform in the North Sea. Although endorsed by the UK government, Shell rescinded the plan due to public pressure, while asserting its environmental preferability. The corporation subsequently issued an explicit commitment to sustainable development, a stance further reinforced in subsequent executive communications.

input: The history of Latin canon law can be divided into four periods: the jus antiquum, the jus novum, the jus novissimum and the Code of Canon Law. In relation to the Code, history can be divided into the jus vetus (all law before the Code) and the jus novum (the law of the Code, or jus codicis).
rewrite: The historical development of Latin canon law is categorized into four periods: the *jus antiquum*, *jus novum*, *jus novissimum*, and the Code of Canon Law. Regarding the Code, history is further divided into the *jus vetus* (all preceding law) and the *jus novum* (the law of the Code, or *jus codicis*).

input: Scholars and historians are divided as to what event signals the end of the Hellenistic era. The Hellenistic period may be seen to end either with the final conquest of the Greek heartlands by Rome in 146 BC following the Achean War, with the final defeat of the Ptolemaic Kingdom at the Battle of Actium in 31 BC, or even the move by Roman emperor Constantine the Great of the capital of the Roman Empire to Constantinople in 330 AD. "Hellenistic" is distinguished from "Hellenic" in that the first encompasses the entire sphere of direct ancient Greek influence, while the latter refers to Greece itself.
rewrite: Academic consensus regarding the terminal event of the Hellenistic era remains divided. Proposed conclusions include the Roman conquest of mainland Greece in 146 BCE, the defeat of the Ptolemaic Kingdom at the Battle of Actium in 31 BCE, or the relocation of the Roman imperial capital to Constantinople in 330 CE. The term "Hellenistic" itself denotes the extensive sphere of direct Greek cultural and political influence following Alexander the Great, in contrast to "Hellenic," which pertains specifically to classical Greece itself.

input: During World War I, the palace, then the home of King George V and Queen Mary, escaped unscathed. Its more valuable contents were evacuated to Windsor but the royal family remained in situ. The King imposed rationing at the palace, much to the dismay of his guests and household. To the King's later regret, David Lloyd George persuaded him to go further by ostentatiously locking the wine cellars and refraining from alcohol, to set a good example to the supposedly inebriated working class. The workers continued to imbibe and the King was left unhappy at his enforced abstinence. In 1938, the north-west pavilion, designed by Nash as a conservatory, was converted into a swimming pool.
rewrite: During the First World War, Buckingham Palace, the residence of King George V and Queen Mary, remained undamaged. While its most valuable contents were removed for safekeeping at Windsor, the royal family stayed in London. The King instituted rationing within the palace, a measure unpopular with the household and guests. Subsequently, Prime Minister David Lloyd George persuaded the monarch to adopt a more symbolic gesture of austerity: publicly locking the wine cellars and abstaining from alcohol to model restraint for the industrial workforce, whom he characterized as prone to drunkenness. This policy proved ineffective in curbing popular consumption and was a source of personal dissatisfaction for the King. Later, in 1938, the north-west pavilion, originally designed by John Nash as a conservatory, was remodeled into a swimming pool.

input: According to the endurance running hypothesis, long-distance running as in persistence hunting, a method still practiced by some hunter-gatherer groups in modern times, was likely the driving evolutionary force leading to the evolution of certain human characteristics. This hypothesis does not necessarily contradict the scavenging hypothesis: both subsistence strategies could have been in use – sequentially, alternating or even simultaneously.
rewrite: The endurance running hypothesis posits that persistence hunting served as a primary evolutionary driver for distinct human traits. This view remains compatible with the scavenging hypothesis, as both subsistence strategies could have been employed sequentially, alternately, or concurrently.

input: To compete with the popular Family Computer in Japan, NEC Home Electronics launched the PC Engine in 1987, and Sega Enterprises followed suit with the Mega Drive in 1988. The two platforms were later launched in North America in 1989 as the TurboGrafx-16 and the Genesis respectively. Both systems were built on 16-bit architectures and offered improved graphics and sound over the 8-bit NES. However, it took several years for Sega's system to become successful. Nintendo executives were in no rush to design a new system, but they reconsidered when they began to see their dominance in the market slipping.
rewrite: In response to the popularity of Nintendo's Family Computer in Japan, NEC Home Electronics released the PC Engine in 1987, with Sega Enterprises introducing the Mega Drive in 1988. These 16-bit consoles, which offered superior graphics and audio capabilities compared to the 8-bit Nintendo Entertainment System, subsequently launched in North America in 1989 as the TurboGrafx-16 and the Genesis, respectively. While the Mega Drive required several years to achieve commercial success, its growing market presence ultimately prompted Nintendo, whose executives had initially been reluctant to develop a successor, to reconsider its strategy in order to address its eroding market dominance.

input: Von Neumann is credited with the equilibrium strategy of mutual assured destruction, providing the deliberately humorous acronym, MAD. (Other humorous acronyms coined by von Neumann include his computer, the Mathematical Analyzer, Numerical Integrator, and Computer—or MANIAC). He also "moved heaven and earth" to bring MAD about. His goal was to quickly develop ICBMs and the compact hydrogen bombs that they could deliver to the USSR, and he knew the Soviets were doing similar work because the CIA interviewed German rocket scientists who were allowed to return to Germany, and von Neumann had planted a dozen technical people in the CIA. The Russians believed that bombers would soon be vulnerable, and they shared von Neumann's view that an H-bomb in an ICBM was the ne plus ultra of weapons, and they believed that whoever had superiority in these weapons would take over the world, without necessarily using them. He was afraid of a "missile gap" and took several more steps to achieve his goal of keeping up with the Soviets:
rewrite: John von Neumann is credited with formulating the equilibrium strategy of mutual assured destruction, for which he devised the deliberately ironic acronym MAD. (This reflects his penchant for such coinages, as exemplified by his computer, the Mathematical Analyzer, Numerical Integrator, and Computer—or MANIAC.) He actively and vigorously promoted the realization of this doctrine. His objective was to accelerate the development of intercontinental ballistic missiles (ICBMs) and the compact thermonuclear warheads they could deliver against the Soviet Union. Aware of parallel Soviet efforts through intelligence channels—including CIA debriefings of repatriated German rocket scientists and his own placement of technical personnel within the Agency—von Neumann understood the strategic competition. Soviet strategists, sharing his assessment, viewed thermonuclear-armed ICBMs as the ultimate weapon system, believing that supremacy in this domain could confer global dominance without necessitating their actual use. Fearing a potential "missile gap," von Neumann undertook further measures to ensure the United States maintained parity with Soviet advancements.

input: Because of their ability to quickly grow and the relative ease with which they can be manipulated, bacteria are the workhorses for the fields of molecular biology, genetics and biochemistry. By making mutations in bacterial DNA and examining the resulting phenotypes, scientists can determine the function of genes, enzymes and metabolic pathways in bacteria, then apply this knowledge to more complex organisms. This aim of understanding the biochemistry of a cell reaches its most complex expression in the synthesis of huge amounts of enzyme kinetic and gene expression data into mathematical models of entire organisms. This is achievable in some well-studied bacteria, with models of Escherichia coli metabolism now being produced and tested. This understanding of bacterial metabolism and genetics allows the use of biotechnology to bioengineer bacteria for the production of therapeutic proteins, such as insulin, growth factors, or antibodies.
rewrite: Due to their rapid growth rates and genetic tractability, bacteria serve as fundamental model organisms within molecular biology, genetics, and biochemistry. Researchers analyze phenotypic outcomes following targeted DNA mutations to elucidate gene function, enzymatic roles, and metabolic pathways. Insights gained from these prokaryotic systems are frequently extrapolated to more complex organisms. This foundational aim of cellular biochemical understanding achieves its most sophisticated form through the integration of extensive enzyme kinetic and gene expression datasets into comprehensive mathematical models. Such whole-organism models, now being constructed and validated for well-characterized bacteria like *Escherichia coli*, represent a significant advance. Furthermore, this detailed knowledge of bacterial genetics and metabolism enables their biotechnological application, including the bioengineering of strains for the synthesis of therapeutic proteins like insulin, growth factors, and antibodies.

input: The Hephthalites (or Ephthalites), also known as the White Huns, were a nomadic confederation in Central Asia during the late antiquity period. The White Huns established themselves in modern-day Afghanistan by the first half of the 5th century. Led by the Hun military leader Toramana, they overran the northern region of Pakistan and North India. Toramana's son Mihirakula, a Saivite Hindu, moved up to near Pataliputra to the east and Gwalior to the central India. Hiuen Tsiang narrates Mihirakula's merciless persecution of Buddhists and destruction of monasteries, though the description is disputed as far as the authenticity is concerned. The Huns were defeated by the Indian kings Yasodharman of Malwa and Narasimhagupta in the 6th century. Some of them were driven out of India and others were assimilated in the Indian society.
rewrite: The Hephthalites, alternatively termed the Ephthalites or White Huns, constituted a nomadic confederation that emerged in Central Asia during late antiquity. By the early fifth century, they had established a polity in the territory of present-day Afghanistan. Under the command of the Hun leader Toramana, they subsequently expanded into northern Pakistan and northwestern India. His successor, Mihirakula, a devotee of Saivite Hinduism, extended this reach eastward toward Pataliputra and centrally to Gwalior. The seventh-century pilgrim Xuanzang (Hiuen Tsiang) records Mihirakula’s severe persecution of Buddhists and the razing of monasteries, although the historical veracity of this account is debated. In the sixth century, a coalition of Indian rulers, notably Yasodharman of Malwa and Narasimhagupta, ultimately defeated the Hephthalites. Following their military reversal, a segment was expelled from the subcontinent while the remainder was gradually assimilated into indigenous society.

input: The Han dynasty was an age of economic prosperity and saw a significant growth of the money economy first established during the Zhou dynasty (c. 1050–256 BC). The coinage issued by the central government mint in 119 BC remained the standard coinage of China until the Tang dynasty (618–907 AD). The period saw a number of limited institutional innovations. To pay for its military campaigns and the settlement of newly conquered frontier territories, the government nationalized the private salt and iron industries in 117 BC, but these government monopolies were repealed during the Eastern Han period. Science and technology during the Han period saw significant advances, including papermaking, the nautical steering rudder, the use of negative numbers in mathematics, the raised-relief map, the hydraulic-powered armillary sphere for astronomy, and a seismometer employing an inverted pendulum.
rewrite: The Han dynasty was characterized by considerable economic prosperity and a marked expansion of the monetary economy, which had initially emerged during the Zhou dynasty (c. 1050–256 BC). The coinage minted by the central government in 119 BC became the standard currency in China until the Tang dynasty (618–907 AD). This era witnessed several limited institutional innovations. To finance military campaigns and the colonization of newly acquired frontier regions, the state nationalized the private salt and iron industries in 117 BC, though these monopolies were later abolished in the Eastern Han period. Significant progress was also made in science and technology, including developments in papermaking, the nautical sternpost rudder, the mathematical application of negative numbers, raised-relief cartography, a hydraulic-powered armillary sphere for astronomy, and a seismometer utilizing an inverted pendulum.

input: Following the announcement of Nasser's death, Egypt and the Arab world were in a state of shock. Nasser's funeral procession through Cairo on 1 October was attended by at least five million mourners. The 10-kilometer (6.2 mi) procession to his burial site began at the old RCC headquarters with a flyover by MiG-21 jets. His flag-draped coffin was attached to a gun carriage pulled by six horses and led by a column of cavalrymen. All Arab heads of state attended, with the exception of Saudi King Faisal. King Hussein and Arafat cried openly, and Muammar Gaddafi of Libya fainted from emotional distress twice. A few major non-Arab dignitaries were present, including Soviet Premier Alexei Kosygin and French Prime Minister Jacques Chaban-Delmas.
rewrite: The announcement of Gamal Abdel Nasser’s death precipitated a profound state of shock throughout Egypt and the broader Arab world. His funeral procession in Cairo on 1 October drew no fewer than five million mourners. The cortege, spanning ten kilometers to his interment site, commenced at the former Revolutionary Command Council headquarters, preceded by a flyover of MiG-21 aircraft. Nasser’s flag-draped coffin, borne on a gun carriage drawn by six horses, was led by a cavalry column. With the noted absence of Saudi King Faisal, all other Arab heads of state attended. King Hussein and Yasser Arafat wept openly, while Libya’s Muammar Gaddafi fainted twice from emotional distress. Several prominent non-Arab dignitaries were also present, including Soviet Premier Alexei Kosygin and French Prime Minister Jacques Chaban-Delmas.

input: Since the beginning of the study of electricity non conductive materials like glass, porcelain, paper and mica have been used as insulators. These materials some decades later were also well-suited for further use as the dielectric for the first capacitors. Paper capacitors made by sandwiching a strip of impregnated paper between strips of metal, and rolling the result into a cylinder were commonly used in the late 19century; their manufacture started in 1876, and they were used from the early 20th century as decoupling capacitors in telecommunications (telephony).
rewrite: From the inception of electrical science, non-conductive materials such as glass, porcelain, paper, and mica served as insulators. Decades later, these same substances proved equally suitable as dielectrics in early capacitors. Notably, paper capacitors, constructed by rolling metal strips around impregnated paper into a cylindrical form, entered manufacture in 1876. Prevalent by the late nineteenth century, they saw widespread application from the early twentieth century onward as decoupling components within telephonic telecommunications systems.

input: Programmes, such as the politically fuelled Give My Head Peace (produced by BBC Northern Ireland) and the soap opera River City (produced by BBC Scotland), have been created specifically to cater for some viewers in their respective nations, who may have found programmes created for English audiences irrelevant. BBC Scotland produces daily programmes for its Gaelic-speaking viewers, including current affairs, political and children's programming such as the popular Eòrpa and Dè a-nis?. BBC Wales also produces a large amount of Welsh language programming for S4C, particularly news, sport and other programmes, especially the soap opera Pobol y Cwm ('People of the Valley'). The UK nations also produce a number of programmes that are shown across the UK, such as BBC Scotland's comedy series Chewin' the Fat, and BBC Northern Ireland's talk show Patrick Kielty Almost Live.
rewrite: Broadcasters within the United Kingdom produce dedicated programming to serve the distinct linguistic and cultural needs of the devolved nations. For instance, BBC Northern Ireland and BBC Scotland have created series like *Give My Head Peace* and *River City*, respectively, to provide content more relevant to local audiences than productions aimed primarily at England. Furthermore, substantial indigenous-language output is maintained. BBC Scotland delivers daily Gaelic programming, including current affairs and children's shows like *Eòrpa* and *Dè a-nis?*, while BBC Wales produces extensive Welsh-language content for S4C, spanning news, sport, and the enduring soap opera *Pobol y Cwm*. Concurrently, these nations also contribute content for UK-wide distribution, exemplified by comedy series such as *Chewin' the Fat* and talk shows like *Patrick Kielty Almost Live*.

input: Dismayed to find that groundbreaking work had already been undertaken by Helmholtz who had conveyed vowel sounds by means of a similar tuning fork "contraption", he pored over the German scientist's book. Working from his own erroneous mistranslation of a French edition, Bell fortuitously then made a deduction that would be the underpinning of all his future work on transmitting sound, reporting: "Without knowing much about the subject, it seemed to me that if vowel sounds could be produced by electrical means, so could consonants, so could articulate speech." He also later remarked: "I thought that Helmholtz had done it ... and that my failure was due only to my ignorance of electricity. It was a valuable blunder ... If I had been able to read German in those days, I might never have commenced my experiments!"[N 7]
rewrite: Upon discovering with disappointment that Hermann von Helmholtz had already conducted pioneering research, having reproduced vowel sounds through a comparable tuning fork apparatus, Bell meticulously studied the German scientist's publication. Proceeding from an inaccurate translation of a French edition, Bell subsequently arrived at a fortuitous deduction that would form the foundation of his subsequent work in sound transmission. He noted: "Without knowing much about the subject, it seemed to me that if vowel sounds could be produced by electrical means, so could consonants, and thus articulate speech." Bell later reflected: "I believed Helmholtz had accomplished this... and that my initial failure stemmed merely from my limited understanding of electricity. It was a valuable mistake... Had I been proficient in German at the time, I might never have begun my experiments!"[N 7]

input: In Surely You're Joking, Mr. Feynman!, he gives advice on the best way to pick up a girl in a hostess bar. At Caltech, he used a nude or topless bar as an office away from his usual office, making sketches or writing physics equations on paper placemats. When the county officials tried to close the place, all visitors except Feynman refused to testify in favor of the bar, fearing that their families or patrons would learn about their visits. Only Feynman accepted, and in court, he affirmed that the bar was a public need, stating that craftsmen, technicians, engineers, common workers, "and a physics professor" frequented the establishment. While the bar lost the court case, it was allowed to remain open as a similar case was pending appeal.
rewrite: In his work *Surely You’re Joking, Mr. Feynman!*, Richard Feynman recounts advising on social approaches within a hostess bar. During his tenure at Caltech, he regularly utilized a nude or topless bar as an alternative workspace, often drafting sketches or writing physics equations on paper placemats. When local authorities attempted to close the establishment, all other patrons declined to testify in its defense, fearing personal or professional repercussions should their attendance become known. Feynman alone agreed to testify. In court, he asserted that the bar served a public need, noting its patronage by craftsmen, technicians, engineers, laborers, "and a physics professor." Although the bar lost the initial case, it was permitted to remain open pending the appeal of a related legal matter.

input: The period between 1815 and 1871 saw a large number of revolutionary attempts and independence wars. Balkan nations began to regain independence from the Ottoman Empire. Italy unified into a nation state. The capture of Rome in 1870 ended the Papal temporal power. Rivalry in a scramble for empires spread in what is known as The Age of Empire.
rewrite: The era from 1815 to 1871 was characterized by numerous revolutionary movements and wars of independence. Balkan states progressively achieved sovereignty from Ottoman rule, while Italy was consolidated into a unified nation-state. The Papacy's temporal authority concluded with Rome's annexation in 1870. Concurrently, imperial rivalries intensified, defining the so-called Age of Empire.

input: The simplest way to gain information about brain anatomy is by visual inspection, but many more sophisticated techniques have been developed. Brain tissue in its natural state is too soft to work with, but it can be hardened by immersion in alcohol or other fixatives, and then sliced apart for examination of the interior. Visually, the interior of the brain consists of areas of so-called grey matter, with a dark color, separated by areas of white matter, with a lighter color. Further information can be gained by staining slices of brain tissue with a variety of chemicals that bring out areas where specific types of molecules are present in high concentrations. It is also possible to examine the microstructure of brain tissue using a microscope, and to trace the pattern of connections from one brain area to another.
rewrite: The most fundamental method for investigating neuroanatomy is direct visual observation, though numerous more advanced methodologies exist. Native brain tissue possesses a pliable consistency unsuitable for detailed study, but it can be solidified through fixation in agents such as alcohol, subsequently allowing for thin sectioning to examine internal structures. Macroscopically, the cerebral interior comprises regions of grey matter, characterized by a darker hue, interspersed with lighter-toned white matter. Enhanced morphological detail is achieved by applying histological stains to tissue sections; these chemical agents selectively bind to and reveal zones with high concentrations of particular biomolecules. Furthermore, microscopic analysis permits the examination of cytoarchitecture, while specialized techniques enable the mapping of neural pathways between distinct brain regions.

input: Marvel earned a great deal of money and recognition during the comic book boom of the early 1990s, launching the successful 2099 line of comics set in the future (Spider-Man 2099, etc.) and the creatively daring though commercially unsuccessful Razorline imprint of superhero comics created by novelist and filmmaker Clive Barker. In 1990, Marvel began selling Marvel Universe Cards with trading card maker SkyBox International. These were collectible trading cards that featured the characters and events of the Marvel Universe. The 1990s saw the rise of variant covers, cover enhancements, swimsuit issues, and company-wide crossovers that affected the overall continuity of the fictional Marvel Universe
rewrite: Marvel achieved significant financial success and critical acclaim amid the comic book industry's expansion in the early 1990s. This period included the launch of the futuristic and commercially viable 2099 series, such as *Spider-Man 2099*, alongside the creatively bold but less profitable Razorline imprint, developed by novelist and filmmaker Clive Barker. In 1990, Marvel partnered with SkyBox International to produce Marvel Universe Cards, collectibles depicting characters and narratives from its fictional world. The decade also witnessed the proliferation of variant covers, enhanced cover art, swimsuit editions, and extensive cross-over events that reshaped Marvel's overarching continuity.

input: Von Neumann was the first to establish a rigorous mathematical framework for quantum mechanics, known as the Dirac–von Neumann axioms, with his 1932 work Mathematical Foundations of Quantum Mechanics. After having completed the axiomatization of set theory, he began to confront the axiomatization of quantum mechanics. He realized, in 1926, that a state of a quantum system could be represented by a point in a (complex) Hilbert space that, in general, could be infinite-dimensional even for a single particle. In this formalism of quantum mechanics, observable quantities such as position or momentum are represented as linear operators acting on the Hilbert space associated with the quantum system.
rewrite: John von Neumann originated a rigorous mathematical framework for quantum mechanics, formalized as the Dirac–von Neumann axioms in his 1932 treatise *Mathematical Foundations of Quantum Mechanics*. Following his prior axiomatization of set theory, he turned to the foundational structure of quantum theory. As early as 1926, he recognized that a quantum system’s state could be represented by a point within a complex Hilbert space, which may be infinite-dimensional even for a single particle. Within this formalism, observables like position and momentum correspond to linear operators acting upon the system’s associated Hilbert space.

input: Modern computers based on integrated circuits are millions to billions of times more capable than the early machines, and occupy a fraction of the space. Computers are small enough to fit into mobile devices, and mobile computers can be powered by small batteries. Personal computers in their various forms are icons of the Information Age and are generally considered as "computers". However, the embedded computers found in many devices from MP3 players to fighter aircraft and from electronic toys to industrial robots are the most numerous.
rewrite: Contemporary computing systems, founded upon integrated circuitry, demonstrate capabilities millions to billions of times greater than early computers while occupying a substantially reduced physical volume. Their miniaturization enables integration into portable devices powered by compact batteries. Although personal computers in their diverse configurations are emblematic of the Information Age and commonly synonymous with the term "computer," the most prevalent type is the embedded system. These are integrated into a vast array of products, ranging from consumer electronics like MP3 players and toys to specialized equipment such as industrial robots and military aircraft.

input: Countrywide, sued by California Attorney General Jerry Brown for "unfair business practices" and "false advertising" was making high cost mortgages "to homeowners with weak credit, adjustable rate mortgages (ARMs) that allowed homeowners to make interest-only payments". When housing prices decreased, homeowners in ARMs then had little incentive to pay their monthly payments, since their home equity had disappeared. This caused Countrywide's financial condition to deteriorate, ultimately resulting in a decision by the Office of Thrift Supervision to seize the lender.
rewrite: California Attorney General Jerry Brown sued Countrywide for engaging in "unfair business practices" and "false advertising," specifically for issuing high-cost mortgages. These adjustable-rate mortgages (ARMs), often with interest-only terms, were extended to borrowers with poor credit. Subsequently, declining home prices erased homeowner equity, reducing the incentive to maintain monthly payments. This deterioration in loan performance severely weakened Countrywide's financial position, prompting the Office of Thrift Supervision to seize the institution.

input: According to the Hebrew Bible narrative, Jewish ancestry is traced back to the Biblical patriarchs such as Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, and the Biblical matriarchs Sarah, Rebecca, Leah, and Rachel, who lived in Canaan around the 18th century BCE. Jacob and his family migrated to Ancient Egypt after being invited to live with Jacob's son Joseph by the Pharaoh himself. The patriarchs' descendants were later enslaved until the Exodus led by Moses, traditionally dated to the 13th century BCE, after which the Israelites conquered Canaan.[citation needed]
rewrite: The Hebrew Bible recounts that Jewish lineage originates with the patriarchs Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and the matriarchs Sarah, Rebecca, Leah, and Rachel, who resided in Canaan circa the 18th century BCE. Following an invitation from the Pharaoh to Joseph, Jacob's family relocated to Ancient Egypt. Their descendants were subsequently enslaved, preceding the Exodus under Moses—traditionally dated to the 13th century BCE—which was followed by the Israelite conquest of Canaan.

input: In May 2015, a coalition of more than 60 Asian-American organizations filed federal complaints with the Education and Justice Departments against Harvard University. The coalition asked for a civil rights investigation into what they described as Harvard's discriminatory admission practices against Asian-American applicants. The complaint asserts that recent studies indicate that Harvard has engaged in systematic and continuous discrimination against Asian Americans in its "holistic" admissions process. Asian-American applicants with near-perfect test scores, top-one-percent grade point averages, academic awards, and leadership positions are allegedly rejected by Harvard because the university uses racial stereotypes, racially differentiated standards, and de facto racial quotas. This federal complaint was dismissed in July 2015 because the Students for Fair Admissions lawsuit makes similar allegations.
rewrite: In May 2015, a coalition comprising over sixty Asian-American organizations submitted formal complaints to the U.S. Departments of Education and Justice, alleging discriminatory admissions practices by Harvard University. The filings requested a federal civil rights investigation, citing studies purporting to show systematic bias within Harvard's holistic review process. Specifically, the complaints contend that academically exceptional Asian-American candidates—possessing near-perfect standardized test scores, elite grade point averages, and significant extracurricular distinctions—face disproportionate rejection. This outcome is attributed to the alleged application of racial stereotypes, differential standards by race, and de facto racial quotas. The federal complaints were subsequently dismissed in July 2015, as authorities deferred to the parallel litigation advanced by Students for Fair Admissions.

input: The Georgics' tone wavers between optimism and pessimism, sparking critical debate on the poet's intentions, but the work lays the foundations for later didactic poetry. Virgil and Maecenas are said to have taken turns reading the Georgics to Octavian upon his return from defeating Antony and Cleopatra at the Battle of Actium in 31 BC.
rewrite: The Georgics' ambivalent tone, fluctuating between optimism and pessimism, has prompted scholarly debate regarding Virgil's intent, yet the work established essential foundations for subsequent didactic poetry. Tradition holds that Virgil and Maecenas alternately recited the Georgics to Octavian following his victory at the Battle of Actium in 31 BC.

input: IBM has been a leading proponent of the Open Source Initiative, and began supporting Linux in 1998. The company invests billions of dollars in services and software based on Linux through the IBM Linux Technology Center, which includes over 300 Linux kernel developers. IBM has also released code under different open source licenses, such as the platform-independent software framework Eclipse (worth approximately US$40 million at the time of the donation), the three-sentence International Components for Unicode (ICU) license, and the Java-based relational database management system (RDBMS) Apache Derby. IBM's open source involvement has not been trouble-free, however (see SCO v. IBM).
rewrite: As a prominent advocate of the Open Source Initiative, IBM commenced its support for Linux in 1998. The corporation channels billions of dollars into Linux-based services and software via the IBM Linux Technology Center, which employs over 300 developers contributing to the Linux kernel. Furthermore, IBM has released significant code under various open source licenses. Notable contributions include the Eclipse software framework—a platform-independent tool valued at approximately $40 million upon donation—the International Components for Unicode (ICU) under a concise three-sentence license, and the Java-based relational database management system Apache Derby. Nevertheless, IBM's open source engagement has encountered legal challenges, exemplified by the SCO v. IBM litigation.

input: Plans for arena football were put on hold in 1982 as the United States Football League was launched. Foster left the NFL to accept a position in the USFL. He eventually became executive vice-president with the Chicago Blitz, where he returned to his concept of arena football. In 1983, he began organizing the test game in his spare time from his job with the Blitz. By 1985, the USFL had ceased football operations and he began devoting all his time to arena football, and on April 27, 1986, his concept was realized when the test game was played.
rewrite: The development of arena football was initially deferred in 1982 following the establishment of the United States Football League. James Foster departed the National Football League to assume a role within the USFL, ultimately rising to executive vice-president of the Chicago Blitz. In this capacity, he revisited his arena football concept, commencing organization of a test game during his spare time in 1983. After the USFL terminated operations in 1985, he dedicated his efforts fully to the project. The foundational test game was consequently realized on April 27, 1986, materializing his original vision.

input: When auto-changing turntables were commonplace, records were typically pressed with a raised (or ridged) outer edge and a raised label area, allowing records to be stacked onto each other without the delicate grooves coming into contact, reducing the risk of damage. Auto-changers included a mechanism to support a stack of several records above the turntable itself, dropping them one at a time onto the active turntable to be played in order. Many longer sound recordings, such as complete operas, were interleaved across several 10-inch or 12-inch discs for use with auto-changing mechanisms, so that the first disk of a three-disk recording would carry sides 1 and 6 of the program, while the second disk would carry sides 2 and 5, and the third, sides 3 and 4, allowing sides 1, 2, and 3 to be played automatically; then the whole stack reversed to play sides 4, 5, and 6.
rewrite: During the era when automatic record changers were prevalent, phonograph records were manufactured with a raised outer rim and a similarly elevated label area. This design permitted the stacking of multiple discs without allowing the delicate grooves to contact one another, thereby mitigating the risk of surface damage. The automatic changer mechanism itself supported a stack of records above the turntable platter, sequentially dropping each one for playback. To accommodate this technology, extended audio works, such as complete operas, were often distributed across multiple 10-inch or 12-inch discs with an interleaved sequencing. For instance, in a three-disc set, the first disc contained sides 1 and 6 of the program, the second sides 2 and 5, and the third sides 3 and 4. This arrangement enabled the automatic playback of sides 1, 2, and 3; the stack could then be manually reversed to play the remaining sides in order.

input: Tehran is the country's capital and largest city, as well as its leading cultural and economic center. Iran is a major regional and middle power, exerting considerable influence in international energy security and the world economy through its large reserves of fossil fuels, which include the largest natural gas supply in the world and the fourth-largest proven oil reserves. Iran's rich cultural legacy is reflected in part by its 19 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, the fourth-largest number in Asia and 12th-largest in the world.
rewrite: Tehran serves as Iran's capital, largest city, and primary cultural and economic hub. As a significant regional and middle power, Iran wields substantial influence in global energy security and the economy, owing to its extensive fossil fuel reserves. These comprise the world's largest natural gas supply and its fourth-largest proven oil reserves. The nation's profound cultural heritage is evidenced by its 19 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, ranking fourth in Asia and twelfth globally.

input: Model plants such as Arabidopsis thaliana are used for studying the molecular biology of plant cells and the chloroplast. Ideally, these organisms have small genomes that are well known or completely sequenced, small stature and short generation times. Corn has been used to study mechanisms of photosynthesis and phloem loading of sugar in C4 plants. The single celled green alga Chlamydomonas reinhardtii, while not an embryophyte itself, contains a green-pigmented chloroplast related to that of land plants, making it useful for study. A red alga Cyanidioschyzon merolae has also been used to study some basic chloroplast functions. Spinach, peas, soybeans and a moss Physcomitrella patens are commonly used to study plant cell biology.
rewrite: Model organisms in plant biology, such as *Arabidopsis thaliana*, are selected for their utility in investigating cellular and chloroplast molecular mechanisms. Ideal traits include compact, fully sequenced genomes, small physical size, and rapid life cycles. Maize (*Zea mays*) serves as a key system for examining photosynthesis and sugar transport in C4 plants. The unicellular green alga *Chlamydomonas reinhardtii*, though not a land plant, possesses a chloroplast homologous to those of embryophytes, facilitating comparative studies. Additionally, the red alga *Cyanidioschyzon merolae* is employed for fundamental chloroplast research. Other commonly utilized species include spinach, pea, soybean, and the moss *Physcomitrella patens* for broader plant cell biological inquiries.

input: Following the German unconditional surrender, Eisenhower was appointed Military Governor of the U.S. Occupation Zone, based at the IG Farben Building in Frankfurt am Main. He had no responsibility for the other three zones, controlled by Britain, France and the Soviet Union, except for the city of Berlin, which was managed by the Four-Power Authorities through the Allied Kommandatura as the governing body. Upon discovery of the Nazi concentration camps, he ordered camera crews to document evidence of the atrocities in them for use in the Nuremberg Trials. He reclassified German prisoners of war (POWs) in U.S. custody as Disarmed Enemy Forces (DEFs), who were no longer subject to the Geneva Convention. Eisenhower followed the orders laid down by the Joint Chiefs of Staff (JCS) in directive JCS 1067, but softened them by bringing in 400,000 tons of food for civilians and allowing more fraternization. In response to the devastation in Germany, including food shortages and an influx of refugees, he arranged distribution of American food and medical equipment. His actions reflected the new American attitudes of the German people as Nazi victims not villains, while aggressively purging the ex-Nazis.
rewrite: Following Germany's unconditional surrender, General Dwight D. Eisenhower was designated Military Governor of the American Occupation Zone, establishing his headquarters at the IG Farben Building in Frankfurt am Main. His authority was confined to this zone, as the British, French, and Soviet administrations controlled the other three. The sole exception was Berlin, which was governed collectively by the Four-Power Authorities via the Allied Kommandatura. After the liberation of the Nazi concentration camps, Eisenhower mandated that film crews comprehensively document the atrocities to preserve evidence for the subsequent Nuremberg Trials. He also authorized the reclassification of German prisoners of war under U.S. custody as Disarmed Enemy Forces, thereby removing their protections under the Geneva Convention. While implementing the stringent occupation policies outlined in Joint Chiefs of Staff directive JCS 1067, Eisenhower mitigated their severity by importing 400,000 tons of food for civilians and permitting increased fraternization. Confronting widespread devastation, severe food shortages, and a refugee crisis, he facilitated the distribution of American food and medical supplies. These measures embodied a shifting American perception of the German populace as victims of Nazism rather than solely as perpetrators, even while pursuing an aggressive policy of denazification.

input: These critics of the modern separation of church and state also note the official establishment of religion in several of the states at the time of ratification, to suggest that the modern incorporation of the Establishment Clause as to state governments goes against the original constitutional intent.[citation needed] The issue is complex, however, as the incorporation ultimately bases on the passage of the 14th Amendment in 1868, at which point the first amendment's application to the state government was recognized. Many of these constitutional debates relate to the competing interpretive theories of originalism versus modern, progressivist theories such as the doctrine of the Living Constitution. Other debates center on the principle of the law of the land in America being defined not just by the Constitution's Supremacy Clause, but also by legal precedence, making an accurate reading of the Constitution subject to the mores and values of a given era, and rendering the concept of historical revisionism irrelevant when discussing the Constitution.
rewrite: Scholars who challenge contemporary interpretations of the separation of church and state frequently observe that several states maintained officially established religions at the time of the Constitution's ratification. They argue from this historical fact that applying the Establishment Clause to state governments via incorporation contradicts the document's original intent. This constitutional issue is nuanced, however, as the doctrine of incorporation is fundamentally rooted in the Fourteenth Amendment (1868), which subsequently enabled the application of the First Amendment to the states. Such debates often engage broader interpretive frameworks, notably the tension between originalist theory and progressive doctrines like the Living Constitution. Further discussions concern the nature of American law, which is shaped not solely by the Constitution’s Supremacy Clause but also by judicial precedent. This reliance on precedent means constitutional interpretation is inevitably influenced by contemporary mores, thereby complicating appeals to a fixed historical understanding and challenging the utility of historical revisionism in constitutional analysis.

input: The official language of the Republic is Modern Standard Arabic. Arabic was adopted by the Egyptians after the Arab invasion of Egypt. The spoken languages are: Egyptian Arabic (68%), Sa'idi Arabic (29%), Eastern Egyptian Bedawi Arabic (1.6%), Sudanese Arabic (0.6%), Domari (0.3%), Nobiin (0.3%), Beja (0.1%), Siwi and others. Additionally, Greek, Armenian and Italian are the main languages of immigrants. In Alexandria in the 19th century there was a large community of Italian Egyptians and Italian was the "lingua franca" of the city.
rewrite: The Republic's official language is Modern Standard Arabic, which was established following the Arab conquest of Egypt. Predominant spoken varieties include Egyptian Arabic (68%) and Sa'idi Arabic (29%), alongside minority languages such as Eastern Egyptian Bedawi, Sudanese Arabic, Domari, Nobiin, Beja, and Siwi. Immigrant communities primarily utilize Greek, Armenian, and Italian. Historically, during the 19th century, Italian served as Alexandria's lingua franca due to its substantial Italian Egyptian population.

input: Catalan is split in two major dialectal blocks: Eastern Catalan, and Western Catalan. The main difference lies in the treatment of unstressed a and e; which have merged to /ə/ in Eastern dialects, but which remain distinct as /a/ and /e/ in Western dialects. There are a few other differences in pronunciation, verbal morphology, and vocabulary.
rewrite: Catalan is divided into two principal dialectal groups: Eastern and Western Catalan. Their primary distinction involves the unstressed vowels *a* and *e*, which merge to /ə/ in Eastern varieties but remain separate as /a/ and /e/ in Western ones. Additional phonological, morphological, and lexical variations also exist.

input: On basic Church teachings, the pope was unwavering. On the tenth anniversary of Humanae vitae, he reconfirmed this teaching. In his style and methodology, he was a disciple of Pius XII, whom he deeply revered. He suffered for the attacks on Pius XII for his alleged silences during the Holocaust. Pope Paul VI was less outstanding than his predecessors: he was not credited with an encyclopedic memory, nor a gift for languages, nor the brilliant writing style of Pius XII, nor did he have the charisma and outpouring love, sense of humor and human warmth of John XXIII. He took on himself the unfinished reform work of these two popes, bringing them diligently with great humility and common sense and without much fanfare to conclusion. In doing so, Paul VI saw himself following in the footsteps of the Apostle Paul, torn to several directions as Saint Paul, who said, "I am attracted to two sides at once, because the Cross always divides."
rewrite: In matters of fundamental Church doctrine, Pope Paul VI remained resolute, reaffirming the teachings of *Humanae Vitae* on its tenth anniversary. His style and methodology reflected his profound reverence for Pope Pius XII, whose disciple he considered himself; he was pained by criticisms of Pius XII’s perceived silence during the Holocaust. Paul VI did not possess the encyclopedic memory, linguistic gifts, or literary brilliance of Pius XII, nor did he exhibit the charismatic warmth, humor, and abundant affection characteristic of Pope John XXIII. Nevertheless, he assumed the unfinished reform efforts of both pontiffs, completing them with diligent humility, sound judgment, and minimal ostentation. In this undertaking, Paul VI viewed himself as following the example of the Apostle Paul, feeling similarly pulled in multiple directions, echoing the saint’s words: “I am attracted to two sides at once, because the Cross always divides.”

input: The earliest known document in Galician-Portuguese dates from 1228. The Foro do bo burgo do Castro Caldelas was granted by Alfonso IX of León to the town of Burgo, in Castro Caldelas, after the model of the constitutions of the town of Allariz. A distinct Galician Literature emerged during the Middle Ages: In the 13th century important contributions were made to the romance canon in Galician-Portuguese, the most notable those by the troubadour Martín Codax, the priest Airas Nunes, King Denis of Portugal and King Alfonso X of Castile, Alfonso O Sabio ("Alfonso the Wise"), the same monarch who began the process of establishing the hegemony of Castilian. During this period, Galician-Portuguese was considered the language of love poetry in the Iberian Romance linguistic culture. The names and memories of Codax and other popular cultural figures are well preserved in modern Galicia and, despite the long period of Castilian linguistic domination, these names are again household words.
rewrite: The earliest extant document in Galician-Portuguese originates from 1228. This text, the Foro do bo burgo do Castro Caldelas, was a charter granted by Alfonso IX of León to the town of Burgo in Castro Caldelas, modeled upon the constitutions of Allariz. A distinct Galician literary tradition emerged during the medieval period. The thirteenth century witnessed significant contributions to the romance canon in Galician-Portuguese, most notably by the troubadour Martín Codax, the cleric Airas Nunes, King Denis of Portugal, and King Alfonso X of Castile, known as Alfonso the Wise—the same monarch who initiated the process of establishing Castilian hegemony. During this era, Galician-Portuguese was regarded as the preeminent language for love poetry within Iberian Romance culture. The legacies of Codax and other prominent cultural figures remain well preserved in modern Galicia; despite a prolonged period of Castilian linguistic domination, these names have re-entered common usage.

input: The city is home to New Haven Promise, a scholarship funded by Yale University for students who meet the requirements. Students must be enrolled in a public high school (charters included) for four years, be a resident of the city during that time, carry a 3.0 cumulative grade-point average, have a 90-percent attendance rate and perform 40 hours of service to the city. The initiative was launched in 2010 and there are currently more than 500 Scholars enrolled in qualifying Connecticut colleges and universities. There are more than 60 cities in the country that have a Promise-type program for their students.
rewrite: The city hosts the New Haven Promise, a scholarship program established and funded by Yale University. Eligibility requires four years of enrollment in a public or charter high school within the city, maintenance of a 3.0 cumulative GPA, a 90% attendance record, and completion of 40 hours of community service. Launched in 2010, the initiative currently supports over 500 Scholars attending eligible institutions across Connecticut. This program is part of a broader national trend, with more than sixty American cities operating similar Promise-type educational initiatives.

input: Red was the color of the banner of the Byzantine emperors. In Western Europe, Emperor Charlemagne painted his palace red as a very visible symbol of his authority, and wore red shoes at his coronation. Kings, princes and, beginning in 1295, Roman Catholic cardinals began to wear red costumes. When Abbe Suger rebuilt Saint Denis Basilica outside Paris in the early 12th century, he added stained glass windows colored blue cobalt glass and red glass tinted with copper. Together they flooded the basilica with a mystical light. Soon stained glass windows were being added to cathedrals all across France, England and Germany. In Medieval painting red was used to attract attention to the most important figures; both Christ and the Virgin Mary were commonly painted wearing red mantles.
rewrite: The color red served as a significant emblem of authority within the Byzantine Empire, prominently displayed on the imperial banner. In Western Europe, Charlemagne reinforced this association by adorning his palace in red and donning red shoes for his coronation. By 1295, the use of red expanded to the vestments of kings, princes, and Roman Catholic cardinals. During the early twelfth century, Abbot Suger incorporated stained glass windows of cobalt blue and copper-tinted red into the Basilica of Saint-Denis, producing a mystical illumination that inspired similar installations across French, English, and German cathedrals. In medieval art, red was strategically employed to highlight central sacred figures, notably Christ and the Virgin Mary, who were frequently depicted in red mantles.

input: Democratic Party candidates were consistently elected to local office, increasing the city's ties to the South and its dominant party. In 1861, Mayor Fernando Wood called on the aldermen to declare independence from Albany and the United States after the South seceded, but his proposal was not acted on. Anger at new military conscription laws during the American Civil War (1861–1865), which spared wealthier men who could afford to pay a $300 (equivalent to $5,766 in 2016) commutation fee to hire a substitute, led to the Draft Riots of 1863, whose most visible participants were ethnic Irish working class. The situation deteriorated into attacks on New York's elite, followed by attacks on black New Yorkers and their property after fierce competition for a decade between Irish immigrants and blacks for work. Rioters burned the Colored Orphan Asylum to the ground, but more than 200 children escaped harm due to efforts of the New York City Police Department, which was mainly made up of Irish immigrants. According to historian James M. McPherson (2001), at least 120 people were killed. In all, eleven black men were lynched over five days, and the riots forced hundreds of blacks to flee the city for Williamsburg, Brooklyn, as well as New Jersey; the black population in Manhattan fell below 10,000 by 1865, which it had last been in 1820. The white working class had established dominance. Violence by longshoremen against black men was especially fierce in the docks area. It was one of the worst incidents of civil unrest in American history.
rewrite: Throughout the mid-nineteenth century, the repeated election of Democratic Party candidates to municipal office strengthened the city's political and economic affiliations with the South and its prevailing political institution. In 1861, following Southern secession, Mayor Fernando Wood proposed that the city’s aldermen declare independence from both Albany and the United States, though this measure was never implemented. Subsequently, widespread resentment erupted during the American Civil War (1861–1865) in response to new conscription legislation. These laws permitted wealthier individuals to avoid service by paying a commutation fee of $300 (equivalent to $5,766 in 2016) to hire a substitute, a provision that incited the Draft Riots of 1863. The most conspicuous participants in these riots were members of the ethnic Irish working class. Initial hostilities directed at New York’s elite rapidly devolved into brutal assaults against black residents and their property, exacerbated by years of intense labor competition between Irish immigrants and African Americans. Rioters destroyed the Colored Orphan Asylum by fire; however, over two hundred children were evacuated safely, largely through the intervention of the New York City Police Department, which was predominantly composed of Irish immigrants. Historian James M. McPherson (2001) records a death toll of at least 120. Over five days, eleven black men were lynched, and hundreds of African Americans were displaced, fleeing to Williamsburg, Brooklyn, and New Jersey. Consequently, Manhattan’s black population fell below 10,000 by 1865, a level not seen since 1820. These events cemented the dominance of the white working class, with particularly severe violence perpetrated by longshoremen against black men in the dockyards. The Draft Riots remain among the most severe episodes of civil disorder in United States history.

input: 90th Street is split into two segments. The first segment, West 90th Street begins at Riverside Drive and ends at Central Park West or West Drive, when it is open, in Central Park on the Upper West Side. The second segment of East 90th Street begins at East Drive, at Engineers Gate of Central Park. When East Drive is closed, East 90th Street begins at Fifth Avenue on the Upper East Side and curves to the right at the FDR Drive becoming East End Avenue. Our Lady of Good Counsel Church, is located on East 90th Street between Third Avenue and Second Avenue, across the street from Ruppert Towers (1601 and 1619 Third Avenue) and Ruppert Park. Asphalt Green, which is located on East 90th Street between York Avenue and East End Avenue.
rewrite: Nineteeth Street comprises two discontinuous sections. The western segment, designated West 90th Street, originates at Riverside Drive on the Upper West Side and terminates at Central Park West, or at West Drive within Central Park when that route is accessible. The eastern segment, East 90th Street, commences at Engineers Gate on Central Park's East Drive. During closures of East Drive, the starting point shifts to Fifth Avenue on the Upper East Side; the street then curves eastward at the Franklin D. Roosevelt Drive, becoming East End Avenue. Notable landmarks along East 90th Street include Our Lady of Good Counsel Church, situated between Third and Second Avenues opposite Ruppert Towers and Ruppert Park, and Asphalt Green, located between York Avenue and East End Avenue.

input: Tuvalu participates in the Alliance of Small Island States (AOSIS), which is a coalition of small island and low-lying coastal countries that have concerns about their vulnerability to the adverse effects of global climate change. Under the Majuro Declaration, which was signed on 5 September 2013, Tuvalu has commitment to implement power generation of 100% renewable energy (between 2013 and 2020), which is proposed to be implemented using Solar PV (95% of demand) and biodiesel (5% of demand). The feasibility of wind power generation will be considered. Tuvalu participates in the operations of the Pacific Islands Applied Geoscience Commission (SOPAC) and the Secretariat of the Pacific Regional Environment Programme (SPREP).
rewrite: Tuvalu is a member state of the Alliance of Small Island States (AOSIS), a coalition representing small island and low-lying coastal nations vulnerable to the adverse impacts of global climate change. In accordance with the Majuro Declaration of September 5, 2013, Tuvalu committed to achieving 100% renewable energy generation for power between 2013 and 2020. This target was to be met primarily through solar photovoltaics (95% of demand) and biodiesel (5%), with the feasibility of wind power under consideration. Furthermore, Tuvalu participates in the Pacific Islands Applied Geoscience Commission (SOPAC) and the Secretariat of the Pacific Regional Environment Programme (SPREP).

input: In higher organisms (like people), these two modes of perception combine into what Whitehead terms "symbolic reference", which links appearance with causation in a process that is so automatic that both people and animals have difficulty refraining from it. By way of illustration, Whitehead uses the example of a person's encounter with a chair. An ordinary person looks up, sees a colored shape, and immediately infers that it is a chair. However, an artist, Whitehead supposes, "might not have jumped to the notion of a chair", but instead "might have stopped at the mere contemplation of a beautiful color and a beautiful shape." This is not the normal human reaction; most people place objects in categories by habit and instinct, without even thinking about it. Moreover, animals do the same thing. Using the same example, Whitehead points out that a dog "would have acted immediately on the hypothesis of a chair and would have jumped onto it by way of using it as such." In this way symbolic reference is a fusion of pure sense perceptions on the one hand and causal relations on the other, and that it is in fact the causal relationships that dominate the more basic mentality (as the dog illustrates), while it is the sense perceptions which indicate a higher grade mentality (as the artist illustrates).
rewrite: In higher organisms, including humans, these dual modes of perception integrate into what Alfred North Whitehead identifies as "symbolic reference." This process forges a connection between perceptual appearance and causal interpretation, operating with such automaticity that both humans and animals struggle to abstain from it. To illustrate, Whitehead presents the instance of encountering a chair. An ordinary individual, upon seeing a colored shape, immediately infers the presence of a chair. In contrast, an artist, Whitehead suggests, "might not have jumped to the notion of a chair," but could instead pause at "the mere contemplation of a beautiful color and a beautiful shape." This deliberative response is atypical; habitual categorization of objects is the normative human and animal reaction, performed instinctively. Extending the example, Whitehead observes that a dog "would have acted immediately on the hypothesis of a chair and would have jumped onto it by way of using it as such." Symbolic reference thus constitutes a synthesis of pure sense perception and causal inference. Notably, causal relations predominate in more basic mental operations, as exemplified by the dog’s pragmatic response, whereas a heightened focus on sensory qualities signifies a more advanced mentality, as demonstrated by the artist’s contemplative stance.

input: Above the forestry, there is often a band of short pine trees (Pinus mugo), which is in turn superseded by Alpenrosen, dwarf shrubs, typically Rhododendron ferrugineum (on acid soils) or Rhododendron hirsutum (on alkaline soils). Although the Alpenrose prefers acidic soil, the plants are found throughout the region. Above the tree line is the area defined as "alpine" where in the alpine meadow plants are found that have adapted well to harsh conditions of cold temperatures, aridity, and high altitudes. The alpine area fluctuates greatly because of regional fluctuations in tree lines.
rewrite: Above the montane forest zone, a belt of dwarf mountain pine (Pinus mugo) is frequently succeeded by Alpenrosen, a dwarf shrub layer predominantly comprising Rhododendron ferrugineum on acidic substrates or Rhododendron hirsutum on calcareous soils. While favoring acidity, these shrubs occur across the region. Beyond the tree line lies the alpine zone, characterized by meadows containing flora specially adapted to severe cold, aridity, and high elevation. The extent of this alpine area varies considerably due to regional differences in the altitude of the tree line.

input: Carpet-weaving is historically a major traditional profession for the majority of Armenian women, including many Armenian families. Prominent Karabakh carpet weavers there were men too. The oldest extant Armenian carpet from the region, referred to as Artsakh (see also Karabakh carpet) during the medieval era, is from the village of Banants (near Gandzak) and dates to the early 13th century. The first time that the Armenian word for carpet, gorg, was used in historical sources was in a 1242–1243 Armenian inscription on the wall of the Kaptavan Church in Artsakh.
rewrite: Historically, carpet-weaving constituted a principal traditional occupation for many Armenian women and their families, though notably, skilled male weavers also existed in Karabakh. The earliest surviving Armenian carpet from the medieval region of Artsakh (Karabakh) originates from Banants village, dating to the early thirteenth century. Furthermore, the initial documented use of the Armenian word for carpet, *gorg*, appears in an inscription from 1242–1243 on the Kaptavan Church wall in Artsakh.

input: "Azure, three ships with three masts, rigged and under full sail, the sails, pennants and ensigns Argent, each charged with a cross Gules; on a chief of the second a pale quarterly Azure and Gules, on the 1st and 4th a fleur-de-lis or, on the 2nd and 3rd a leopard or, between two roses Gules seeded Or barbed Vert." The shield had as a crest: "A sphere without a frame, bounded with the Zodiac in bend Or, between two pennants flottant Argent, each charged with a cross Gules, over the sphere the words DEUS INDICAT" (Latin: God Indicates). The supporters were two sea lions (lions with fishes' tails) and the motto was DEO DUCENTE NIL NOCET (Latin: Where God Leads, Nothing Hurts).
rewrite: The blazon describes a shield azure, charged with three three-masted ships in full sail, all argent, with their sails, pennants, and ensigns each bearing a cross gules. Above, a chief argent displays a pale quarterly azure and gules; the first and fourth quarters bear a fleur-de-lis or, while the second and third show a leopard or, the pale being flanked by two roses gules seeded or and barbed vert. The crest is a frameless sphere encircled by the zodiac in bend or, set between two pennants flottant argent, each charged with a cross gules, and inscribed above with "DEUS INDICAT." Supporters are two sea lions, and the motto is "DEO DUCENTE NIL NOCET."

input: Immunology is a branch of biomedical science that covers the study of immune systems in all organisms. It charts, measures, and contextualizes the: physiological functioning of the immune system in states of both health and diseases; malfunctions of the immune system in immunological disorders (such as autoimmune diseases, hypersensitivities, immune deficiency, and transplant rejection); the physical, chemical and physiological characteristics of the components of the immune system in vitro, in situ, and in vivo. Immunology has applications in numerous disciplines of medicine, particularly in the fields of organ transplantation, oncology, virology, bacteriology, parasitology, psychiatry, and dermatology.
rewrite: Immunology is a biomedical discipline dedicated to the scientific investigation of immune systems across all organisms. It involves the mapping, quantification, and interpretation of the immune system's physiological operations in health and disease, including its malfunctions in disorders like autoimmunity, hypersensitivity, and immunodeficiency. The field also examines the structural and functional properties of immune components through in vitro, in situ, and in vivo studies. Its principles are critically applied across medical specialties, including transplantation, oncology, microbiology, and dermatology.

input: In 1911 arsphenamine, the first synthetic anti-infective drug, was developed by Paul Ehrlich and chemist Alfred Bertheim of the Institute of Experimental Therapy in Berlin. The drug was given the commercial name Salvarsan. Ehrlich, noting both the general toxicity of arsenic and the selective absorption of certain dyes by bacteria, hypothesized that an arsenic-containing dye with similar selective absorption properties could be used to treat bacterial infections. Arsphenamine was prepared as part of a campaign to synthesize a series of such compounds, and found to exhibit partially selective toxicity. Arsphenamine proved to be the first effective treatment for syphilis, a disease which prior to that time was incurable and led inexorably to severe skin ulceration, neurological damage, and death.[citation needed]
rewrite: In 1911, the inaugural synthetic anti-infective agent, arsphenamine, was developed by Paul Ehrlich and chemist Alfred Bertheim at the Institute of Experimental Therapy in Berlin, subsequently marketed as Salvarsan. Ehrlich’s hypothesis stemmed from the recognized general toxicity of arsenic and the observed selective uptake of specific dyes by bacterial cells. He postulated that an arsenic-based compound exhibiting analogous selective affinity could target bacterial infections. This compound emerged from a systematic campaign to synthesize a series of such agents, demonstrating partially selective toxicity. Arsphenamine provided the first efficacious treatment for syphilis, a previously incurable disease that invariably progressed to severe ulceration, neurological deterioration, and mortality.

input: This constitution was created when the U.S. Congress directed local government to organize a constitutional convention to write the Puerto Rico Constitution in 1951. The acceptance of that constitution by Puerto Rico's electorate, the U.S. Congress, and the U.S. president occurred in 1952. In addition, the rights, privileges and immunities attendant to United States citizens are "respected in Puerto Rico to the same extent as though Puerto Rico were a state of the union" through the express extension of the Privileges and Immunities Clause of the U.S. Constitution by the U.S. Congress in 1948.
rewrite: The Constitution of Puerto Rico was formulated following a directive from the U.S. Congress, which authorized a local constitutional convention in 1951. Its ratification was subsequently secured through approval by the Puerto Rican electorate, the U.S. Congress, and the President in 1952. Furthermore, pursuant to a 1948 act of Congress, the Privileges and Immunities Clause of the U.S. Constitution was expressly extended to the territory. This ensures that the rights, privileges, and immunities of U.S. citizens are respected in Puerto Rico to the same degree as within a state of the Union.

input: Today, this term also refers to the doctrines and practices of the Reformed churches of which Calvin was an early leader. Less commonly, it can refer to the individual teaching of Calvin himself. The particulars of Calvinist theology may be stated in a number of ways. Perhaps the best known summary is contained in the five points of Calvinism, though these points identify the Calvinist view on soteriology rather than summarizing the system as a whole. Broadly speaking, Calvinism stresses the sovereignty or rule of God in all things — in salvation but also in all of life. This concept is seen clearly in the doctrines of predestination and total depravity.
rewrite: The term presently denotes the doctrines and practices of the Reformed churches historically led by John Calvin. More narrowly, it may reference Calvin's own theological teachings. Calvinist theology can be articulated through various formulations, the most prominent being the five points of Calvinism, which specifically address soteriological perspectives rather than providing a comprehensive summary. Fundamentally, Calvinism emphasizes the absolute sovereignty of God over all aspects of existence, including salvation and general providence. This principle is most evident in the distinct doctrines of predestination and total depravity.

input: The Pagode de Vincennes Buddhist temple, near Lake Daumesnil in the Bois de Vincennes, is the former Cameroon pavilion from the 1931 Paris Colonial Exposition. It hosts several different schools of Buddhism, and does not have a single leader. It shelters the biggest Buddha statue in Europe, more than nine metres high. There are two other small temples located in the Asian community in the 13th arrondissement. A Hindu temple, dedicated to Ganesh, on Rue Pajol in the 18th arrondissement, opened in 1985.
rewrite: Originally the Cameroon pavilion of the 1931 Paris Colonial Exposition, the Pagode de Vincennes Buddhist temple is situated near Lake Daumesnil in the Bois de Vincennes. It serves multiple Buddhist traditions without a centralized leadership and houses Europe's tallest Buddha statue, exceeding nine meters. Additionally, two smaller temples exist within the 13th arrondissement's Asian community. A separate Hindu temple dedicated to Ganesh opened in 1985 on Rue Pajol in the 18th arrondissement.

input: There have been cases of a variety of speech being deliberately reclassified to serve political purposes. One example is Moldovan. In 1996, the Moldovan parliament, citing fears of "Romanian expansionism", rejected a proposal from President Mircea Snegur to change the name of the language to Romanian, and in 2003 a Moldovan–Romanian dictionary was published, purporting to show that the two countries speak different languages. Linguists of the Romanian Academy reacted by declaring that all the Moldovan words were also Romanian words; while in Moldova, the head of the Academy of Sciences of Moldova, Ion Bărbuţă, described the dictionary as a politically motivated "absurdity".
rewrite: Historical instances exist wherein linguistic classification has been deliberately altered for political objectives. A pertinent case is that of Moldovan. In 1996, Moldova’s parliament, invoking concerns over "Romanian expansionism," declined President Mircea Snegur’s initiative to officially rename the state language Romanian. Subsequently, a 2003 Moldovan–Romanian dictionary was issued to substantiate claims of distinct languages. The Romanian Academy's linguists countered that all cited terms were inherently Romanian, while Moldovan Academician Ion Bărbuţă dismissed the dictionary as a politically driven absurdity.

input: The Neapolitan style has an almond-shaped body resembling a bowl, constructed from curved strips of wood. It usually has a bent sound table, canted in two planes with the design to take the tension of the 8 metal strings arranged in four courses.
