Owing to its substantial contingent of liberal political figures, the state emerged from the Reform War with relatively minimal disruption. The conservative movement of 1858 failed to gain traction locally, despite a successful military incursion by conservative commander Zuloaga, whose force of one thousand men occupied the cities of Chihuahua and Parral. In August 1859, Zuloaga's troops were defeated by liberal forces under Orozco, who subsequently deposed the state governor. Orozco was, however, compelled to flee to Durango two months later. During the late 1860s, conservative General Cajen briefly entered the state following his campaign in Jalisco, aiding in the installation of conservative officials and expelling liberal leaders Jesús González Ortega and José María Patoni. After seizing the state capital and appointing himself governor, Cajen promptly assembled a large force and defeated liberal troops at La Batalla del Gallo. Although he secured several advantages over liberal factions within the state, a vigorous liberal resurgence soon eroded his position. Liberal leaders José María Patoni of Durango and J.E. Muñoz of Chihuahua consolidated power by curtailing the political rights of the clergy through implementation of a presidential decree. The state subsequently elected General Luis Terrazas, a liberal leader, as governor; throughout 1861, he continued to engage in minor military actions to quell persistent conservative uprisings.

input: Another example of the persecution of heretics under Protestant rule was the execution of the Boston martyrs in 1659, 1660, and 1661. These executions resulted from the actions of the Anglican Puritans, who at that time wielded political as well as ecclesiastic control in the Massachusetts Bay Colony. At the time, the colony leaders were apparently hoping to achieve their vision of a "purer absolute theocracy" within their colony .[citation needed] As such, they perceived the teachings and practices of the rival Quaker sect as heretical, even to the point where laws were passed and executions were performed with the aim of ridding their colony of such perceived "heresies".[citation needed] It should be noticed that the Eastern Orthodox and Oriental Orthodox communions generally regard the Puritans themselves as having been heterodox or heretical.
rewrite: A further instance of the suppression of heresy within a Protestant regime occurred with the execution of the Boston martyrs between 1659 and 1661. These executions were conducted under the authority of the Puritan establishment, which exercised combined political and ecclesiastical dominion over the Massachusetts Bay Colony. The colonial leadership, aspiring to realize a purified theocratic state, deemed the doctrines and rituals of the Quaker sect heretical. Consequently, they enacted specific legislation and carried out capital punishments to eliminate these perceived deviations from orthodoxy. Notably, both Eastern and Oriental Orthodox traditions have historically regarded the Puritans themselves as heterodox or heretical.

input: The approaching era of jet travel, and a series of midair collisions (most notable was the 1956 Grand Canyon mid-air collision), prompted passage of the Federal Aviation Act of 1958. This legislation gave the CAA's functions to a new independent body, the Federal Aviation Agency. The act transferred air safety regulation from the CAB to the new FAA, and also gave the FAA sole responsibility for a common civil-military system of air navigation and air traffic control. The FAA's first administrator, Elwood R. Quesada, was a former Air Force general and adviser to President Eisenhower.
rewrite: The advent of jet aviation and a sequence of midair collisions, most prominently the 1956 Grand Canyon disaster, precipitated the enactment of the Federal Aviation Act of 1958. This statute reallocated the Civil Aeronautics Administration's duties to a newly established independent entity, the Federal Aviation Agency. It shifted primary air safety regulatory authority from the Civil Aeronautics Board to the FAA and vested the agency with exclusive control over a unified civil-military system for air navigation and traffic control. Its inaugural administrator was former Air Force General Elwood R. Quesada, an adviser to President Eisenhower.

input: Boston's early European settlers had first called the area Trimountaine (after its "three mountains"—only traces of which remain today) but later renamed it Boston after Boston, Lincolnshire, England, the origin of several prominent colonists. The renaming, on September 7, 1630 (Old Style),[b] was by Puritan colonists from England, who had moved over from Charlestown earlier that year in quest of fresh water. Their settlement was initially limited to the Shawmut Peninsula, at that time surrounded by the Massachusetts Bay and Charles River and connected to the mainland by a narrow isthmus. The peninsula is known to have been inhabited as early as 5000 BC.
rewrite: The initial European settlers designated the area Trimountaine, referencing its three prominent hills, of which minimal traces persist. On September 7, 1630, Puritan colonists, having relocated from Charlestown in search of potable water, formally renamed it Boston after Boston, England. Their settlement was confined to the Shawmut Peninsula, then encircled by the Massachusetts Bay and Charles River and linked to the mainland via a narrow isthmus. Archaeological evidence indicates the peninsula was inhabited as early as 5000 BC.

input: When the Xbox 360 was released, Microsoft's online gaming service Xbox Live was shut down for 24 hours and underwent a major upgrade, adding a basic non-subscription service called Xbox Live Silver (later renamed Xbox Live Free) to its already established premium subscription-based service (which was renamed Gold). Xbox Live Free is included with all SKUs of the console. It allows users to create a user profile, join on message boards, and access Microsoft's Xbox Live Arcade and Marketplace and talk to other members. A Live Free account does not generally support multiplayer gaming; however, some games that have rather limited online functions already, (such as Viva Piñata) or games that feature their own subscription service (e.g. EA Sports games) can be played with a Free account. Xbox Live also supports voice the latter a feature possible with the Xbox Live Vision.
rewrite: Upon the launch of the Xbox 360, Microsoft temporarily suspended its Xbox Live online service for a 24-hour period to implement a significant upgrade. This revision introduced a new, non-subscription tier named Xbox Live Silver, subsequently rebranded as Xbox Live Free, complementing the existing premium subscription, which was concurrently renamed Xbox Live Gold. The Free service is integrated into all console variants. It permits users to establish a profile, participate in message boards, access the Xbox Live Arcade and Marketplace, and communicate with other members. While multiplayer functionality is typically restricted, certain titles with inherently limited online features, such as *Viva Piñata*, or games operating independent subscription models, like some EA Sports offerings, remain accessible under a Free account. The service also incorporates voice communication, a capability enabled by the Xbox Live Vision peripheral.

input: The Eastern Roman Empire – today conventionally named the Byzantine Empire, a name not in use during its own time – became increasingly influenced by Greek culture after the 7th century, when Emperor Heraclius (AD 575 - 641) decided to make Greek the empire's official language. Certainly from then on, but likely earlier, the Roman and Greek cultures were virtually fused into a single Greco-Roman world. Although the Latin West recognized the Eastern Empire's claim to the Roman legacy for several centuries, after Pope Leo III crowned Charlemagne, king of the Franks, as the "Roman Emperor" on 25 December 800, an act which eventually led to the formation of the Holy Roman Empire, the Latin West started to favour the Franks and began to refer to the Eastern Roman Empire largely as the Empire of the Greeks (Imperium Graecorum).
rewrite: Following the seventh century, the Eastern Roman Empire—retrospectively termed the Byzantine Empire, a designation not employed contemporaneously—underwent a pronounced process of Hellenization. This shift was formally institutionalized under Emperor Heraclius (AD 575–641), who established Greek as the official administrative language. Consequently, the Roman and Greek cultural traditions effectively merged into a singular Greco-Roman synthesis. While the Latin West had long acknowledged the Eastern Empire’s claim to the Roman patrimony, this recognition diminished after Pope Leo III crowned Charlemagne, King of the Franks, as “Roman Emperor” on 25 December 800. This act, a precursor to the Holy Roman Empire, prompted the Latin West to increasingly align with the Frankish polity and to refer to the Eastern Roman realm pejoratively as the *Imperium Graecorum*, or Empire of the Greeks.

input: Allied submarines did not adopt a defensive posture and wait for the enemy to attack. Within hours after the Pearl Harbor attack, in retribution against Japan, Roosevelt promulgated a new doctrine: unrestricted submarine warfare against Japan. This meant sinking any warship, commercial vessel, or passenger ship in Axis-controlled waters, without warning and without help to survivors.[nb 13] At the outbreak of the war in the Pacific the Dutch Admiral in charge of the naval defense of the East Indies, Conrad Helfrich, gave instructions to wage war aggressively. His small force of submarines sank more Japanese ships in the first weeks of the war than the entire British and US navies together, an exploit which earned him the nickname "Ship-a-day Helfrich". The Dutch force were in fact the first to sink an enemy warship; On 24 December 1941, HNLMS K XVI torpedoed and sank the Japanese destroyer Sagiri.
rewrite: Allied submarines did not assume a defensive stance following the outbreak of hostilities. In direct response to the attack on Pearl Harbor, President Franklin D. Roosevelt swiftly authorized a policy of unrestricted submarine warfare against Japan. This doctrine mandated the sinking of any vessel—whether warship, merchantman, or passenger ship—within Axis-controlled waters, without prior warning and without rendering aid to survivors. Concurrently, in the Pacific theater, Dutch Admiral Conrad Helfrich, commanding the naval defense of the East Indies, issued orders for an aggressive campaign. His modest submarine fleet achieved considerable early success, sinking more Japanese tonnage in the initial weeks than the combined British and American navies, an accomplishment that garnered Helfrich the epithet "Ship-a-day." Notably, Dutch forces were the first to destroy an enemy warship, when HNLMS K XVI torpedoed and sank the Japanese destroyer *Sagiri* on 24 December 1941.

input: In 1368, a Han Chinese revolt known as the Red Turban Rebellion toppled the Mongol Yuan dynasty in China. Zhu Yuanzhang then established the Ming dynasty, ruling as the Hongwu Emperor (r. 1368–1398). It is not clear how much the early Ming court understood the civil war going on in Tibet between rival religious sects, but the first emperor was anxious to avoid the same trouble that Tibet had caused for the Tang dynasty. Instead of recognizing the Phagmodru ruler, the Hongwu Emperor sided with the Karmapa of the nearer Kham region and southeastern Tibet, sending envoys out in the winter of 1372–1373 to ask the Yuan officeholders to renew their titles for the new Ming court.
rewrite: In 1368, the Mongol Yuan dynasty in China was overthrown by the Han Chinese Red Turban Rebellion. Zhu Yuanzhang subsequently founded the Ming dynasty, reigning as the Hongwu Emperor from 1368 to 1398. The extent to which the nascent Ming court comprehended the contemporaneous sectarian civil war in Tibet remains uncertain. However, the Hongwu Emperor, seeking to avert the recurrent difficulties Tibet had posed for the preceding Tang dynasty, deliberately avoided endorsing the Phagmodru ruler. Instead, he aligned with the Karmapa hierarch in the nearer Kham and southeastern Tibetan regions. During the winter of 1372–1373, the emperor dispatched envoys to incumbent Yuan officials, instructing them to renew their titles under Ming authority.

input: Maria Deraismes was initiated into Freemasonry in 1882, then resigned to allow her lodge to rejoin their Grand Lodge. Having failed to achieve acceptance from any masonic governing body, she and Georges Martin started a mixed masonic lodge that actually worked masonic ritual. Annie Besant spread the phenomenon to the English speaking world. Disagreements over ritual led to the formation of exclusively female bodies of Freemasons in England, which spread to other countries. Meanwhile, the French had re-invented Adoption as an all-female lodge in 1901, only to cast it aside again in 1935. The lodges, however, continued to meet, which gave rise, in 1959, to a body of women practising continental Freemasonry.
rewrite: Maria Deraismes was initiated into Freemasonry in 1882, subsequently resigning to facilitate her lodge's return to its Grand Lodge. Following unsuccessful attempts to gain recognition from existing masonic authorities, she and Georges Martin founded a mixed-gender lodge that practiced traditional masonic ritual. Annie Besant later propagated this model within the English-speaking world. Divergent interpretations of ritual prompted the establishment of exclusively female masonic orders in England, a structure which subsequently expanded internationally. Concurrently, in France, the all-female Adoption Rite was revived in 1901 before being formally discontinued in 1935. Despite this, its constituent lodges persisted, ultimately leading to the formation in 1959 of an organization dedicated to women practicing continental Freemasonry.

input: John Forbes Kerry was born on December 11, 1943 in Aurora, Colorado, at Fitzsimons Army Hospital. He was the second oldest of four children born to Richard John Kerry, a Foreign Service officer and lawyer, and Rosemary Isabel Forbes, a nurse and social activist. His father was raised Catholic (John's paternal grandparents were Austro-Hungarian Jewish immigrants who converted to Catholicism) and his mother was Episcopalian. He was raised with an elder sister named Margaret (born 1941), a younger sister named Diana (born 1947) and a younger brother named Cameron (born 1950). The children were raised in their father's faith; John Kerry served as an altar boy.
rewrite: John Forbes Kerry was born on December 11, 1943, at Fitzsimons Army Hospital in Aurora, Colorado. He was the second of four children born to Richard John Kerry, a Foreign Service officer and attorney, and Rosemary Isabel Forbes, a nurse and social activist. His father, raised Catholic—his own parents were Austro-Hungarian Jewish converts to Catholicism—and his Episcopalian mother raised the children in the Catholic faith. Alongside his elder sister Margaret (born 1941), younger sister Diana (born 1947), and younger brother Cameron (born 1950), Kerry served as an altar boy during his upbringing.

input: The US Air Force Fitness Test (AFFT) is designed to test the abdominal circumference, muscular strength/endurance and cardiovascular respiratory fitness of airmen in the USAF. As part of the Fit to Fight program, the USAF adopted a more stringent physical fitness assessment; the new fitness program was put into effect on 1 June 2010. The annual ergo-cycle test which the USAF had used for several years had been replaced in 2004. In the AFFT, Airmen are given a score based on performance consisting of four components: waist circumference, the sit-up, the push-up, and a 1.5-mile (2.4 km) run. Airmen can potentially earn a score of 100, with the run counting as 60%, waist circumference as 20%, and both strength test counting as 10% each. A passing score is 75 points. Effective 1 July 2010, the AFFT is administered by the base Fitness Assessment Cell (FAC), and is required twice a year. Personnel may test once a year if he or she earns a score above a 90%. Additionally, only meeting the minimum standards on each one of these tests will not get you a passing score of 75%, and failing any one component will result in a failure for the entire test.
rewrite: The United States Air Force Fitness Test (AFFT) serves to evaluate key physical attributes of USAF personnel, specifically abdominal circumference, muscular strength and endurance, and cardiovascular respiratory fitness. This assessment was implemented under the Fit to Fight program, superseding an annual ergo-cycle test previously utilized and discontinued in 2004. The current, more rigorous AFFT was formally enacted on 1 June 2010. The evaluation comprises four components: waist circumference measurement, timed sit-up and push-up exercises, and a 1.5-mile (2.4 km) run. Scoring is weighted, with the run constituting 60% of the total possible 100 points, waist circumference 20%, and each strength assessment 10%. A minimum score of 75 points is required to pass. Administered by the base Fitness Assessment Cell (FAC) effective 1 July 2010, the test is mandated biannually. Personnel achieving a score above 90% are permitted to test annually. It is important to note that merely meeting the minimum standard on each component does not guarantee an overall passing score, and failure on any single component results in failure of the entire assessment.

input: As the 10th century progressed, the Khazars were no longer able to command tribute from the Volga Bulgars, and their relationship with the Byzantines deteriorated, as Byzantium increasingly allied with the Pechenegs against them. The Pechenegs were thus secure to raid the lands of the Khazars from their base between the Volga and Don rivers, allowing them to expand to the west. Rus' relations with the Pechenegs were complex, as the groups alternately formed alliances with and against one another. The Pechenegs were nomads roaming the steppe raising livestock which they traded with the Rus' for agricultural goods and other products. The lucrative Rus' trade with the Byzantine Empire had to pass through Pecheneg-controlled territory, so the need for generally peaceful relations was essential. Nevertheless, while the Primary Chronicle reports the Pechenegs entering Rus' territory in 915 and then making peace, they were waging war with one another again in 920. Pechenegs are reported assisting the Rus' in later campaigns against the Byzantines, yet allied with the Byzantines against the Rus' at other times.
rewrite: During the tenth century, the Khazar Khaganate experienced a marked decline in its regional authority, ceasing to extract tribute from the Volga Bulgars and witnessing a deterioration in its relations with the Byzantine Empire. Byzantium increasingly aligned itself with the Pechenegs, a nomadic confederation based between the Volga and Don rivers. This alliance enabled the Pechenegs to raid Khazar territories with impunity and facilitated their westward expansion. Interactions between the Pechenegs and the Rus’ were characterized by a complex and shifting dynamic of conflict and cooperation. As pastoralists, the Pechenegs engaged in trade with the Rus’, exchanging livestock for agricultural and manufactured goods. The critical commercial route connecting the Rus’ to the Byzantine Empire traversed Pecheneg-controlled steppes, necessitating generally peaceful relations. Despite this mutual interest, periods of warfare punctuated the peace, as recorded in the Primary Chronicle for the years 915 and 920. This pattern of alternating allegiance continued, with the Pechenegs later aiding the Rus’ against Byzantium on certain occasions while opposing them as Byzantine allies on others.

input: Other local colleges and universities include Concordia University Ann Arbor, a Lutheran liberal-arts institution; a campus of the University of Phoenix; and Cleary University, a private business school. Cooley Law School acquired the former Ave Maria buildings for use as a branch campus.

input: The original city council line-up of 14 members (nine district-based and five at-large positions) was based on a U.S. Justice Department mandate which took effect in 1979. At-large council members represent the entire city. Under the city charter, once the population in the city limits exceeded 2.1 million residents, two additional districts were to be added. The city of Houston's official 2010 census count was 600 shy of the required number; however, as the city was expected to grow beyond 2.1 million shortly thereafter, the two additional districts were added for, and the positions filled during, the August 2011 elections.
rewrite: The original composition of the city council, established by a 1979 U.S. Justice Department mandate, consisted of fourteen members: nine elected from single-member districts and five at-large representatives serving the entire municipality. The city charter stipulated that upon exceeding a population of 2.1 million within its limits, two additional council districts would be created. Although the official 2010 census recorded a count approximately 600 residents below this threshold, imminent growth projections justified the addition. Consequently, the two new districts were established and their positions filled during the August 2011 elections.

input: Externally, Orthodox Jews can be identified by their manner of dress and family lifestyle. Orthodox women dress modestly by keeping most of their skin covered. Additionally, married women cover their hair, most commonly in the form of a scarf, also in the form of hats, bandanas, berets, snoods or, sometimes, wigs. Orthodox men wear a skullcap known as a kipa and often fringes called "tzitzit". Haredi men often grow beards and always wear black hats and suits, indoors and outdoors. However, Modern Orthodox Jews are commonly indistinguishable in their dress from those around them.
rewrite: Orthodox Jewish communities are often externally identifiable through distinctive attire and familial practices. Women adhere to modesty standards, typically covering most of their skin; married women also cover their hair, frequently with scarves, hats, or wigs. Men customarily wear a kipa (skullcap) and often display tzitzit (ritual fringes). Haredi men usually maintain beards and consistently wear black hats and suits. In contrast, Modern Orthodox individuals frequently adopt contemporary dress, making them largely indistinguishable from the general populace in their appearance.

input: Gain is a parameter which measures the degree of directivity of the antenna's radiation pattern. A high-gain antenna will radiate most of its power in a particular direction, while a low-gain antenna will radiate over a wider angle. The antenna gain, or power gain of an antenna is defined as the ratio of the intensity (power per unit surface area)  radiated by the antenna in the direction of its maximum output, at an arbitrary distance, divided by the intensity  radiated at the same distance by a hypothetical isotropic antenna which radiates equal power in all directions. This dimensionless ratio is usually expressed logarithmically in decibels, these units are called "decibels-isotropic" (dBi)
rewrite: Antenna gain quantifies the directivity of an antenna's radiation pattern. A high-gain antenna concentrates its radiated power within a narrow beam, whereas a low-gain antenna disperses power over a broader angular range. Technically, gain is defined as the ratio of the radiation intensity, measured in the direction of maximum power density at a specified distance, to the intensity that would be radiated by a lossless isotropic source at the same distance. This dimensionless ratio is typically expressed on a logarithmic scale in decibels relative to an isotropic radiator, denoted as dBi.

input: Light is the signal by which plants synchronize their internal clocks to their environment and is sensed by a wide variety of photoreceptors. Red and blue light are absorbed through several phytochromes and cryptochromes. One phytochrome, phyA, is the main phytochrome in seedlings grown in the dark but rapidly degrades in light to produce Cry1. Phytochromes B–E are more stable with phyB, the main phytochrome in seedlings grown in the light. The cryptochrome (cry) gene is also a light-sensitive component of the circadian clock and is thought to be involved both as a photoreceptor and as part of the clock's endogenous pacemaker mechanism. Cryptochromes 1–2 (involved in blue–UVA) help to maintain the period length in the clock through a whole range of light conditions.
rewrite: Light serves as the primary signal enabling plants to align their circadian rhythms with environmental cycles, detected through an array of photoreceptors. Red and blue light are predominantly absorbed by multiple phytochromes and cryptochromes. Among these, phytochrome A (phyA) functions as the principal phytochrome in etiolated seedlings but undergoes rapid degradation upon light exposure, facilitating the production of cryptochrome 1 (Cry1). In contrast, phytochromes B through E exhibit greater stability, with phyB being the dominant phytochrome in light-grown seedlings. The cryptochrome gene itself constitutes a light-sensitive element of the circadian system, proposed to act both as a photoreceptor and as an integral component of the endogenous pacemaker. Specifically, cryptochromes 1 and 2, responsive to blue and UVA light, contribute to maintaining consistent period length across varying light conditions.

input: Genetic studies of mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) of Amerindians and some Siberian and Central Asian peoples also revealed that the gene pool of the Turkic-speaking peoples of Siberia such as Altaians, Khakas, Shors and Soyots, living between the Altai and Lake Baikal along the Sayan mountains, are genetically closest to Amerindians.[citation needed] This view is shared by other researchers who argue that "the ancestors of the American Indians were the first to separate from the great Asian population in the Middle Paleolithic. 2012 research found evidence for a recent common ancestry between Native Americans and indigenous Altaians based on mitochondrial DNA and Y-Chromosome analysis. The paternal lineages of Altaians mostly belong to the subclades of haplogroup P-M45 (xR1a 38-93%; xQ1a 4-32%).
rewrite: Genetic analyses of mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) indicate that the Turkic-speaking populations of Siberia, including the Altaians, Khakas, Shors, and Soyots inhabiting the region from the Altai to Lake Baikal along the Sayan Mountains, possess a gene pool most closely related to that of Indigenous peoples of the Americas. This perspective is corroborated by additional scholarship, which posits an early Middle Paleolithic divergence of ancestral Native American groups from a broader Asian population. Supporting this connection, a 2012 study identified shared paternal and maternal lineages, demonstrating a recent common ancestry. Specifically, the paternal lineages among Altaians are predominantly characterized by subclades of haplogroup P-M45 (excluding R1a and Q1a at 38-93% and 4-32%, respectively).

input: 8th and 9th Streets run parallel to each other, beginning at Avenue D, interrupted by Tompkins Square Park at Avenue B, resuming at Avenue A and continuing to Sixth Avenue. West 8th Street is an important local shopping street. 8th Street between Avenue A and Third Avenue is called St Mark's Place, but it is counted in the length below.

Their continuity is interrupted by Tompkins Square Park between Avenues B and A, after which they resume and continue to Sixth Avenue. West Eighth Street serves as a significant local commercial corridor. The segment between Avenue A and Third Avenue, designated St. Mark's Place, is included in the total length.

input: TechRadar deemed the Xbox 360 as the most influential game system through its emphasis of digital media distribution, Xbox Live online gaming service, and game achievement feature. During the console's lifetime, the Xbox brand has grown from gaming-only to encompassing all multimedia, turning it into a hub for "living-room computing environment". Five years after the Xbox 360's original debut, the well-received Kinect motion capture camera was released, which became the fastest selling consumer electronic device in history, and extended the life of the console.

Over its lifespan, the Xbox brand evolved from a gaming platform into a comprehensive multimedia hub, establishing a "living-room computing environment." input: Boston's colleges and universities have a significant effect on the regional economy. Boston attracts more than 350,000 college students from around the world, who contribute more than $4.8 billion annually to the city's economy. The area's schools are major employers and attract industries to the city and surrounding region. The city is home to a number of technology companies and is a hub for biotechnology, with the Milken Institute rating Boston as the top life sciences cluster in the country. Boston receives the highest absolute amount of annual funding from the National Institutes of Health of all cities in the United States.
rewrite: The institutions of higher education in Boston exert a substantial influence on the regional economy. Annually attracting over 350,000 international students, these institutions inject more than $4.8 billion into the local economy. They serve as major employers and draw various industries to the metropolitan area. This is evident in Boston's concentration of technology firms and its prominence as a biotechnology hub, which the Milken Institute ranks as the nation's top life sciences cluster. Furthermore, Boston receives a greater absolute amount of annual funding from the National Institutes of Health than any other U.S. city.

input: Another extreme case of impedance matching occurs when using a small loop antenna (usually, but not always, for receiving) at a relatively low frequency where it appears almost as a pure inductor. Resonating such an inductor with a capacitor at the frequency of operation not only cancels the reactance but greatly magnifies the very small radiation resistance of such a loop.[citation needed] This is implemented in most AM broadcast receivers, with a small ferrite loop antenna resonated by a capacitor which is varied along with the receiver tuning in order to maintain resonance over the AM broadcast band
rewrite: An additional instance of extreme impedance matching arises with small loop antennas, typically employed for reception at relatively low frequencies, where they exhibit nearly pure inductive characteristics. By resonating such an inductor with a capacitor at the operational frequency, the reactance is not only canceled, but the loop's minimal radiation resistance is also substantially amplified. This principle is commonly applied in most AM broadcast receivers, which utilize a small ferrite loop antenna resonated by a variable capacitor. This capacitor is adjusted in tandem with the receiver tuning to sustain resonance across the entire AM broadcast band.

input: Despite the internal stability (known as the paz porfiriana), modernization, and economic growth in Mexico during the Porfiriato from 1876 to 1910, many across the state became deeply dissatisfied with the political system. When Díaz first ran for office, he committed to a strict “No Re-election” policy in which he disqualified himself to serve consecutive terms. Eventually backtracking on many of his initial political positions Díaz became a de facto dictator. Díaz became increasingly unpopular due to brutal suppression of political dissidents by using the Rurales and manipulating the elections to solidify his political machine. The working class was frustrated with the Díaz regime due to the corruption of the political system that had increased the inequality between the rich and poor. The peasants felt disenfranchised by the policies that promoted the unfair distribution of land where 95% of the land was owned by the top 5%.
rewrite: The period of the Porfiriato (1876-1910) in Mexico was characterized by internal stability, termed *paz porfiriana*, alongside significant modernization and economic growth. Nevertheless, these developments were accompanied by widespread and deepening dissatisfaction with the political regime. Initially elected on a platform featuring a strict “No Re-election” principle, President Porfirio Díaz ultimately abandoned this and other early commitments, consolidating power as a de facto dictator. His administration grew increasingly unpopular through the brutal suppression of dissent, often employing the Rurales paramilitary force, and the systematic manipulation of elections to fortify his political machine. This discontent was particularly acute among the working class, who faced systemic corruption that exacerbated wealth inequality, and the peasantry, who were disenfranchised by land policies resulting in a profoundly unequal distribution, with approximately 95% of land held by the wealthiest 5% of the population.

input: Eton has a long list of distinguished former pupils. David Cameron is the 19th British prime minister to have attended the school, and has recommended that Eton set up a school in the state sector to help drive up standards. Eton now co-sponsors a state sixth-form college in Newham, a deprived area of East London, called the London Academy of Excellence, opened in 2012, which is free of charge and aims to get all its students into higher education. In September 2014, Eton opened, and became the sole educational sponsor for, a new purpose-built co-educational state boarding and day school for around 500 pupils, Holyport College, in Maidenhead in Berkshire, with construction costing around £15 million, in which a fifth of places for day pupils will be set aside for children from poor homes, 21 boarding places will go to youngsters on the verge of being taken into care, and a further 28 boarders will be funded or part-funded through bursaries.
rewrite: Eton College possesses an extensive roster of distinguished alumni. David Cameron, the nineteenth British Prime Minister to have been educated at the institution, has advocated for Eton to establish a school within the state sector to help elevate educational standards. In response, Eton now co-sponsors the London Academy of Excellence, a state sixth-form college in the deprived East London borough of Newham. Opened in 2012, this tuition-free academy aims to secure higher education placements for all its students. Furthermore, in September 2014, Eton became the sole educational sponsor for Holyport College, a newly constructed co-educational state boarding and day school in Maidenhead, Berkshire. With construction costs of approximately £15 million, the school serves around 500 pupils. Its provisions include reserving twenty percent of day places for children from disadvantaged backgrounds, allocating 21 boarding places for children at risk of entering care, and funding a further 28 boarders fully or partially through bursaries.

input: When learning how to write hanja, students are taught to memorize the native Korean pronunciation for the hanja's meaning and the Sino-Korean pronunciations (the pronunciation based on the Chinese pronunciation of the characters) for each hanja respectively so that students know what the syllable and meaning is for a particular hanja. For example, the name for the hanja 水 is 물 수 (mul-su) in which 물 (mul) is the native Korean pronunciation for "water", while 수 (su) is the Sino-Korean pronunciation of the character. The naming of hanja is similar to if "water" were named "water-aqua", "horse-equus", or "gold-aurum" based on a hybridization of both the English and the Latin names. Other examples include 사람 인 (saram-in) for 人 "person/people", 큰 대 (keun-dae) for 大 "big/large//great", 작을 소 (jakeul-so) for 小 "small/little", 아래 하 (arae-ha) for 下 "underneath/below/low", 아비 부 (abi-bu) for 父 "father", and 나라이름 한 (naraimreum-han) for 韓 "Han/Korea".
rewrite: In pedagogical approaches to Hanja literacy, students are instructed to memorize dual readings for each character: the native Korean pronunciation, which conveys its semantic meaning, and the Sino-Korean pronunciation, derived from historical Chinese phonology. This dual system ensures comprehension of both the meaning and the standard phonetic value of a given Hanja. For instance, the character 水 is formally presented as 물 수 (*mul-su*), where *mul* is the native Korean term for "water" and *su* is its Sino-Korean reading. This nomenclature can be analogized to a hybrid English-Latin system where "water" might be designated "water-aqua," "horse-equus," or "gold-aurum." Additional illustrative examples encompass 사람 인 (*saram-in*) for 人 ("person"), 큰 대 (*keun-dae*) for 大 ("large"), 작을 소 (*jakeul-so*) for 小 ("small"), 아래 하 (*arae-ha*) for 下 ("below"), 아비 부 (*abi-bu*) for 父 ("father"), and 나라이름 한 (*naraireum-han*) for 韓 ("Han/Korea").

input: Norwegian researchers at the University of Tromsø have shown that some Arctic animals (ptarmigan, reindeer) show circadian rhythms only in the parts of the year that have daily sunrises and sunsets. In one study of reindeer, animals at 70 degrees North showed circadian rhythms in the autumn, winter and spring, but not in the summer. Reindeer on Svalbard at 78 degrees North showed such rhythms only in autumn and spring. The researchers suspect that other Arctic animals as well may not show circadian rhythms in the constant light of summer and the constant dark of winter.
rewrite: Research conducted at the University of Tromsø demonstrates that certain Arctic species, including ptarmigan and reindeer, exhibit circadian rhythmicity exclusively during seasons with distinct daily photoperiods. A study of reindeer populations revealed those at 70°N maintained rhythms in autumn, winter, and spring, but not during summer. Individuals at 78°N on Svalbard displayed rhythms solely in autumn and spring. The findings suggest other Arctic fauna may similarly lack endogenous circadian organization under the continuous illumination of summer and the prolonged darkness of winter.

input: The Catholic Church has what is claimed to be the oldest continuously functioning internal legal system in Western Europe, much later than Roman law but predating the evolution of modern European civil law traditions. What began with rules ("canons") adopted by the Apostles at the Council of Jerusalem in the first century has developed into a highly complex legal system encapsulating not just norms of the New Testament, but some elements of the Hebrew (Old Testament), Roman, Visigothic, Saxon, and Celtic legal traditions.
rewrite: Canon law constitutes the oldest continuously operating internal legal system in Western Europe, postdating Roman law but preceding modern civil law traditions. Originating with apostolic canons established at the first-century Council of Jerusalem, it has evolved into a sophisticated juridical corpus. This system integrates norms from the New Testament alongside elements drawn from Hebrew, Roman, Visigothic, Saxon, and Celtic legal traditions.

input: Nonetheless, within a few years of his death, Gregory of Nazianzus called him the "Pillar of the Church". His writings were well regarded by all Church fathers who followed, in both the West and the East, who noted their rich devotion to the Word-become-man, great pastoral concern, and profound interest in monasticism. Athanasius is counted as one of the four great Eastern Doctors of the Church in the Roman Catholic Church. In the Eastern Orthodox Church, he is labeled the "Father of Orthodoxy". Some Protestants label him "Father of the Canon". Athanasius is venerated as a Christian saint, whose feast day is 2 May in Western Christianity, 15 May in the Coptic Orthodox Church, and 18 January in the other Eastern Orthodox Churches. He is venerated by the Oriental and Eastern Orthodox Churches, the Roman Catholic Church, the Lutherans, and the Anglican Communion.
rewrite: Nonetheless, within a few years of his death, Gregory of Nazianzus designated him the "Pillar of the Church." Subsequent Church Fathers in both Western and Eastern traditions consistently esteemed his writings, praising their profound devotion to the incarnate Word, significant pastoral sensitivity, and deep engagement with monastic thought. Athanasius is recognized as one of the four great Eastern Doctors of the Church in Roman Catholicism. Within the Eastern Orthodox Church, he is honored as the "Father of Orthodoxy," while some Protestant traditions refer to him as the "Father of the Canon." He is revered by the Oriental and Eastern Orthodox Churches, the Roman Catholic Church, Lutheran churches, and the Anglican Communion.

input: The Odrysian Kingdom was a union of Thracian tribes under the kings of the powerful Odrysian tribe centered around the region of Thrace. Various parts of Thrace were under Macedonian rule under Philip II of Macedon, Alexander the Great, Lysimachus, Ptolemy II, and Philip V but were also often ruled by their own kings. The Thracians and Agrianes were widely used by Alexander as peltasts and light cavalry, forming about one fifth of his army. The Diadochi also used Thracian mercenaries in their armies and they were also used as colonists. The Odrysians used Greek as the language of administration and of the nobility. The nobility also adopted Greek fashions in dress, ornament and military equipment, spreading it to the other tribes. Thracian kings were among the first to be Hellenized.
rewrite: The Odrysian Kingdom constituted a political unification of Thracian tribes, led by monarchs from the dominant Odrysian tribe and centered in the region of Thrace. While significant portions of Thrace experienced periods of Macedonian control under rulers including Philip II, Alexander the Great, and several Diadochi, local kingship frequently persisted. Thracian and Agrianian troops, notably employed as peltasts and light cavalry, comprised approximately twenty percent of Alexander the Great’s forces; subsequent Hellenistic successors likewise utilized Thracian mercenaries and settlers. Within the Odrysian realm, Greek served as the administrative and aristocratic language. The nobility further adopted Hellenic styles in attire, ornamentation, and military gear, disseminating these cultural forms among subordinate tribes. Consequently, Thracian rulers were notably early participants in the process of Hellenization.

input: Madonna's music has been the subject of much analysis and scrutiny. Robert M. Grant, author of Contemporary Strategy Analysis (2005), commented that what has brought Madonna success is "certainly not outstanding natural talent. As a vocalist, musician, dancer, songwriter, or actress, Madonna's talents seem modest." He asserts Madonna's success is in relying on the talents of others, and that her personal relationships have served as cornerstones to the numerous reinventions in the longevity of her career. Madonna's approach was far from the music industry wisdom of "Find a winning formula and stick to it." Her musical career has been a continuous experimentation with new musical ideas and new images and a constant quest for new heights of fame and acclaim. Grant concluded that "having established herself as the queen of popular music, Madonna did not stop there, but continued re-inventing." Musicologist Susan McClary wrote that "Madonna's art itself repeatedly deconstructs the traditional notion of the unified subject with finite ego boundaries. Her pieces explore various ways of constituting identities that refuse stability, that remain fluid, that resist definition."
rewrite: The musical output of Madonna has been extensively analyzed within academic discourse. Robert M. Grant, in *Contemporary Strategy Analysis* (2005), observes that her sustained success is "certainly not [due to] outstanding natural talent," noting that her abilities as a vocalist, musician, dancer, songwriter, or actress appear "modest." He contends that her achievements rely significantly on leveraging the talents of others and that her personal relationships have been foundational to the repeated reinventions characterizing her career longevity. Contrary to the industry adage of finding a fixed winning formula, Madonna’s trajectory demonstrates continuous experimentation with novel musical ideas and public personas in a persistent pursuit of greater fame and critical acclaim. Grant concludes that, "having established herself as the queen of popular music, Madonna did not stop there, but continued re-inventing." This perspective is echoed by musicologist Susan McClary, who argues that "Madonna's art itself repeatedly deconstructs the traditional notion of the unified subject with finite ego boundaries," instead exploring fluid and resistant identity formations that defy stable definition.

input: Following the death of Pope Pius XII on 9 October 1958, Roncalli watched the live funeral on his last full day in Venice on 11 October. His journal was specifically concerned with the funeral and the abused state of the late pontiff's corpse. Roncalli left Venice for the conclave in Rome well aware that he was papabile,[b] and after eleven ballots, was elected to succeed the late Pius XII, so it came as no surprise to him, though he had arrived at the Vatican with a return train ticket to Venice.[citation needed]
rewrite: Following the death of Pope Pius XII on 9 October 1958, Cardinal Roncalli observed the televised funeral proceedings from Venice on 11 October. His personal diary notes focus upon the funeral rites and the deteriorated condition of the deceased pontiff’s body. Traveling to the papal conclave in Rome, Roncalli was cognizant of his status as a papabile candidate. His election after eleven ballots, while reportedly prompting no personal astonishment, was such that he had initially retained a return railway ticket to Venice.

input: When granting assent by commission, the sovereign authorises three or more (normally five) lords who are Privy Counsellors to grant assent in his or her name. The Lords Commissioners, as the monarch's representatives are known, wear scarlet parliamentary robes and sit on a bench between the throne and the Woolsack. The Lords Reading Clerk reads the commission aloud; the senior commissioner then states, "My Lords, in obedience to Her Majesty's Commands, and by virtue of the Commission which has been now read, We do declare and notify to you, the Lords Spiritual and Temporal and Commons in Parliament assembled, that Her Majesty has given Her Royal Assent to the several Acts in the Commission mentioned."
rewrite: In the procedure of granting assent by commission, the sovereign delegates authority to a minimum of three, typically five, Privy Counsellors who are lords to confer assent on his or her behalf. These individuals, designated as Lords Commissioners and acting as the monarch's representatives, don scarlet parliamentary robes and occupy the bench situated between the throne and the Woolsack. Following the oral reading of the commission by the Lords Reading Clerk, the senior commissioner proclaims: "My Lords, in obedience to Her Majesty's Commands, and by virtue of the Commission which has been now read, We do declare and notify to you, the Lords Spiritual and Temporal and Commons in Parliament assembled, that Her Majesty has given Her Royal Assent to the several Acts in the Commission mentioned."

input: Approximately 26,000 citizen soldiers, sailors, and airmen and women, trained to the level of and interchangeable with their Regular Force counterparts, and posted to CAF operations or duties on a casual or ongoing basis, make up the Primary Reserve. This group is represented, though not commanded, at NDHQ by the Chief of Reserves and Cadets, who is usually a major general or rear admiral, and is divided into four components that are each operationally and administratively responsible to its corresponding environmental command in the Regular Force – the Naval Reserve (NAVRES), Land Force Reserve (LFR), and Air Reserve (AIRRES) – in addition to one force that does not fall under an environmental command, the Health Services Reserve under the Canadian Forces Health Services Group.
rewrite: The Primary Reserve consists of approximately 26,000 part-time military personnel, including soldiers, sailors, and aviators. These members are trained to standards equivalent to those of the Regular Force and are deployable on either casual or sustained terms. At National Defence Headquarters, the Chief of Reserves and Cadets, typically holding the rank of major general or rear admiral, provides representation without exercising command authority. The Reserve is organized into four distinct components. Three are aligned with the environmental commands of the Regular Force: the Naval Reserve (NAVRES), the Land Force Reserve (LFR), and the Air Reserve (AIRRES). The fourth, the Health Services Reserve, falls under the Canadian Forces Health Services Group rather than an environmental command.

input: In the early Western Han, a wealthy salt or iron industrialist, whether a semi-autonomous king or wealthy merchant, could boast funds that rivaled the imperial treasury and amass a peasant workforce of over a thousand. This kept many peasants away from their farms and denied the government a significant portion of its land tax revenue. To eliminate the influence of such private entrepreneurs, Emperor Wu nationalized the salt and iron industries in 117 BC and allowed many of the former industrialists to become officials administering the monopolies. By Eastern Han times, the central government monopolies were repealed in favor of production by commandery and county administrations, as well as private businessmen.
rewrite: During the early Western Han dynasty, prominent industrialists in the salt and iron sectors—whether semi-autonomous kings or affluent merchants—could command financial resources comparable to the imperial treasury and mobilize labor forces exceeding a thousand peasants. This diversion of agricultural labor reduced land cultivation and consequently diminished state tax revenues from land. To curtail the power of these private magnates, Emperor Wu nationalized the salt and iron industries in 117 BC, incorporating many former industrialists as officials overseeing the new state monopolies. By the Eastern Han period, these central government monopolies were abolished, with production responsibilities transferred to commandery and county administrations alongside licensed private merchants.

input: The topography of the state is roughly defined by the Continental Divide, which splits much of the state into distinct eastern and western regions. Most of Montana's 100 or more named mountain ranges are concentrated in the western half of the state, most of which is geologically and geographically part of the Northern Rocky Mountains. The Absaroka and Beartooth ranges in the south-central part of the state are technically part of the Central Rocky Mountains. The Rocky Mountain Front is a significant feature in the north-central portion of the state, and there are a number of isolated island ranges that interrupt the prairie landscape common in the central and eastern parts of the state. About 60 percent of the state is prairie, part of the northern Great Plains.
rewrite: The state's topography is broadly delineated by the Continental Divide, which bisects much of its territory into distinct eastern and western regions. The majority of Montana's more than one hundred named mountain ranges are situated in its western half, an area predominantly situated within the geologic and geographic province of the Northern Rocky Mountains. Exceptions include the Absaroka and Beartooth ranges in the south-central area, which are classified within the Central Rocky Mountains. A prominent feature in the north-central portion is the Rocky Mountain Front, while isolated island ranges punctuate the prairie landscape prevalent in the central and eastern sections. Approximately sixty percent of the state consists of prairie, forming a segment of the northern Great Plains.

input: Birds have evolved a variety of mating behaviors, with the peacock tail being perhaps the most famous example of sexual selection and the Fisherian runaway. Commonly occurring sexual dimorphisms such as size and color differences are energetically costly attributes that signal competitive breeding situations. Many types of avian sexual selection have been identified; intersexual selection, also known as female choice; and intrasexual competition, where individuals of the more abundant sex compete with each other for the privilege to mate. Sexually selected traits often evolve to become more pronounced in competitive breeding situations until the trait begins to limit the individual’s fitness. Conflicts between an individual fitness and signaling adaptations ensure that sexually selected ornaments such as plumage coloration and courtship behavior are "honest" traits. Signals must be costly to ensure that only good-quality individuals can present these exaggerated sexual ornaments and behaviors.
rewrite: Avian reproductive strategies encompass diverse mating behaviors, with the peacock's tail serving as a prominent illustration of sexual selection and Fisherian runaway processes. Commonly observed sexual dimorphisms, including disparities in size and coloration, represent energetically costly traits that signal the presence of competitive breeding environments. Avian sexual selection primarily manifests in two forms: intersexual selection, often characterized by female mate choice, and intrasexual competition, typically involving conflict among members of the more abundant sex for mating access. These sexually selected traits frequently undergo evolutionary exaggeration in competitive contexts, potentially progressing to a point where they impose fitness costs on the individual. The inherent conflict between individual fitness and signaling adaptations ensures that ornamental traits, such as elaborate plumage and complex courtship displays, function as "honest" signals. The necessity for these signals to be biologically costly guarantees that only high-quality individuals can sustain the development and expression of such exaggerated sexual characteristics.

input: Great Britain: The torch relay leg held in London, the host city of the 2012 Summer Olympics, on April 6 began at Wembley Stadium, passed through the City of London, and eventually ended at O2 Arena in the eastern part of the city. The 48 km (30 mi) leg took a total of seven and a half hours to complete, and attracted protests by pro-Tibetan independence and pro-Human Rights supporters, prompting changes to the planned route and an unscheduled move onto a bus, which was then briefly halted by protestors. Home Secretary Jacqui Smith has officially complained to Beijing Organising Committee about the conduct of the tracksuit-clad Chinese security guards. The Chinese officials, seen manhandling protesters, were described by both the London Mayor Ken Livingstone and Lord Coe, chairman of the London Olympic Committee as "thugs". A Metropolitan police briefing paper revealed that security for the torch relay cost £750,000 and the participation of the Chinese security team had been agreed in advance, despite the Mayor stating, "We did not know beforehand these thugs were from the security services. Had I known so, we would have said no."
rewrite: The London segment of the Olympic torch relay for the 2012 Summer Games commenced on April 6 at Wembley Stadium. The route proceeded through the City of London, concluding at the O2 Arena in the city's eastern district. This 48-kilometer (30-mile) leg required approximately seven and a half hours to complete. The event was marked by demonstrations from supporters of Tibetan independence and human rights advocacy. These protests necessitated alterations to the planned route, including an unscheduled transfer of the torch to a bus, which was subsequently briefly obstructed by demonstrators. The conduct of Chinese security personnel, who were attired in tracksuits and were observed physically confronting protesters, elicited official criticism. Home Secretary Jacqui Smith registered a formal complaint with the Beijing Organising Committee. Both the Mayor of London, Ken Livingstone, and the Chairman of the London Olympic Committee, Lord Coe, publicly characterized these officials as "thugs." According to a Metropolitan Police briefing document, security for the relay incurred costs of £750,000, and the involvement of the Chinese security team had been pre-approved. This occurred despite Mayor Livingstone's subsequent assertion that prior knowledge of their official status would have led to a refusal of their participation.

input: The government of India is based on a tiered system, in which the Constitution of India delineates the subjects on which each tier of government has executive powers. The Constitution originally provided for a two-tier system of government, the Union Government (also known as the Central Government), representing the Union of India, and the State governments. Later, a third tier was added in the form of Panchayats and Municipalities. In the current arrangement, The Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution delimits the subjects of each level of governmental jurisdiction, dividing them into three lists:
rewrite: The governance structure of India operates through a tiered system, as established by the Constitution of India, which specifies the executive authority of each governmental level. Initially, the Constitution prescribed a two-tier framework comprising the Union Government, representing the nation as a whole, and the individual State governments. Subsequently, a third tier was incorporated, consisting of Panchayats and Municipalities. Presently, the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution delineates the respective jurisdictions by categorizing subjects into three distinct lists.

input: In an effort to demonstrate peaceful intentions toward Germany, on 13 April 1941, the Soviets signed a neutrality pact with Axis power Japan. While Stalin had little faith in Japan's commitment to neutrality, he felt that the pact was important for its political symbolism, to reinforce a public affection for Germany. Stalin felt that there was a growing split in German circles about whether Germany should initiate a war with the Soviet Union. Stalin did not know that Hitler had been secretly discussing an invasion of the Soviet Union since summer 1940, and that Hitler had ordered his military in late 1940 to prepare for war in the east regardless of the parties' talks of a potential Soviet entry as a fourth Axis Power.
rewrite: On 13 April 1941, the Soviet Union entered into a neutrality pact with Japan, an Axis power, as a demonstrative gesture of its peaceful intentions toward Germany. Although Soviet leader Joseph Stalin placed limited credence in Japan’s adherence to neutrality, he regarded the pact as politically significant for its symbolic value in cultivating German public goodwill. Stalin perceived a growing divergence within German leadership regarding the advisability of initiating a conflict with the USSR. Unbeknownst to him, Adolf Hitler had been conducting clandestine deliberations concerning an invasion of the Soviet Union since the summer of 1940. Furthermore, by late 1940, Hitler had issued directives for military preparations for an eastern war, irrespective of ongoing diplomatic discussions regarding the potential inclusion of the Soviet Union as a fourth Axis partner.

input: Ottoman Turkish was the official language of the Empire. It was an Oghuz Turkic language highly influenced by Persian and Arabic. The Ottomans had several influential languages: Turkish, spoken by the majority of the people in Anatolia and by the majority of Muslims of the Balkans except in Albania and Bosnia; Persian, only spoken by the educated; Arabic, spoken mainly in Arabia, North Africa, Iraq, Kuwait, the Levant and parts of the Horn of Africa; and Somali throughout the Horn of Africa. In the last two centuries, usage of these became limited, though, and specific: Persian served mainly as a literary language for the educated, while Arabic was used for religious rites.
rewrite: The official administrative language of the Ottoman Empire was Ottoman Turkish, an Oghuz Turkic variety heavily infused with Persian and Arabic. Within the empire's multilingual sphere, vernacular Turkish was predominant among Anatolia's population and most Balkan Muslims, excluding Albania and Bosnia. Persian functioned primarily as a literary and scholarly language for the educated elite. Arabic held a central role in religious rituals and was widely spoken in regions including Arabia, North Africa, the Levant, and parts of the Horn of Africa, alongside Somali. Over the final two centuries of the empire, the use of these languages became increasingly specialized and circumscribed.

input: In his book, Humanism (1997), Tony Davies calls these critics "humanist anti-humanists". Critics of antihumanism, most notably Jürgen Habermas, counter that while antihumanists may highlight humanism's failure to fulfil its emancipatory ideal, they do not offer an alternative emancipatory project of their own. Others, like the German philosopher Heidegger considered themselves humanists on the model of the ancient Greeks, but thought humanism applied only to the German "race" and specifically to the Nazis and thus, in Davies' words, were anti-humanist humanists. Such a reading of Heidegger's thought is itself deeply controversial; Heidegger includes his own views and critique of Humanism in Letter On Humanism. Davies acknowledges that after the horrific experiences of the wars of the 20th century "it should no longer be possible to formulate phrases like 'the destiny of man' or the 'triumph of human reason' without an instant consciousness of the folly and brutality they drag behind them". For "it is almost impossible to think of a crime that has not been committed in the name of human reason". Yet, he continues, "it would be unwise to simply abandon the ground occupied by the historical humanisms. For one thing humanism remains on many occasions the only available alternative to bigotry and persecution. The freedom to speak and write, to organise and campaign in defence of individual or collective interests, to protest and disobey: all these can only be articulated in humanist terms."
rewrite: In his 1997 work *Humanism*, Tony Davies designates certain critics as "humanist anti-humanists." Critics of antihumanism, most prominently Jürgen Habermas, respond that while antihumanists effectively underscore humanism's failure to realize its emancipatory promises, they fail to propose a substantive alternative project of emancipation. Other figures, such as the German philosopher Martin Heidegger, identified as humanists in the tradition of ancient Greek thought. However, Heidegger restricted authentic humanism solely to the German "race" and, more specifically, to the Nazis, rendering him, in Davies’s terminology, an anti-humanist humanist. This interpretation of Heidegger remains deeply contested; Heidegger articulates his own position and critique of humanism in his *Letter on Humanism*. Davies observes that following the atrocities of twentieth-century warfare, it has become untenable to invoke phrases such as "the destiny of man" or the "triumph of human reason" without immediate recognition of the folly and brutality historically associated with them, noting that scarcely any crime has been omitted from those committed in the name of human reason. Nevertheless, he argues it would be imprudent to wholly vacate the conceptual terrain held by historical humanisms. Humanism frequently persists as the sole available counter to bigotry and persecution. Essential liberties—including the freedoms of speech and writing, of organizing and campaigning for individual or collective interests, and of protest and civil disobedience—can, Davies contends, only be coherently articulated within a humanist framework.

input: In 2006, a study by Behar et al., based on what was at that time high-resolution analysis of haplogroup K (mtDNA), suggested that about 40% of the current Ashkenazi population is descended matrilineally from just four women, or "founder lineages", that were "likely from a Hebrew/Levantine mtDNA pool" originating in the Middle East in the 1st and 2nd centuries CE. Additionally, Behar et al. suggested that the rest of Ashkenazi mtDNA is originated from ~150 women, and that most of those were also likely of Middle Eastern origin. In reference specifically to Haplogroup K, they suggested that although it is common throughout western Eurasia, "the observed global pattern of distribution renders very unlikely the possibility that the four aforementioned founder lineages entered the Ashkenazi mtDNA pool via gene flow from a European host population".
rewrite: A 2006 study by Behar et al., employing then high-resolution analysis of mitochondrial DNA haplogroup K, proposed that approximately 40% of the contemporary Ashkenazi Jewish population descends matrilineally from merely four distinct "founder lineages." These maternal ancestors were posited as "likely from a Hebrew/Levantine mtDNA pool" with a Middle Eastern origin during the first and second centuries CE. The research further indicated that the remaining Ashkenazi mitochondrial lineages derive from approximately 150 women, a majority also probable of Middle Eastern ancestry. Regarding haplogroup K specifically, the authors argued that, despite its prevalence across western Eurasia, the distribution pattern makes it highly improbable that the four founder lineages were introduced into the Ashkenazi gene pool via admixture with a European host population.

input: The radio stations in San Diego include nationwide broadcaster, Clear Channel Communications; CBS Radio, Midwest Television, Lincoln Financial Media, Finest City Broadcasting, and many other smaller stations and networks. input: Extended systems of underwater caves, sinkholes and springs are found throughout the state and supply most of the water used by residents. The limestone is topped with sandy soils deposited as ancient beaches over millions of years as global sea levels rose and fell. During the last glacial period, lower sea levels and a drier climate revealed a much wider peninsula, largely savanna. The Everglades, an enormously wide, slow-flowing river encompasses the southern tip of the peninsula. Sinkhole damage claims on property in the state exceeded a total of $2 billion from 2006 through 2010.
rewrite: The state's extensive network of underwater caves, sinkholes, and springs constitutes the primary freshwater source for its population. Overlying the limestone bedrock are sandy soils, remnants of ancient beach deposits accumulated over millions of years of fluctuating sea levels. During the last glacial period, reduced sea levels and arid conditions exposed a broader peninsula, predominantly characterized as savanna. The southern peninsula is dominated by the Everglades, a vast, slow-moving river system. Notably, property damage claims related to sinkholes surpassed $2 billion between 2006 and 2010.

input: Tibet was once a strong power contemporaneous with Tang China (618–907). Until the Tibetan Empire's collapse in the 9th century, it was the Tang's major rival in dominating Inner Asia. The Yarlung rulers of Tibet also signed various peace treaties with the Tang, culminating in a treaty in 821 that fixed the borders between Tibet and China.
rewrite: The Tibetan Empire, a significant power contemporaneous with Tang China (618–907), served as the Tang Dynasty's primary rival for influence in Inner Asia until its ninth-century collapse. This period also included diplomatic engagements, notably a formal 821 treaty that established a fixed border between the two polities.

input: The first newspaper in Namibia was the German-language Windhoeker Anzeiger, founded 1898. Radio was introduced in 1969, TV in 1981. During German rule, the newspapers mainly reflected the living reality and the view of the white German-speaking minority. The black majority was ignored or depicted as a threat. During South African rule, the white bias continued, with mentionable influence of the Pretoria government on the "South West African" media system. Independent newspapers were seen as a menace to the existing order, critical journalists threatened.
rewrite: The inaugural newspaper in Namibia, the German-language Windhoeker Anzeiger, was established in 1898, followed by radio in 1969 and television in 1981. Under German colonial administration, the press predominantly reflected the perspectives and lived reality of the white German-speaking minority, while largely ignoring or portraying the Black majority as a threat. This institutional bias persisted during South African rule, with significant governmental influence from Pretoria over the media in "South West Africa." Independent publications were perceived as subversive, and critical journalists faced intimidation.

input: Hemimetabolous insects, those with incomplete metamorphosis, change gradually by undergoing a series of molts. An insect molts when it outgrows its exoskeleton, which does not stretch and would otherwise restrict the insect's growth. The molting process begins as the insect's epidermis secretes a new epicuticle inside the old one. After this new epicuticle is secreted, the epidermis releases a mixture of enzymes that digests the endocuticle and thus detaches the old cuticle. When this stage is complete, the insect makes its body swell by taking in a large quantity of water or air, which makes the old cuticle split along predefined weaknesses where the old exocuticle was thinnest.:142
rewrite: Hemimetabolous insects, characterized by incomplete metamorphosis, develop gradually through successive molts. Molting occurs when the rigid, non-expansile exoskeleton becomes too restrictive for growth. The process initiates as the epidermis secretes a new epicuticle beneath the existing cuticle. Subsequently, the epidermis releases enzymatic compounds that digest the endocuticle, thereby separating the old cuticle. Following this digestion, the insect ingests substantial air or water to increase internal pressure, causing the old exoskeleton to rupture along predetermined lines of weakness where the exocuticle is thinnest.

input: Following the death of Grand Prince Igor in 945, his wife Olga ruled as regent in Kiev until their son Sviatoslav reached maturity (ca. 963). His decade-long reign over Rus' was marked by rapid expansion through the conquest of the Khazars of the Pontic steppe and the invasion of the Balkans. By the end of his short life, Sviatoslav carved out for himself the largest state in Europe, eventually moving his capital from Kiev to Pereyaslavets on the Danube in 969. In contrast with his mother's conversion to Christianity, Sviatoslav, like his druzhina, remained a staunch pagan. Due to his abrupt death in an ambush in 972, Sviatoslav's conquests, for the most part, were not consolidated into a functioning empire, while his failure to establish a stable succession led to a fratricidal feud among his sons, which resulted in two of his three sons being killed.
rewrite: Following the demise of Grand Prince Igor in 945, his widow, Olga, governed the Kievan realm as regent until their son, Sviatoslav, attained maturity around 963. Sviatoslav’s subsequent decade-long reign was characterized by aggressive military expansion, including the subjugation of the Khazar Khaganate in the Pontic steppe and campaigns into the Balkans. By his death, he had forged the most extensive polity in Europe, transferring his capital from Kiev to Pereyaslavets on the Danube in 969. In contrast to Olga’s conversion to Christianity, Sviatoslav and his *druzhina* (retinue) remained committed pagans. His abrupt death in an ambush in 972 prevented the consolidation of his conquests into a durable empire. Furthermore, his lack of a clear succession plan precipitated a fratricidal war among his sons, leading to the death of two of the three siblings.

input: In December 2014, Myanmar signed an agreement to set up its first stock exchange. The Yangon Stock Exchange Joint Venture Co. Ltd will be set up with Myanma Economic Bank sharing 51 percent, Japan's Daiwa Institute of Research Ltd 30.25 percent and Japan Exchange Group 18.75 percent. The Yangon Stock Exchange (YSX) officially opened for business on Friday, March 25, 2016. First Myanmar Investment Co., Ltd. (FMI) became the first stock to be traded after receiving approval for an opening price of 26,000 kyats ($22).
rewrite: In December 2014, Myanmar established a joint venture to create its inaugural securities exchange. The entity, Yangon Stock Exchange Joint Venture Co. Ltd., is owned 51% by Myanma Economic Bank, 30.25% by Japan's Daiwa Institute of Research Ltd., and 18.75% by Japan Exchange Group. The Yangon Stock Exchange (YSX) commenced official operations on March 25, 2016. First Myanmar Investment Co., Ltd. (FMI) was the first listed security, trading at an approved opening price of 26,000 kyats (approximately $22).

input: The Galician road network includes autopistas and autovías connecting the major cities, as well as national and secondary roads to the rest of the municipalities. The Autovía A-6 connects A Coruña and Lugo to Madrid, entering Galicia at Pedrafita do Cebreiro. The Autovía A-52 connects O Porriño, Ourense and Benavente, and enters Galicia at A Gudiña. Two more autovías are under construction. Autovía A-8 enters Galicia on the Cantabrian coast, and ends in Baamonde (Lugo province). Autovía A-76 enters Galicia in Valdeorras; it is an upgrade of the existing N-120 to Ourense and Vigo.
rewrite: The Galician road infrastructure comprises a system of autopistas and autovías linking primary urban centers, supplemented by national and secondary routes serving other municipalities. The A-6 connects A Coruña and Lugo to Madrid, entering the region at Pedrafita do Cebreiro. The A-52, entering at A Gudiña, links O Porriño and Ourense to Benavente. Two additional autovías are currently under construction: the A-8, entering along the Cantabrian coast and terminating in Baamonde (Lugo), and the A-76, an upgrade of the N-120 entering at Valdeorras and extending to Ourense and Vigo.

input: The TD Garden, formerly called the FleetCenter and built to replace the old, since-demolished Boston Garden, is adjoined to North Station and is the home of two major league teams: the Boston Bruins of the National Hockey League and the Boston Celtics of the National Basketball Association. The arena seats 18,624 for basketball games and 17,565 for ice hockey games. The Bruins were the first American member of the National Hockey League and an Original Six franchise. The Boston Celtics were founding members of the Basketball Association of America, one of the two leagues that merged to form the NBA. The Celtics have the distinction of having won more championships than any other NBA team, with seventeen.
rewrite: TD Garden, originally named the FleetCenter, was constructed to replace the demolished Boston Garden. Adjacent to North Station, it serves as the home venue for two major professional franchises: the Boston Bruins of the National Hockey League and the Boston Celtics of the National Basketball Association. The arena's capacity is 18,624 for basketball and 17,565 for hockey. The Bruins are an Original Six franchise and were the NHL's first American member. The Celtics were founding members of the Basketball Association of America, a precursor league to the NBA, and hold a record seventeen championships, the most in NBA history.

input: Charlemagne planned to continue the Frankish tradition of dividing his kingdom between all his heirs, but was unable to do so as only one son, Louis the Pious (r. 814–840), was still alive by 813. Just before Charlemagne died in 814, he crowned Louis as his successor. Louis's reign of 26 years was marked by numerous divisions of the empire among his sons and, after 829, civil wars between various alliances of father and sons over the control of various parts of the empire. Eventually, Louis recognised his eldest son Lothair I (d. 855) as emperor and gave him Italy. Louis divided the rest of the empire between Lothair and Charles the Bald (d. 877), his youngest son. Lothair took East Francia, comprising both banks of the Rhine and eastwards, leaving Charles West Francia with the empire to the west of the Rhineland and the Alps. Louis the German (d. 876), the middle child, who had been rebellious to the last, was allowed to keep Bavaria under the suzerainty of his elder brother. The division was disputed. Pepin II of Aquitaine (d. after 864), the emperor's grandson, rebelled in a contest for Aquitaine, while Louis the German tried to annex all of East Francia. Louis the Pious died in 840, with the empire still in chaos.
rewrite:
Charlemagne initially intended to adhere to the Frankish custom of partitioning his realm among his legitimate heirs. However, by 813, only a single son, Louis the Pious (r. 814–840), survived, compelling a singular succession. Charlemagne formally crowned Louis as co-emperor shortly before his own death in 814. Louis’s twenty-six-year reign was subsequently defined by repeated divisions of the imperial territory among his own sons and, particularly after 829, by intermittent civil wars. These conflicts involved shifting alliances between the emperor and his sons, each vying for control over specific regions.

In a later settlement, Louis ultimately recognized his eldest son, Lothair I (d. 855), as emperor and granted him Italy. The remaining territories were apportioned between Lothair and the youngest son, Charles the Bald (d. 877). Lothair received East Francia, encompassing lands on both sides of the Rhine and extending eastward, while Charles was allotted West Francia, comprising regions west of the Rhineland and the Alps. The middle son, the previously rebellious Louis the German (d. 876), was permitted to retain Bavaria under the suzerainty of his elder brother. This arrangement proved unstable. It was contested by Pepin II of Aquitaine (d. after 864), the emperor’s grandson, who rebelled to claim Aquitaine, and by Louis the German, who sought to seize all of East Francia. Consequently, when Louis the Pious died in 840, the Carolingian Empire remained in a state of profound disorder.

input: High neoclassicism was an international movement. Though neoclassical architecture employed the same classical vocabulary as Late Baroque architecture, it tended to emphasize its planar qualities, rather than sculptural volumes. Projections and recessions and their effects of light and shade were more flat; sculptural bas-reliefs were flatter and tended to be enframed in friezes, tablets or panels. Its clearly articulated individual features were isolated rather than interpenetrating, autonomous and complete in themselves.
