rewrite: High neoclassicism constituted an international architectural movement. While utilizing the classical vocabulary of the Late Baroque, it emphasized planar qualities over sculptural volumes. Projections, recessions, and their chiaroscuro effects were rendered more flatly; bas-reliefs became flatter and were often framed within friezes or panels. Its individual features were clearly articulated, isolated, and autonomous, presenting as complete entities rather than interpenetrating forms.

input: Before creation of Warsaw Pact, fearing Germany rearmed, Czechoslovak leadership sought to create security pact with East Germany and Poland. These states protested strongly against re-militarization of West Germany. The Warsaw Pact was primarily put in place as a consequence of the rearming of West Germany inside NATO. Soviet leaders, as many European countries in both western and eastern side, feared Germany being once again a military power as a direct threat and German militarism remained a fresh memory among Soviets and Eastern Europeans. As Soviet Union had already bilateral treaties with all of its eastern satellites, the Pact has been long considered 'superfluous', and because of the rushed way in which it was conceived, NATO officials labeled it as a 'cardboard castle'. Previously, in March 1954, the USSR, fearing the restoration of German Militarism in West Germany, requested admission to NATO.
rewrite: The establishment of the Warsaw Pact was precipitated by the rearmament of West Germany and its integration into NATO, a development viewed with acute apprehension by the Soviet Union and its Eastern European allies. Czechoslovak efforts to forge a security agreement with Poland and East Germany prior to the Pact underscored regional fears of resurgent German militarism, a potent memory from the recent war. Although the Soviet Union maintained bilateral defense treaties with its satellite states, rendering a multilateral pact ostensibly superfluous, the formalization of the Warsaw Treaty Organization served as a direct political and military counterweight to NATO. Its rapid conception led some contemporary NATO officials to dismiss it as a mere "cardboard castle." Notably, Soviet anxieties were further evidenced by a prior diplomatic overture in March 1954, when the USSR, seeking to forestall West German militarization, unsuccessfully petitioned for NATO membership itself.

input: Racial discrimination continued to be enacted in new laws in the 20th century, for instance the one-drop rule was enacted in Virginia's 1924 Racial Integrity Law and in other southern states, in part influenced by the popularity of eugenics and ideas of racial purity. People buried fading memories that many whites had multiracial ancestry. Many families were multiracial. Similar laws had been proposed but not passed in the late nineteenth century in South Carolina and Virginia, for instance. After regaining political power in Southern states by disenfranchising blacks, white Democrats passed laws to impose Jim Crow and racial segregation to restore white supremacy. They maintained these until forced to change in the 1960s and after by enforcement of federal legislation authorizing oversight of practices to protect the constitutional rights of African Americans and other minority citizens.
rewrite: The twentieth century witnessed the continued codification of racial discrimination through new legislation. Notably, Virginia’s 1924 Racial Integrity Act, alongside statutes in other southern states, institutionalized the "one-drop rule." This was partly driven by the contemporary influence of eugenics and ideologies of racial purity, which obscured the historical reality of widespread multiracial ancestry among white families. While similar legal measures had been proposed, yet failed, in late nineteenth-century South Carolina and Virginia, their eventual enactment followed the disenfranchisement of Black voters. Having regained political control, white Democratic legislators established Jim Crow laws and racial segregation to reinstate white supremacy. These systems remained entrenched until the 1960s and beyond, when federal legislation was enforced to oversee state practices and protect the constitutional rights of African Americans and other minorities.

input: Breeding usually involves some form of courtship display, typically performed by the male. Most displays are rather simple and involve some type of song. Some displays, however, are quite elaborate. Depending on the species, these may include wing or tail drumming, dancing, aerial flights, or communal lekking. Females are generally the ones that drive partner selection, although in the polyandrous phalaropes, this is reversed: plainer males choose brightly coloured females. Courtship feeding, billing and allopreening are commonly performed between partners, generally after the birds have paired and mated.
rewrite: Courtship displays, typically conducted by males, are integral to avian breeding. While many such displays are relatively simple vocalizations, others are more elaborate, potentially involving drumming, dancing, aerial maneuvers, or communal lekking. Mate selection is generally driven by females, though this is reversed in polyandrous species like phalaropes, where males select more ornamented females. Following pair formation, common affiliative behaviors include courtship feeding, billing, and allopreening.

input: The Staten Island Ferry is the world's busiest ferry route, carrying approximately 20 million passengers on the 5.2-mile (8.4 km) route between Staten Island and Lower Manhattan and running 24 hours a day. Other ferry systems shuttle commuters between Manhattan and other locales within the city and the metropolitan area.
rewrite: The Staten Island Ferry operates the world's busiest route, transporting roughly 20 million passengers annually on its 5.2-mile, 24-hour service between Staten Island and Lower Manhattan. Additional ferry systems serve commuters traveling between Manhattan and other city or metropolitan locales.

input: The concept's origins can potentially be traced back further. Jewish law includes several considerations whose effects are similar to those of modern intellectual property laws, though the notion of intellectual creations as property does not seem to exist – notably the principle of Hasagat Ge'vul (unfair encroachment) was used to justify limited-term publisher (but not author) copyright in the 16th century. In 500 BCE, the government of the Greek state of Sybaris offered one year's patent "to all who should discover any new refinement in luxury".
rewrite: The origins of this concept may extend further into history. Jewish law encompasses principles analogous to modern intellectual property, despite lacking a formal notion of creative works as property. Notably, the doctrine of Hasagat Ge'vul (unfair encroachment) supported limited-term publisher copyrights in the 16th century. Earlier, in 500 BCE, the Greek state of Sybaris granted one-year patents to inventors of novel luxuries.

input: In addition, the Prussian military education system was superior to the French model; Prussian staff officers were trained to exhibit initiative and independent thinking. Indeed, this was Moltke's expectation. The French, meanwhile, suffered from an education and promotion system that stifled intellectual development. According to the military historian Dallas Irvine, the system "was almost completely effective in excluding the army's brain power from the staff and high command. To the resulting lack of intelligence at the top can be ascribed all the inexcusable defects of French military policy."
rewrite: Moreover, the Prussian military education system surpassed the French model by rigorously training staff officers to demonstrate initiative and independent thought, in accordance with Moltke’s doctrine. Conversely, the French system of education and promotion actively suppressed intellectual development. As military historian Dallas Irvine argues, it “was almost completely effective in excluding the army’s brain power from the staff and high command,” a deficiency which explains the profound failures in French military policy.

input: Stemmatics, stemmology or stemmatology is a rigorous approach to textual criticism. Karl Lachmann (1793–1851) greatly contributed to making this method famous, even though he did not invent it. The method takes its name from the word stemma. The Ancient Greek word στέμματα and its loanword in classical Latin stemmata may refer to "family trees". This specific meaning shows the relationships of the surviving witnesses (the first known example of such a stemma, albeit with the name, dates from 1827). The family tree is also referred to as a cladogram. The method works from the principle that "community of error implies community of origin." That is, if two witnesses have a number of errors in common, it may be presumed that they were derived from a common intermediate source, called a hyparchetype. Relations between the lost intermediates are determined by the same process, placing all extant manuscripts in a family tree or stemma codicum descended from a single archetype. The process of constructing the stemma is called recension, or the Latin recensio.
rewrite: Stemmatics, also termed stemmatology, constitutes a rigorous methodological framework within textual criticism. Although not devised by Karl Lachmann (1793–1851), his scholarly efforts were instrumental in its widespread adoption. The discipline derives its name from the word *stemma*, originating from the Ancient Greek *στέμματα* and its Latin loanword *stemmata*, which can denote “family trees.” This specific denotation reflects the genealogical relationships among surviving manuscript witnesses; the earliest recorded stemma employing this terminology dates from 1827. Such a structure is also described as a cladogram. The method operates on the principle that “community of error implies community of origin.” Consequently, when two witnesses share a set of errors, it is inferred that they descend from a common intermediary source, termed a hyparchetype. By recursively applying this analytical process to lost intermediaries, all extant manuscripts can be situated within a comprehensive genealogical tree, or *stemma codicum*, ultimately derived from a single archetype. The procedure of reconstructing this stemma is designated recension, from the Latin *recensio*.

input: Although a resonant antenna has a purely resistive feed-point impedance at a particular frequency, many (if not most) applications require using an antenna over a range of frequencies. An antenna's bandwidth specifies the range of frequencies over which its performance does not suffer due to a poor impedance match. Also in the case of a Yagi-Uda array, the use of the antenna very far away from its design frequency reduces the antenna's directivity, thus reducing the usable bandwidth regardless of impedance matching.
rewrite: While a resonant antenna exhibits a purely resistive feed-point impedance at a specific frequency, most practical applications necessitate its operation across a frequency range. Bandwidth defines the span over which performance remains acceptable despite impedance mismatch. Furthermore, in a Yagi-Uda array, operation significantly beyond its design frequency diminishes directivity, thereby constraining the functional bandwidth irrespective of impedance considerations.

input: Peer groups are essential to social and general development. Communication with peers increases significantly during adolescence and peer relationships become more intense than in other stages  and more influential to the teen, affecting both the decisions and choices being made. High quality friendships may enhance children's development regardless of the characteristics of those friends. As children begin to bond with various people and create friendships, it later helps them when they are adolescent and sets up the framework for adolescence and peer groups. Peer groups are especially important during adolescence, a period of development characterized by a dramatic increase in time spent with peers and a decrease in adult supervision. Adolescents also associate with friends of the opposite sex much more than in childhood and tend to identify with larger groups of peers based on shared characteristics. It is also common for adolescents to use friends as coping devices in different situations. A three-factor structure of dealing with friends including avoidance, mastery, and nonchalance has shown that adolescents use friends as coping devices with social stresses.
rewrite: Peer groups play a crucial role in social and general development. During adolescence, communication with peers intensifies significantly, and these relationships gain greater influence over the individual compared to other life stages, substantially impacting decision-making processes. High-quality friendships can positively contribute to a child’s development, irrespective of the specific characteristics of the friends involved. The formative bonds and friendships established in childhood provide a foundational framework for adolescent peer interactions. Adolescence itself is marked by a pronounced increase in time dedicated to peers alongside a reduction in adult supervision. This period also involves more frequent association with opposite-sex friends and a tendency to identify with broader peer collectives based on shared attributes. Furthermore, adolescents commonly utilize friendships as coping mechanisms in various contexts. Research indicates a three-factor structure—encompassing avoidance, mastery, and nonchalance—through which adolescents employ friends to manage social stressors.

input: Israel operates under a parliamentary system as a democratic republic with universal suffrage. A member of parliament supported by a parliamentary majority becomes the prime minister—usually this is the chair of the largest party. The prime minister is the head of government and head of the cabinet. Israel is governed by a 120-member parliament, known as the Knesset. Membership of the Knesset is based on proportional representation of political parties, with a 3.25% electoral threshold, which in practice has resulted in coalition governments.
rewrite: Israel functions as a parliamentary democracy, with a 120-member unicameral legislature known as the Knesset. Members are elected via a system of nationwide proportional representation, subject to a 3.25 percent electoral threshold. This structure typically necessitates coalition governments. The Prime Minister, who serves as head of government and cabinet, is ordinarily the leader of the largest party and must command the confidence of a parliamentary majority.

input: However, from 1971 to 1975, NBA teams played preseason exhibitions against American Basketball Association teams. In the early days of the NBA, league clubs sometimes challenged the legendary barnstorming Harlem Globetrotters, with mixed success. The NBA has played preseason games in Europe and Asia. In the 2006 and 2007 seasons, the NBA and the primary European club competition, the Euroleague, conducted a preseason tournament featuring two NBA teams and the finalists from that year's Euroleague.[citation needed] In the 1998-99 and 2011-12 seasons, teams were limited to only two preseason games due to lockouts.
rewrite: Between 1971 and 1975, NBA teams engaged in preseason exhibitions against American Basketball Association clubs. Historically, NBA franchises also occasionally competed against the renowned barnstorming Harlem Globetrotters, achieving varied results. The league has further expanded its preseason presence internationally, hosting games in Europe and Asia. Notably, a 2006 and 2007 preseason tournament involved two NBA teams and the Euroleague finalists. Preseason schedules have occasionally been abbreviated, as during the 1998–99 and 2011–12 lockouts, when teams were restricted to only two contests.

input: Traditionally, the Speaker is reckoned as the leader of the majority party in the House, with the Majority Leader as second-in-command. For instance, when the Republicans gained the majority in the House after the 2010 elections, Eric Cantor succeeded Boehner as Majority Leader. Despite this, Cantor and his successor, Kevin McCarthy, have been reckoned as the second-ranking Republicans in the House, since Boehner is still reckoned as the leader of the House Republicans. However, there have been some exceptions. The most recent exception to this rule came when Majority Leader Tom DeLay generally overshadowed Speaker Dennis Hastert from 2003 to 2006. In contrast, the Minority Leader is the undisputed leader of the minority party.
rewrite: Conventionally, the Speaker of the House is considered the leader of the majority party, with the Majority Leader serving as the second-ranking member. Following the 2010 elections, for example, Eric Cantor succeeded John Boehner as Majority Leader under Republican control. Both Cantor and his successor, Kevin McCarthy, were regarded as the second-ranking Republicans, as Boehner remained the party's leader as Speaker. This hierarchy, however, has experienced exceptions. Most notably, from 2003 to 2006, Majority Leader Tom DeLay was widely perceived to wield greater influence than Speaker Dennis Hastert. Conversely, the Minority Leader is unequivocally the principal leader of the minority party in the House.

input: Molotov declared in his report entitled "On the Foreign Policy of the Soviet Union" (31 October 1939) held on the fifth (extraordinary) session of the Supreme Soviet, that the Western "ruling circles" disguise their intentions with the pretext of defending democracy against Hitlerism, declaring "their aim in war with Germany is nothing more, nothing less than extermination of Hitlerism. [...] There is absolutely no justification for this kind of war. The ideology of Hitlerism, just like any other ideological system, can be accepted or rejected, this is a matter of political views. But everyone grasps, that an ideology can not be exterminated by force, must not be finished off with a war."
rewrite: In his address titled "On the Foreign Policy of the Soviet Union," delivered at the fifth extraordinary session of the Supreme Soviet on 31 October 1939, Molotov asserted that Western ruling circles concealed their true aims under the pretense of defending democracy from Hitlerism. He stated their proclaimed war objective was "nothing more, nothing less than extermination of Hitlerism," a goal he deemed entirely unjustifiable. Molotov argued that Hitlerism, as an ideological system, could be accepted or rejected as a matter of political perspective. He contended, however, that an ideology cannot be eradicated through force, and thus must not be pursued as a justification for war.

input: Instruments were marketed by teacher-dealers, much as the title character in the popular musical The Music Man. Often, these teacher-dealers conducted mandolin orchestras: groups of 4-50 musicians who played various mandolin family instruments. However, alongside the teacher-dealers were serious musicians, working to create a spot for the instrument in classical music, ragtime and jazz. Like the teacher-dealers, they traveled the U.S., recording records, giving performances and teaching individuals and mandolin orchestras. Samuel Siegel played mandolin in Vaudeville and became one of America's preeminent mandolinists. Seth Weeks was an African American who not only taught and performed in the United States, but also in Europe, where he recorded records. Another pioneering African American musician and director who made his start with a mandolin orchestra was composer James Reese Europe. W. Eugene Page toured the country with a group, and was well known for his mandolin and mandola performances. Other names include Valentine Abt, Samuel Adelstein, William Place, Jr., and Aubrey Stauffer.
rewrite: The dissemination of musical instruments was frequently facilitated by teacher-dealers, analogous to the protagonist in *The Music Man*. These individuals often directed mandolin orchestras, ensembles ranging from four to fifty musicians performing on various instruments within the mandolin family. Concurrently, a cadre of dedicated musicians worked to establish the mandolin within classical, ragtime, and jazz repertoires. Mirroring the itinerant nature of the teacher-dealers, these performers toured nationally, recording discs, presenting concerts, and offering instruction to both individuals and orchestras. Notable figures include Samuel Siegel, a vaudeville performer who rose to national prominence, and Seth Weeks, an African American musician who taught and performed extensively in the United States and Europe, where he made recordings. Pioneering composer and director James Reese Europe also began his career within a mandolin orchestra. W. Eugene Page gained renown touring with an ensemble and for his performances on mandolin and mandola. Further significant contributors were Valentine Abt, Samuel Adelstein, William Place, Jr., and Aubrey Stauffer.

input: Ethnically and linguistically the population of the Republic of the Congo is diverse—Ethnologue recognises 62 spoken languages in the country—but can be grouped into three categories. The Kongo are the largest ethnic group and form roughly half of the population. The most significant subgroups of the Kongo are Laari in Brazzaville and Pool regions and Vili around Pointe-Noire and along the Atlantic coast. The second largest group are the Teke who live to the north of Brazzaville with 17% of the population. Boulangui (M’Boshi) live in the northwest and in Brazzaville and form 12% of the population. Pygmies make up 2% of Congo's population.
rewrite: The Republic of the Congo exhibits notable ethnic and linguistic diversity, with Ethnologue documenting 62 spoken languages. This population can be broadly categorized into three principal groups. The Kongo constitute the largest ethnicity, comprising approximately half of the populace, with key subgroups including the Laari in the Brazzaville and Pool regions and the Vili near Pointe-Noire and the Atlantic coast. The Teke, representing about 17%, form the second-largest group and reside north of Brazzaville. The Boulangui (M’Boshi), accounting for 12%, inhabit the northwest and Brazzaville, while Pygmies represent an estimated 2% of the national population.

input: At the end of the 12th century, Europe was divided into a multitude of city states and kingdoms. The area encompassing modern Germany, southern Denmark, the Netherlands, Belgium, Luxembourg, Switzerland, Austria, Slovakia, Czech Republic and much of northern Italy (excluding Venice and Papal State) was nominally part of the Holy Roman Empire, but local rulers exercised considerable autonomy. France, Denmark, Poland, Hungary, Portugal, Scotland, Castile, Aragon, Navarre, Sicily and Cyprus were independent kingdoms, as was the Angevin Empire, whose Plantagenet kings ruled England and large domains in what was to become modern France. Norway came under the influence of England, while the other Scandinavian countries and Poland were influenced by trading contacts with the Hanseatic League. Angevin kings brought the Gothic tradition from France to Southern Italy, while Lusignan kings introduced French Gothic architecture to Cyprus.
rewrite: By the late twelfth century, the European political landscape was characterized by fragmentation into numerous city-states and kingdoms. The Holy Roman Empire nominally encompassed territories approximating modern Germany, southern Denmark, the Low Countries, Switzerland, Austria, the Czech and Slovak lands, and much of northern Italy (excluding Venice and the Papal States), yet local rulers retained substantial autonomy. Sovereign monarchies included France, Denmark, Poland, Hungary, Portugal, Scotland, the Iberian kingdoms of Castile, Aragon, and Navarre, Sicily, Cyprus, and the Angevin Empire, wherein the Plantagenet dynasty governed England and extensive continental holdings. Norway fell within the English sphere of influence, whereas other Scandinavian realms and Poland were shaped by commercial ties to the Hanseatic League. Cultural transmission occurred through dynastic channels, as Angevin rulers imported the Gothic tradition from France to southern Italy, and the Lusignan kings introduced French Gothic architecture to Cyprus.

input: On December 3, 2013, Adidas officially confirmed a new shoe collaboration deal with West. After months of anticipation and rumors, West confirmed the release of the Adidas Yeezy Boosts with a Twitter announcement directing fans to the domain yeezy.supply. In 2015, West unveiled his Yeezy Season clothing line, premiering Season 1 in collaboration with Adidas early in the year. The release of the Yeezy Boosts and the full Adidas collaboration was showcased in New York City on February 12, 2015, with free streaming to 50 cinemas in 13 countries around the world. An initial release of the Adidas Yeezy Boosts was limited to 9000 pairs to be available only in New York City via the Adidas smartphone app; the Adidas Yeezy Boosts were sold out within 10 minutes. The shoes released worldwide on February 28, 2015, were limited to select boutique stores and the Adidas UK stores. He followed with Season 2 later that year at New York Fashion Week. On February 11, West premiered his Yeezy Season 3 clothing line at Madison Square Garden in conjunction with the previewing of his album The Life of Pablo.
rewrite: On December 3, 2013, Adidas formally announced a collaborative footwear partnership with Kanye West. Following months of speculation, West confirmed the impending launch of the Adidas Yeezy Boost line via a Twitter post that directed followers to the domain yeezy.supply. The collaboration expanded in early 2015 with the debut of the Yeezy Season 1 apparel collection. A comprehensive presentation of the Yeezy Boost footwear and the broader Adidas partnership was held in New York City on February 12, 2015, with the event streamed live to fifty cinemas across thirteen nations. An initial, exclusive release of nine thousand pairs of the Adidas Yeezy Boost was conducted solely in New York City through the brand's mobile application, resulting in a complete sell-out within ten minutes. A subsequent global release on February 28, 2015, was restricted to select boutique retailers and Adidas outlets in the United Kingdom. West subsequently presented the Yeezy Season 2 collection during New York Fashion Week later that year. This was followed on February 11 of the next year by the premiere of Yeezy Season 3 at Madison Square Garden, an event that coincided with a preview of his album *The Life of Pablo*.

input: Synapses are the key functional elements of the brain. The essential function of the brain is cell-to-cell communication, and synapses are the points at which communication occurs. The human brain has been estimated to contain approximately 100 trillion synapses; even the brain of a fruit fly contains several million. The functions of these synapses are very diverse: some are excitatory (exciting the target cell); others are inhibitory; others work by activating second messenger systems that change the internal chemistry of their target cells in complex ways. A large number of synapses are dynamically modifiable; that is, they are capable of changing strength in a way that is controlled by the patterns of signals that pass through them. It is widely believed that activity-dependent modification of synapses is the brain's primary mechanism for learning and memory.
rewrite: Synapses constitute the fundamental functional units of the brain, serving as the specialized junctions where intercellular communication occurs. Estimates suggest the human brain contains roughly 100 trillion synapses, while even a fruit fly brain possesses several million. These structures exhibit considerable functional diversity: some are excitatory, others inhibitory, and a further subset operates via second messenger systems to alter the internal biochemistry of target cells. A substantial proportion of synapses are dynamically modifiable, meaning their strength can be altered in response to specific patterns of neural activity. This activity-dependent synaptic modification is widely regarded as the principal mechanism underlying learning and memory formation in the brain.

input: The highest portion of the range is divided by the glacial trough of the Rhone valley, with the Pennine Alps from Mont Blanc to the Matterhorn and Monte Rosa on the southern side, and the Bernese Alps on the northern. The peaks in the easterly portion of the range, in Austria and Slovenia, are smaller than those in the central and western portions.
rewrite: The range's highest section is bisected by the Rhone valley glacial trough, separating the Pennine Alps to the south from the Bernese Alps to the north. Peaks within the eastern segment, located in Austria and Slovenia, are of lesser elevation than those found in the central and western regions.

input: There are two basic forms of data packet, DATA0 and DATA1. A data packet must always be preceded by an address token, and is usually followed by a handshake token from the receiver back to the transmitter. The two packet types provide the 1-bit sequence number required by Stop-and-wait ARQ. If a USB host does not receive a response (such as an ACK) for data it has transmitted, it does not know if the data was received or not; the data might have been lost in transit, or it might have been received but the handshake response was lost.
rewrite: Data transmission employs two fundamental packet types, DATA0 and DATA1. Each data packet is preceded by an address token and typically succeeded by a receiver-to-transmitter handshake token. These alternating packet types supply the essential one-bit sequence number for the Stop-and-wait ARQ protocol. Consequently, if a USB host receives no response, such as an ACK, it cannot determine whether the original data or the subsequent handshake was lost during transmission.

input: Charleston has a humid subtropical climate (Köppen climate classification Cfa), with mild winters, hot, humid summers, and significant rainfall all year long. Summer is the wettest season; almost half of the annual rainfall occurs from June to September in the form of thundershowers. Fall remains relatively warm through November. Winter is short and mild, and is characterized by occasional rain. Measurable snow (≥0.1 in or 0.25 cm) only occurs several times per decade at the most, with the last such event occurring December 26, 2010. However, 6.0 in (15 cm) fell at the airport on December 23, 1989, the largest single-day fall on record, contributing to a single-storm and seasonal record of 8.0 in (20 cm) snowfall.
rewrite: Charleston experiences a humid subtropical climate (Köppen Cfa), characterized by mild winters, hot and humid summers, and considerable precipitation throughout the year. The summer months constitute the wettest period, with nearly half of the annual rainfall occurring from June through September, primarily as thunderstorms. Autumn remains comparatively warm into November. Winters are brief and mild, featuring intermittent rain. Measurable snowfall (≥0.1 in or 0.25 cm) is infrequent, occurring at most several times per decade, with the most recent instance recorded on December 26, 2010. Notably, the heaviest single-day snowfall was 6.0 inches (15 cm) on December 23, 1989, contributing to a record seasonal storm total of 8.0 inches (20 cm).

input: Murdoch found he had such a rapport with Larry Lamb over lunch that other potential recruits as editor were not interviewed and Lamb was appointed as the first editor of the new Sun. He was scathing in his opinion of the Mirror, where he had recently been employed as a senior sub-editor, and shared Murdoch's view that a paper's quality was best measured by its sales, and he regarded the Mirror as overstaffed, and primarily aimed at an ageing readership. Lamb hastily recruited a staff of about 125 reporters, who were mostly selected for their availability rather than their ability.
rewrite: Murdoch perceived such a strong rapport with Larry Lamb during their lunch that he forwent interviewing other candidates and directly appointed Lamb as the inaugural editor of the Sun. Lamb, recently a senior sub-editor at the Mirror, held a scathing view of that publication, aligning with Murdoch’s conviction that commercial success was the paramount measure of a newspaper’s quality. He criticized the Mirror as overstaffed and excessively oriented toward an aging demographic. Lamb promptly assembled a reporting staff of approximately 125 individuals, prioritizing their immediate availability over demonstrated journalistic ability.

input: The four-year, full-time undergraduate program comprises the majority of enrollments at the university and emphasizes instruction in the arts and sciences, plus the professions of engineering, journalism, communication, music, and education. Although a foundation in the liberal arts and sciences is required in all majors, there is no required common core curriculum; individual degree requirements are set by the faculty of each school. Northwestern's full-time undergraduate and graduate programs operate on an approximately 10-week academic quarter system with the academic year beginning in late September and ending in early June. Undergraduates typically take four courses each quarter and twelve courses in an academic year and are required to complete at least twelve quarters on campus to graduate. Northwestern offers honors, accelerated, and joint degree programs in medicine, science, mathematics, engineering, and journalism. The comprehensive doctoral graduate program has high coexistence with undergraduate programs.
rewrite: The university's primary enrollment consists of a four-year, full-time undergraduate curriculum centered on instruction in the arts, sciences, and professional fields including engineering, journalism, communication, music, and education. While all majors incorporate a foundational liberal arts and sciences component, no universal core curriculum exists; instead, specific degree requirements are established by the faculty within each school. The institution operates on a quarter system, with the full-time undergraduate and graduate academic year spanning from late September to early June across three approximately ten-week quarters. Undergraduate students typically enroll in four courses per quarter, totaling twelve annually, and must complete a minimum of twelve quarters in residence to graduate. The university provides honors, accelerated, and joint degree options in areas such as medicine, science, mathematics, engineering, and journalism. Its comprehensive doctoral program maintains substantial integration with undergraduate offerings.

input: In 2010, a genetic study was conducted on the mummified remains of baboons that were brought back as gifts from Punt by the ancient Egyptians. Led by a research team from the Egyptian Museum and the University of California, the scientists used oxygen isotope analysis to examine hairs from two baboon mummies that had been preserved in the British Museum. One of the baboons had distorted isotopic data, so the other's oxygen isotope values were compared to those of present-day baboon specimens from regions of interest. The researchers found that the mummies most closely matched modern baboon specimens in Eritrea and Ethiopia, which they suggested implied that Punt was likely a narrow region that included eastern Ethiopia and all of Eritrea.
rewrite: A 2010 genetic investigation analyzed mummified baboon remains, originally presented as gifts from Punt to ancient Egypt. A collaborative research team from the Egyptian Museum and the University of California performed oxygen isotope analysis on hairs from two baboon mummies housed in the British Museum. Due to distorted isotopic data from one specimen, the study focused on comparing the other's oxygen isotope values with those of modern baboon samples from potential regions. The results indicated the closest match with contemporary specimens from Eritrea and eastern Ethiopia. Consequently, the researchers proposed that the land of Punt likely comprised a confined territory encompassing eastern Ethiopia and the entirety of Eritrea.

input: After the Great Fire of Rome in 64 AD, Emperor Nero accused the Christians as convenient scapegoats, who were later persecuted and killed. From that point on, Roman official policy towards Christianity tended towards persecution. During the various Imperial crises of the 3rd century, “contemporaries were predisposed to decode any crisis in religious terms”, regardless of their allegiance to particular practices or belief systems. Christianity drew its traditional base of support from the powerless, who seemed to have no religious stake in the well-being of the Roman State, and therefore threatened its existence. The majority of Rome’s elite continued to observe various forms of inclusive Hellenistic monism; Neoplatonism in particular accommodated the miraculous and the ascetic within a traditional Graeco-Roman cultic framework. Christians saw these ungodly practices as a primary cause of economic and political crisis.
rewrite: Following the Great Fire of Rome in 64 AD, Emperor Nero initiated the persecution of Christians, casting them as convenient scapegoats. This established a precedent for subsequent Roman imperial policy, which increasingly inclined toward systematic suppression. During the third-century imperial crises, contemporaries widely interpreted such turmoil through a religious lens, irrespective of personal creed. Christianity derived its core adherents from among the disenfranchised, a demographic perceived as having no vested interest in the state’s religious welfare and thus posing a threat to its stability. Meanwhile, the Roman elite predominantly adhered to inclusive Hellenistic monistic traditions. Notably, Neoplatonism integrated the miraculous and ascetic within the established Graeco-Roman cultic system. Christians, in contrast, viewed these syncretic practices as fundamentally impious and a principal source of the era’s economic and political distress.

input: The first non-stop transatlantic crossing was made by the British airship R34 in 1919. Regular passenger service resumed in the 1920s and the discovery of helium reserves in the United States promised increased safety, but the U.S. government refused to sell the gas for this purpose. Therefore, H2 was used in the Hindenburg airship, which was destroyed in a midair fire over New Jersey on 6 May 1937. The incident was broadcast live on radio and filmed. Ignition of leaking hydrogen is widely assumed to be the cause, but later investigations pointed to the ignition of the aluminized fabric coating by static electricity. But the damage to hydrogen's reputation as a lifting gas was already done.
rewrite: The inaugural non-stop transatlantic flight was achieved by the British airship R34 in 1919. While regular passenger services recommenced in the 1920s and the discovery of helium reserves in the United States offered enhanced safety prospects, the U.S. government prohibited its sale for this application. Consequently, hydrogen was utilized in the Hindenburg airship, which was consumed by a midair fire over New Jersey on 6 May 1937. The event received extensive live radio and film coverage. Although the ignition of leaking hydrogen is the predominant causal hypothesis, subsequent investigations have suggested the aluminized fabric coating was ignited by static electricity. Nonetheless, the reputation of hydrogen as a lifting gas was irreparably damaged.

input: A 2009 Cochrane review concluded that thiazide antihypertensive drugs reduce the risk of death (RR 0.89), stroke (RR 0.63), coronary heart disease (RR 0.84), and cardiovascular events (RR 0.70) in people with high blood pressure. In the ensuring years other classes of antihypertensive drug were developed and found wide acceptance in combination therapy, including loop diuretics (Lasix/furosemide, Hoechst Pharmaceuticals, 1963), beta blockers (ICI Pharmaceuticals, 1964) ACE inhibitors, and angiotensin receptor blockers. ACE inhibitors reduce the risk of new onset kidney disease [RR 0.71] and death [RR 0.84] in diabetic patients, irrespective of whether they have hypertension.
rewrite: A 2009 Cochrane review established that thiazide antihypertensive agents significantly reduce the risk of mortality (RR 0.89), stroke (RR 0.63), coronary heart disease (RR 0.84), and overall cardiovascular events (RR 0.70) in hypertensive patients. Subsequently, additional drug classes gained prominence in combination regimens, such as loop diuretics (e.g., furosemide, 1963), beta blockers (1964), ACE inhibitors, and angiotensin receptor blockers. Notably, ACE inhibitors lower the risk of new-onset kidney disease (RR 0.71) and death (RR 0.84) in diabetic patients, independent of hypertensive status.

input: A count may be started at any time that a wrestler's shoulders are down (both shoulders touching the mat), back-first and any part of the opponent's body is lying over the wrestler. This often results in pins that can easily be kicked out of, if the defensive wrestler is even slightly conscious. For example, an attacking wrestler who is half-conscious may simply drape an arm over an opponent, or a cocky wrestler may place their foot gently on the opponent's body, prompting a three-count from the referee.
rewrite: A pinfall count may be initiated whenever a wrestler is positioned supine with both shoulders in contact with the mat and any portion of the opponent's body is positioned above them. This frequently leads to precarious pinning situations from which the defensive wrestler can readily escape with minimal awareness. For instance, a dazed attacker might merely rest an arm across an opponent, or an overconfident competitor could lightly place a foot on the opponent's torso, each action potentially eliciting a three-count from the official.

input: The Republic of Letters was the sum of a number of Enlightenment ideals: an egalitarian realm governed by knowledge that could act across political boundaries and rival state power. It was a forum that supported "free public examination of questions regarding religion or legislation". Immanuel Kant considered written communication essential to his conception of the public sphere; once everyone was a part of the "reading public", then society could be said to be enlightened. The people who participated in the Republic of Letters, such as Diderot and Voltaire, are frequently known today as important Enlightenment figures. Indeed, the men who wrote Diderot's Encyclopédie arguably formed a microcosm of the larger "republic".
rewrite: The Republic of Letters constituted a manifestation of core Enlightenment principles, representing an intellectual domain governed by reason and transcending political borders in a manner that could counterbalance state authority. It functioned as a discursive arena committed to the unrestricted public scrutiny of religious and legislative matters. Philosopher Immanuel Kant deemed written discourse fundamental to the public sphere, positing that a fully "reading public" signified an enlightened society. Key participants, including Denis Diderot and Voltaire, are now recognized as seminal Enlightenment thinkers. The collaborative network that produced Diderot's *Encyclopédie* itself exemplified a microcosm of this broader republic.

input: The Chicago Cubs have not won a World Series championship since 1908, and have not appeared in the Fall Classic since 1945, although between their postseason appearance in 1984 and their most recent in 2015, they have made the postseason seven times. 107 seasons is the longest championship drought in all four of the major North American professional sports leagues, which also includes the National Football League (NFL), the National Basketball Association (NBA), and the National Hockey League (NHL). In fact, the Cubs' last World Series title occurred before those other three leagues even existed, and even the Cubs' last World Series appearance predates the founding of the NBA. The much publicized drought was concurrent to championship droughts by the Boston Red Sox and the Chicago White Sox, who both had over 80 years between championships. It is this unfortunate distinction that has led to the club often being known as "The Lovable Losers." The team was one win away from breaking what is often called the "Curse of the Billy Goat" in 1984 and 2003 (Steve Bartman incident), but was unable get the victory that would send it to the World Series.
rewrite: The Chicago Cubs’ World Series championship drought, which began in 1908, represents the longest such period without a title among the four major North American professional sports leagues—Major League Baseball (MLB), the National Football League (NFL), the National Basketball Association (NBA), and the National Hockey League (NHL). The franchise has not appeared in the World Series since 1945, a span that predates the founding of the NBA. Despite seven postseason appearances between 1984 and 2015, the team has been unable to secure a championship. This protracted period of futility coincided with notable droughts of other franchises, including the Boston Red Sox and the Chicago White Sox, each of which endured over eighty years between titles. The Cubs’ distinctive history has contributed to the club’s colloquial moniker, “The Lovable Losers.” On two occasions, in 1984 and 2003 (the latter infamously associated with the Steve Bartman incident), the team came within a single victory of reaching the World Series, yet failed to overcome what is popularly termed the “Curse of the Billy Goat.”

input: The Carnival of Malmedy is locally called Cwarmê. Even if Malmedy is located in the east Belgium, near the German-speaking area, the Cwarmê is a pure walloon and Latin carnival. The celebration takes place during 4 days before the Shrove Tuesday. The Cwarmê Sunday is the most important and insteresting to see. All the old traditional costumes parade in the street. The Cwarmê is a "street carnival" and is not only a parade. People who are disguised pass through the crowd and perform a part of the traditional costume they wear. The famous traditional costumes at the Cwarmê of Malmedy are the Haguète, the Longuès-Brèsses and the Long-Né.
rewrite: The Carnival of Malmedy, locally designated as the Cwarmê, constitutes a distinctly Walloon and Latin tradition, notwithstanding the city's location in eastern Belgium proximate to German-speaking regions. This celebration occurs over the four days preceding Shrove Tuesday, with Cwarmê Sunday representing the most significant and visually engaging event. It functions as a "street carnival," characterized not merely by a parade but by active participation; costumed individuals move through the crowds to perform according to their specific roles. Notable traditional costumes include the Haguète, the Longuès-Brèsses, and the Long-Né.

input: On February 7, 1987, dozens of political prisoners were freed in the first group release since Khrushchev's "thaw" in the mid-1950s. On May 6, 1987, Pamyat, a Russian nationalist group, held an unsanctioned demonstration in Moscow. The authorities did not break up the demonstration and even kept traffic out of the demonstrators' way while they marched to an impromptu meeting with Boris Yeltsin, head of the Moscow Communist Party and at the time one of Gorbachev's closest allies. On July 25, 1987, 300 Crimean Tatars staged a noisy demonstration near the Kremlin Wall for several hours, calling for the right to return to their homeland, from which they were deported in 1944; police and soldiers merely looked on.
rewrite: On February 7, 1987, the Soviet government authorized the release of dozens of political prisoners, constituting the first such collective amnesty since the period of liberalization under Nikita Khrushchev in the mid-1950s. Subsequently, on May 6, an unsanctioned public demonstration was staged in Moscow by the Russian nationalist organization Pamyat. Authorities permitted the event to proceed unimpeded, even facilitating the marchers' passage to an impromptu meeting with Boris Yeltsin, then the Moscow Communist Party chief and a key ally of Mikhail Gorbachev. Further indicating a shift in state tolerance, approximately 300 Crimean Tatars conducted a vociferous protest near the Kremlin Wall on July 25, demanding repatriation to their homeland, from which they were forcibly removed in 1944; security personnel observed without intervention.

input: The length and nature of parental care varies widely amongst different orders and species. At one extreme, parental care in megapodes ends at hatching; the newly hatched chick digs itself out of the nest mound without parental assistance and can fend for itself immediately. At the other extreme, many seabirds have extended periods of parental care, the longest being that of the great frigatebird, whose chicks take up to six months to fledge and are fed by the parents for up to an additional 14 months. The chick guard stage describes the period of breeding during which one of the adult birds is permanently present at the nest after chicks have hatched. The main purpose of the guard stage is to aid offspring to thermoregulate and protect them from predation.
rewrite: Parental care exhibits considerable variation in duration and form across avian taxa. In megapodes, care concludes upon hatching; chicks independently emerge from the nest mound and are immediately self-sufficient. Conversely, many seabirds demonstrate protracted care, most notably the great frigatebird, whose chicks require up to six months to fledge and subsequently receive parental provisioning for an additional fourteen months. A distinct phase within this care is the chick guard stage, defined as the post-hatching period when at least one adult remains continuously at the nest. This stage primarily functions to facilitate offspring thermoregulation and provide protection from predators.

input: In Virginia prior to 1920, for example, a person was legally white if having seven-eights or more white ancestry. The one-drop rule originated in some Southern United States in the late 19th century, likely in response to whites' attempt to maintain white supremacy and limit black political power following the Democrats' regaining control of state legislatures in the late 1870s. The first year in which the U.S. Census dropped the mulatto category was 1920; that year enumerators were instructed to classify people in a binary way as white or black. This was a result of the Southern-dominated Congress convincing the Census Bureau to change its rules.
rewrite: Prior to 1920, Virginia law, for instance, legally defined a white person as one possessing seven-eighths or more white ancestry. The "one-drop rule" emerged in certain Southern states during the late 19th century, a development widely interpreted as a white supremacist effort to preserve political dominance and restrict African American power following the Democratic Party's resurgence in state legislatures in the late 1870s. Reflecting this shift, the 1920 U.S. Census eliminated the "mulatto" category, instructing enumerators to classify individuals within a strict black-white binary. This change resulted from pressure exerted by a Southern-dominated Congress upon the Census Bureau.

input: A sequence of events, or series of events, is a sequence of items, facts, events, actions, changes, or procedural steps, arranged in time order (chronological order), often with causality relationships among the items. Because of causality, cause precedes effect, or cause and effect may appear together in a single item, but effect never precedes cause. A sequence of events can be presented in text, tables, charts, or timelines. The description of the items or events may include a timestamp. A sequence of events that includes the time along with place or location information to describe a sequential path may be referred to as a world line.
rewrite: A sequence of events constitutes a chronological ordering of items, facts, actions, changes, or procedural steps, frequently interconnected by relationships of causality. Within such a sequence, a cause necessarily precedes its effect, though both may be encapsulated within a single element; an effect never precedes its cause. These sequences can be represented through textual narratives, tables, charts, or timelines, with individual elements potentially including temporal markers. When such a sequence incorporates both temporal and spatial data to delineate a sequential path, it may be termed a world line.

input: According to the prevailing theories of the settlement of the Americas, migrations of humans from Asia (in particular North Asia) to the Americas took place via Beringia, a land bridge which connected the two continents across what is now the Bering Strait. The majority of experts agree that the earliest pre-modern human migration via Beringia took place at least 13,500 years ago, with disputed evidence that people had migrated into the Americas much earlier, up to 40,000 years ago. These early Paleo-Indians spread throughout the Americas, diversifying into many hundreds of culturally distinct nations and tribes. According to the oral histories of many of the indigenous peoples of the Americas, they have been living there since their genesis, described by a wide range of creation myths.
rewrite: Prevailing theories regarding the peopling of the Americas posit that human populations migrated from Asia, specifically North Asia, into the Americas via Beringia. This now-submerged land bridge once connected the continents across the present-day Bering Strait. Scholarly consensus holds that the earliest confirmed migration occurred no later than approximately 13,500 years ago, though contested evidence suggests potential human presence as early as 40,000 years ago. These Paleo-Indians subsequently dispersed throughout the continents, diversifying into numerous culturally distinct nations and tribes. In contrast, the oral traditions and creation narratives of many Indigenous peoples assert their autochthonous origin, describing an unbroken presence in the Americas since their genesis.

input: The denomination with the longest history of objection to Freemasonry is the Roman Catholic Church. The objections raised by the Roman Catholic Church are based on the allegation that Masonry teaches a naturalistic deistic religion which is in conflict with Church doctrine. A number of Papal pronouncements have been issued against Freemasonry. The first was Pope Clement XII's In eminenti apostolatus, 28 April 1738; the most recent was Pope Leo XIII's Ab apostolici, 15 October 1890. The 1917 Code of Canon Law explicitly declared that joining Freemasonry entailed automatic excommunication, and banned books favouring Freemasonry.
rewrite: The Roman Catholic Church represents the most enduring denominational opposition to Freemasonry. Its objections are founded upon the assertion that Masonry promotes a naturalistic deistic religion incompatible with Catholic doctrine. This position has been formalized through multiple papal pronouncements, beginning with Pope Clement XII's *In eminenti apostolatus* in 1738 and extending to Pope Leo XIII's *Ab apostolici* in 1890. The 1917 Code of Canon Law further codified this stance, imposing automatic excommunication for membership and prohibiting literature supportive of Freemasonry.

input: Area air defence, the air defence of a specific area or location, (as opposed to point defence), have historically been operated by both armies (Anti-Aircraft Command in the British Army, for instance) and Air Forces (the United States Air Force's CIM-10 Bomarc). Area defence systems have medium to long range and can be made up of various other systems and networked into an area defence system (in which case it may be made up of several short range systems combined to effectively cover an area). An example of area defence is the defence of Saudi Arabia and Israel by MIM-104 Patriot missile batteries during the first Gulf War, where the objective was to cover populated areas.
rewrite: Area air defence, defined as the protection of a specified geographical zone rather than a single point, has historically fallen under the purview of both army and air force branches. Illustrative examples include the British Army's Anti-Aircraft Command and the United States Air Force's CIM-10 Bomarc. Such systems are characterized by medium to long operational ranges and may integrate various subsystems, potentially networking shorter-range components to achieve comprehensive coverage. A representative case is the deployment of MIM-104 Patriot missile batteries during the first Gulf War, which provided area defence for populated regions in Saudi Arabia and Israel.

input: With roots dating back to 1909 in the university's School of Social Economy, the George Warren Brown School of Social Work (commonly called the Brown School or Brown) was founded in 1925. Brown's academic degree offerings include a Master of Social Work (MSW), a Master of Public Health (MPH), a PhD in Social Work, and a PhD in Public Health Sciences. It is currently ranked first among Master of Social Work programs in the United States. The school was endowed by Bettie Bofinger Brown and named for her husband, George Warren Brown, a St. Louis philanthropist and co-founder of the Brown Shoe Company. The school was the first in the country to have a building for the purpose of social work education, and it is also a founding member of the Association of Schools and Programs of Public Health. The school is housed within Brown and Goldfarb Halls, but a third building expansion is currently in progress and slated to be completed in summer 2015. The new building, adjacent to Brown and Goldfarb Halls, targets LEED Gold certification and will add approximately 105,000 square feet, more than doubling the school's teaching, research, and program space.
rewrite:
The George Warren Brown School of Social Work, often referred to as the Brown School, was formally established in 1925, though its origins trace to 1909 within the university’s School of Social Economy. It was endowed by Bettie Bofinger Brown and named for her husband, George Warren Brown, a St. Louis philanthropist and co-founder of the Brown Shoe Company. The school confers a Master of Social Work (MSW), a Master of Public Health (MPH), a PhD in Social Work, and a PhD in Public Health Sciences. Its MSW program currently holds the top ranking in the United States.

A founding member of the Association of Schools and Programs of Public Health, the institution was also the nation’s first to occupy a building dedicated solely to social work education. It is primarily housed in Brown and Goldfarb Halls. A significant expansion was underway, with a third building adjacent to these halls scheduled for completion in summer 2015. Targeting LEED Gold certification, this approximately 105,000-square-foot addition was designed to more than double the school’s available space for teaching, research, and programs.

input: The oak forests of the southern and central Appalachians consist largely of black, northern red, white, chestnut and scarlet oaks (Quercus velutina, Q. rubra, Q. alba, Q. prinus and Q. coccinea) and hickories, such as the pignut (Carya glabra) in particular. The richest forests, which grade into mesic types, usually in coves and on gentle slopes, have dominantly white and northern red oaks, while the driest sites are dominated by chestnut oak, or sometimes by scarlet or northern red oaks. In the northern Appalachians the oaks, except for white and northern red, drop out, while the latter extends farthest north.
rewrite: The oak-dominated forests of the southern and central Appalachian region are primarily composed of black, northern red, white, chestnut, and scarlet oaks (*Quercus velutina, Q. rubra, Q. alba, Q. prinus, Q. coccinea*), along with hickories, notably pignut (*Carya glabra*). The most diverse stands, which transition to mesic communities, typically occur in coves and on moderate slopes and are chiefly dominated by white and northern red oaks. In contrast, the driest sites are predominantly occupied by chestnut oak, or occasionally by scarlet or northern red oaks. Within the northern Appalachians, oak species diminish, with only the white and northern red oaks persisting, the latter reaching the northernmost extent.

input: Dominic's search for a close relationship with God was determined and unceasing. He rarely spoke, so little of his interior life is known. What is known about it comes from accounts written by people near to him. St. Cecilia remembered him as cheerful, charitable and full of unceasing vigor. From a number of accounts, singing was apparently one of Dominic's great delights. Dominic practiced self-scourging and would mortify himself as he prayed alone in the chapel at night for 'poor sinners.' He owned a single habit, refused to carry money, and would allow no one to serve him.
rewrite: Dominic pursued an intimate relationship with God with singular and persistent determination. As he was a man of few words, his interior life remains largely obscure, known principally through the testimonies of his contemporaries. Saint Cecilia recalled him as perpetually cheerful, charitable, and vigorous. Multiple accounts indicate he found profound joy in singing. Dominic engaged in nocturnal penitential discipline, including self-scourging while praying alone for “poor sinners.” He owned only one habit, eschewed carrying money, and refused all personal service.

input: In his book, The Greatest Show on Earth: The Evidence for Evolution, biologist Richard Dawkins grapples with the question of why pain has to be so very painful. He describes the alternative as a simple, mental raising of a "red flag". To argue why that red flag might be insufficient, Dawkins explains that drives must compete with each other within living beings. The most fit creature would be the one whose pains are well balanced. Those pains which mean certain death when ignored will become the most powerfully felt. The relative intensities of pain, then, may resemble the relative importance of that risk to our ancestors (lack of food, too much cold, or serious injuries are felt as agony, whereas minor damage is felt as mere discomfort). This resemblance will not be perfect, however, because natural selection can be a poor designer. The result is often glitches in animals, including supernormal stimuli. Such glitches help explain pains which are not, or at least no longer directly adaptive (e.g. perhaps some forms of toothache, or injury to fingernails).
rewrite: In his work *The Greatest Show on Earth: The Evidence for Evolution*, biologist Richard Dawkins examines the necessity for pain to be intensely unpleasant. He posits a hypothetical alternative wherein an organism might merely register a cognitive “red flag.” Dawkins contends this simpler signal would be inadequate because multiple motivational drives compete within an organism. Evolutionary fitness, he argues, would favor creatures whose subjective pain responses are calibrated to biological urgency. Thus, pains signaling threats that would be fatal if ignored—such as severe starvation, extreme cold, or critical injury—evolve to be experienced as agonizing, while minor damage registers only as discomfort. Consequently, the relative intensity of different pains broadly mirrors the historical survival risks faced by ancestral populations. This correlation is imperfect, however, as natural selection is an imperfect design process, often producing systemic flaws. These include supernormal stimuli and other glitches, which help explain the persistence of pains with little or no direct adaptive value in modern contexts, such as certain toothaches or injuries to fingernails.

input: On March 27, 1964, the massive Good Friday earthquake killed 133 people and destroyed several villages and portions of large coastal communities, mainly by the resultant tsunamis and landslides. It was the second-most-powerful earthquake in the recorded history of the world, with a moment magnitude of 9.2. It was over one thousand times more powerful than the 1989 San Francisco earthquake. The time of day (5:36 pm), time of year and location of the epicenter were all cited as factors in potentially sparing thousands of lives, particularly in Anchorage.
rewrite: The magnitude 9.2 Good Friday earthquake of March 27, 1964, remains the second most powerful seismic event in recorded history. Its destructive force, over one thousand times greater than the 1989 San Francisco earthquake, resulted in 133 fatalities. The devastation to several villages and coastal communities was primarily caused by subsequent tsunamis and landslides. Scholarly analysis suggests that the timing—late afternoon on a holiday—and the epicenter's remote location mitigated casualties, potentially sparing thousands of lives in Anchorage.

input: In contrast to the Fed, the ECB normally does not buy bonds outright. The normal procedure used by the ECB for manipulating the money supply has been via the so-called refinancing facilities. In these facilities, bonds are not purchased but used in reverse transactions: repurchase agreements, or collateralised loans. These two transactions are similar, i.e. bonds are used as collaterals for loans, the difference being of legal nature. In the repos the ownership of the collateral changes to the ECB until the loan is repaid.
rewrite: Unlike the Federal Reserve, the European Central Bank typically abstains from direct bond purchases. Its standard monetary policy instrument involves refinancing operations, wherein bonds are not bought outright but utilized in reverse transactions—specifically repurchase agreements or collateralized loans. While both mechanisms similarly employ bonds as loan collateral, they differ legally. In repurchase agreements, ownership of the collateral temporarily transfers to the ECB until the loan's repayment.

input: The Shang dynasty oracle bone script and the Zhou dynasty scripts found on Chinese bronze inscriptions are no longer used; the oldest script that is still in use today is the Seal Script (篆書(书), zhuànshū). It evolved organically out of the Spring and Autumn period Zhou script, and was adopted in a standardized form under the first Emperor of China, Qin Shi Huang. The seal script, as the name suggests, is now used only in artistic seals. Few people are still able to read it effortlessly today, although the art of carving a traditional seal in the script remains alive; some calligraphers also work in this style.
rewrite: The oracle bone script of the Shang dynasty and the bronze inscription scripts of the Zhou dynasty are now obsolete. The most ancient writing system still in contemporary use is Seal Script (篆書, zhuànshū). This script developed organically from the Zhou scripts of the Spring and Autumn period before being standardized under the First Emperor of China, Qin Shi Huang. As its name implies, Seal Script is now employed almost exclusively for artistic name seals. While few individuals can read it with ease today, the traditional art of seal carving persists, and some calligraphers continue to practice in this style.

input: Lasers emitting in the red region of the spectrum have been available since the invention of the ruby laser in 1960. In 1962 the red helium–neon laser was invented, and these two types of lasers were widely used in many scientific applications including holography, and in education. Red helium–neon lasers were used commercially in LaserDisc players. The use of red laser diodes became widespread with the commercial success of modern DVD players, which use a 660 nm laser diode technology. Today, red and red-orange laser diodes are widely available to the public in the form of extremely inexpensive laser pointers. Portable, high-powered versions are also available for various applications. More recently, 671 nm diode-pumped solid state (DPSS) lasers have been introduced to the market for all-DPSS laser display systems, particle image velocimetry, Raman spectroscopy, and holography.
rewrite: Lasers operating within the red spectral region have been accessible since the initial development of the ruby laser in 1960. The subsequent invention of the red helium-neon laser in 1962 provided another source, with both types seeing extensive adoption in scientific and educational contexts, notably within holography. The helium-neon laser also found commercial application in LaserDisc players. Widespread utilization of red laser diodes commenced with the proliferation of modern DVD players, which employed 660 nm diode technology. Presently, red and red-orange laser diodes are commonly available as low-cost laser pointers, with higher-power portable variants existing for diverse uses. Most recently, 671 nm diode-pumped solid state (DPSS) lasers have been marketed for applications including all-DPSS display systems, particle image velocimetry, Raman spectroscopy, and holography.

input: Cities not served by road, sea, or river can be reached only by air, foot, dogsled, or snowmachine, accounting for Alaska's extremely well developed bush air services—an Alaskan novelty. Anchorage and, to a lesser extent Fairbanks, is served by many major airlines. Because of limited highway access, air travel remains the most efficient form of transportation in and out of the state. Anchorage recently completed extensive remodeling and construction at Ted Stevens Anchorage International Airport to help accommodate the upsurge in tourism (in 2012-2013, Alaska received almost 2 million visitors).
rewrite: Certain Alaskan communities, inaccessible by road, sea, or river, rely exclusively on air travel, foot, dogsled, or snowmachine. This necessity underpins the state's exceptionally developed bush air service network, a distinctive regional feature. While Anchorage and Fairbanks are hubs for major commercial airlines, limited highway infrastructure renders air transport the most efficient mode for statewide and external connectivity. In response to growing tourism, which drew nearly two million visitors in 2012-2013, Ted Stevens Anchorage International Airport has undergone significant renovation and expansion.

input: The islands enjoy a mild climate and varied soils, giving rise to a diverse pattern of vegetation. Animal and plant life is similar to that of the northwestern European continent. There are however, fewer numbers of species, with Ireland having even less. All native flora and fauna in Ireland is made up of species that migrated from elsewhere in Europe, and Great Britain in particular. The only window when this could have occurred was between the end of the last Ice Age (about 12,000 years ago) and when the land bridge connecting the two islands was flooded by sea (about 8,000 years ago).
rewrite: The islands possess a temperate climate and heterogeneous soils, which produce diverse vegetation patterns. Their flora and fauna broadly resemble those of northwestern continental Europe, albeit with fewer species; Ireland exhibits the most limited biodiversity. All indigenous Irish species originated through migration from other European regions, especially Great Britain. This colonization was only possible within the specific period following the last glacial maximum, approximately 12,000 years ago, and prior to the submergence of the terrestrial connection between the islands around 8,000 years ago.

input: Full-featured USB Type-C cables are active, electronically marked cables that contain a chip with an ID function based on the configuration data channel and vendor-defined messages (VDMs) from the USB Power Delivery 2.0 specification. USB Type-C devices also support power currents of 1.5 A and 3.0 A over the 5 V power bus in addition to baseline 900 mA; devices can either negotiate increased USB current through the configuration line, or they can support the full Power Delivery specification using both BMC-coded configuration line and legacy BFSK-coded VBUS line.
rewrite: Full-featured USB Type-C cables are active, electronically marked assemblies that incorporate an identification chip. This chip operates using the configuration data channel and vendor-defined messages as defined in the USB Power Delivery 2.0 specification. Furthermore, USB Type-C devices support power currents of 1.5 A and 3.0 A over the standard 5 V bus, exceeding the baseline 900 mA. Devices may negotiate this higher current via the configuration channel or implement the complete Power Delivery protocol, utilizing both the BMC-coded configuration line and the legacy BFSK-coded VBUS line.

input: AA gunnery was a difficult business. The problem was of successfully aiming a shell to burst close to its target's future position, with various factors affecting the shells' predicted trajectory. This was called deflection gun-laying, 'off-set' angles for range and elevation were set on the gunsight and updated as their target moved. In this method when the sights were on the target, the barrel was pointed at the target's future position. Range and height of the target determined fuse length. The difficulties increased as aircraft performance improved.
rewrite: Anti-aircraft gunnery presented significant challenges, primarily involving the accurate projection of a shell to detonate near a target's anticipated future location. This process, known as deflection gun-laying, required calculating and continuously adjusting offset angles for range and elevation on the gunsight. When the sights aligned on the target, the barrel was oriented toward its predicted position, with fuse length set by range and altitude. These complexities were exacerbated by advancing aircraft performance.

input: From the 18th century through late 20th century, the history of science, especially of the physical and biological sciences, was often presented in a progressive narrative in which true theories replaced false beliefs. More recent historical interpretations, such as those of Thomas Kuhn, tend to portray the history of science in different terms, such as that of competing paradigms or conceptual systems in a wider matrix that includes intellectual, cultural, economic and political themes outside of science.
rewrite: From the eighteenth to the late twentieth century, the history of science, particularly within the physical and biological disciplines, was frequently narrated as a progressive succession wherein correct theories supplanted erroneous ones. In contrast, more recent historiography, exemplified by the work of Thomas Kuhn, often characterizes scientific development through competing paradigms or conceptual frameworks. This approach situates science within a broader matrix incorporating intellectual, cultural, economic, and political factors.

input: Active solar techniques use photovoltaics, concentrated solar power, solar thermal collectors, pumps, and fans to convert sunlight into useful outputs. Passive solar techniques include selecting materials with favorable thermal properties, designing spaces that naturally circulate air, and referencing the position of a building to the Sun. Active solar technologies increase the supply of energy and are considered supply side technologies, while passive solar technologies reduce the need for alternate resources and are generally considered demand side technologies.
rewrite: Active solar methodologies employ technologies such as photovoltaics, concentrated solar power, solar thermal collectors, pumps, and fans to transform sunlight into functional energy outputs. In contrast, passive solar approaches involve selecting materials with advantageous thermal properties, designing for natural air circulation, and orienting structures relative to the sun. Consequently, active systems augment energy supply and are deemed supply-side technologies, whereas passive systems diminish reliance on alternative resources and are typically classified as demand-side technologies.

input: The ownership of the Spectre organisation—originally stylised "SPECTRE" as an acronym of SPecial Executive for Counter-intelligence, Terrorism, Revenge and Extortion—and its characters, had been at the centre of long-standing litigation starting in 1961 between Ian Fleming and Kevin McClory over the film rights to the novel Thunderball. The dispute began after Fleming incorporated elements of an undeveloped film script written by McClory and screenwriter Jack Whittingham—including characters and plot points—into Thunderball, which McClory contested in court, claiming ownership over elements of the novel. In 1963, Fleming settled out of court with McClory, in an agreement which awarded McClory the film rights. This enabled him to become a producer for the 1965 film Thunderball—with Albert R. Broccoli and Harry Saltzman as executive producers—and the non-Eon film Never Say Never Again, an updated remake of Thunderball, in 1983.[N 3] A second remake, entitled Warhead 2000 A.D., was planned for production and release in the 1990s before being abandoned. Under the terms of the 1963 settlement, the literary rights stayed with Fleming, allowing the Spectre organisation and associated characters to continue appearing in print.
rewrite: The ownership of the Spectre organization—originally stylized as the acronym "SPECTRE," denoting the SPecial Executive for Counter-intelligence, Terrorism, Revenge and Extortion—and its associated characters became the subject of protracted litigation commencing in 1961. This legal conflict arose between author Ian Fleming and filmmaker Kevin McClory concerning the cinematic rights to the novel *Thunderball*. The dispute originated when Fleming integrated narrative elements, including characters and plot details, from an unproduced film treatment authored by McClory and screenwriter Jack Whittingham into his novel. McClory initiated legal proceedings, asserting proprietary claims over these incorporated elements. A 1963 out-of-court settlement awarded McClory the film rights, thereby enabling his subsequent role as producer for the 1965 film *Thunderball*—with Albert R. Broccoli and Harry Saltzman serving as executive producers—and for the 1983 non-Eon production *Never Say Never Again*, an updated remake. A further proposed remake, *Warhead 2000 A.D.*, was ultimately abandoned during the 1990s. Crucially, the settlement permitted Fleming to retain the literary rights, thus allowing the Spectre organization and its characters to persist within the printed canon.

input: The quarrel of the Ancients and the Moderns was a literary and artistic quarrel that heated up in the early 1690s and shook the Académie française. The opposing two sides were, the Ancients (Anciens) who constrain choice of subjects to those drawn from the literature of Antiquity and the Moderns (Modernes), who supported the merits of the authors of the century of Louis XIV. Fontenelle quickly followed with his Digression sur les anciens et les modernes (1688), in which he took the Modern side, pressing the argument that modern scholarship allowed modern man to surpass the ancients in knowledge.
