rewrite: The Swan Inn at Woughton-on-the-Green in Buckinghamshire historically served as a base for the highwayman Dick Turpin. In a later period, the Spread Eagle in Thame, Berkshire, was managed during the 1920s by John Fothergill (1876–1957), who documented his experiences in *An Innkeeper's Diary* (1931). His tenure attracted numerous notable guests, including author H. G. Wells. The social significance of the public house was further illustrated in November 2003, when U.S. President George W. Bush, accompanied by British Prime Minister Tony Blair, visited the Dun Cow in Sedgefield, County Durham, fulfilling a wish to experience a traditional British pub; as a teetotaler, Bush consumed a non-alcoholic lager. By 2009, the United Kingdom contained approximately 53,500 public houses, a figure in steady annual decline. This trend has resulted in the loss of a local pub in nearly half of its smaller villages.

input: By 1840, the Market Hall and Sheds, where fresh meat and produce were brought daily, became a hub of commercial activity. The slave trade also depended on the port of Charleston, where ships could be unloaded and the slaves bought and sold. The legal importation of African slaves had ended in 1808, although smuggling was significant. However, the domestic trade was booming. More than one million slaves were transported from the Upper South to the Deep South in the antebellum years, as cotton plantations were widely developed through what became known as the Black Belt. Many slaves were transported in the coastwise slave trade, with slave ships stopping at ports such as Charleston.
rewrite: By 1840, the Market Hall and Sheds, operating as a daily venue for fresh meat and produce, had emerged as a central commercial hub. Concurrently, Charleston's port facilitated the slave trade, serving as a site for the disembarkation and sale of enslaved persons. Although the legal importation of African slaves ceased in 1808, illicit smuggling persisted. The domestic slave trade, however, expanded significantly. During the antebellum period, over one million enslaved individuals were forcibly relocated from the Upper South to the Deep South, a movement driven by the expansion of cotton plantations across the Black Belt. A substantial portion of this traffic occurred via the coastwise trade, with slave ships routinely docking at ports including Charleston.

input: Even though there is a broad scientific agreement that essentialist and typological conceptualizations of race are untenable, scientists around the world continue to conceptualize race in widely differing ways, some of which have essentialist implications. While some researchers sometimes use the concept of race to make distinctions among fuzzy sets of traits, others in the scientific community suggest that the idea of race often is used in a naive or simplistic way,[page needed] and argue that, among humans, race has no taxonomic significance by pointing out that all living humans belong to the same species, Homo sapiens, and subspecies, Homo sapiens sapiens.
rewrite: Despite a broad scientific consensus rejecting essentialist and typological views of race as biologically untenable, global scientific practice continues to exhibit significant divergence in conceptualizing race, with some approaches retaining essentialist undertones. Certain researchers employ racial categories to delineate broadly overlapping trait clusters, whereas others critique such usage as frequently simplistic or naive. These critics contend that race holds no taxonomic validity for humans, emphasizing that all living humans are members of a single species and subspecies: *Homo sapiens sapiens*.

input: In Evita (1996), Madonna played the title role of Eva Perón. For a long time, Madonna had desired to play Perón and wrote to director Alan Parker to explain why she would be perfect for the part. She said later, "This is the role I was born to play. I put everything of me into this because it was much more than a role in a movie. It was exhilarating and intimidating at the same time..... And I am prouder of Evita than anything else I have done." After securing the role, she had vocal training and learned about the history of Argentina and Perón. During shooting she became ill several times due to the intense emotional effort required. However, as she told Oprah, she was also pregnant during the filming: "I was winded after every take. I had to lie on the couch every ten minutes so I could recover from dizzy spells, I was worried that I was shaking the baby around too much and that would injure it in some way." Madonna wrote in her personal diary at the time: "Ironically, this feeling of vulnerability and weakness is helping me in the movie. I'm sure Evita felt this way every day of her life once she discovered she was ill."
rewrite: In the 1996 film *Evita*, Madonna assumed the titular role of Eva Perón. The performer had long aspired to portray Perón and proactively corresponded with director Alan Parker to articulate her suitability for the part. Reflecting subsequently, she asserted, “This is the role I was born to play. I put everything of me into this because it was much more than a role in a movie. It was exhilarating and intimidating at the same time…. And I am prouder of *Evita* than anything else I have done.” Upon securing the role, she undertook vocal training and engaged in study regarding Argentine history and Perón’s life. The production demanded considerable emotional exertion, resulting in several instances of illness during filming. Concurrently, Madonna was pregnant, a condition she disclosed to Oprah Winfrey, noting, “I was winded after every take. I had to lie on the couch every ten minutes so I could recover from dizzy spells; I was worried that I was shaking the baby around too much and that would injure it in some way.” In a personal diary entry from that period, she observed, “Ironically, this feeling of vulnerability and weakness is helping me in the movie. I’m sure Evita felt this way every day of her life once she discovered she was ill.”

input: Brass, which is an alloy of copper and zinc, has been used since at least the 10th century BC in Judea and by the 7th century BC in Ancient Greece. Zinc metal was not produced on a large scale until the 12th century in India and was unknown to Europe until the end of the 16th century. The mines of Rajasthan have given definite evidence of zinc production going back to the 6th century BC. To date, the oldest evidence of pure zinc comes from Zawar, in Rajasthan, as early as the 9th century AD when a distillation process was employed to make pure zinc. Alchemists burned zinc in air to form what they called "philosopher's wool" or "white snow".
rewrite: Brass, an alloy composed of copper and zinc, has been utilized since at least the tenth century BCE in Judea and by the seventh century BCE in Ancient Greece. However, metallic zinc was not produced on an industrial scale until the twelfth century in India and remained unknown in Europe until the late sixteenth century. Archaeological evidence from Rajasthan confirms zinc extraction dating to the sixth century BCE. The earliest known production of pure zinc originates from Zawar in Rajasthan, circa the ninth century CE, where a distillation technique was employed. Furthermore, alchemists historically burned zinc to create a substance termed "philosopher's wool" or "white snow."

input: In their theoretical rules, the Cubist architects expressed the requirement of dynamism, which would surmount the matter and calm contained in it, through a creative idea, so that the result would evoke feelings of dynamism and expressive plasticity in the viewer. This should be achieved by shapes derived from pyramids, cubes and prisms, by arrangements and compositions of oblique surfaces, mainly triangular, sculpted facades in protruding crystal-like units, reminiscent of the so-called diamond cut, or even cavernous that are reminiscent of the late Gothic architecture. In this way, the entire surfaces of the facades including even the gables and dormers are sculpted. The grilles as well as other architectural ornaments attain a three-dimensional form. Thus, new forms of windows and doors were also created, e. g. hexagonal windows. Czech Cubist architects also designed Cubist furniture.
rewrite: According to their theoretical principles, Cubist architects sought to convey dynamism, transcending the static nature of material through creative conception, thereby evoking sensations of kinetic energy and expressive plasticity in the observer. This was to be accomplished utilizing geometric forms such as pyramids, cubes, and prisms, along with arrangements of oblique, predominantly triangular planes. Facades were sculpted into protruding crystalline facets, akin to diamond cutting, or into cavernous forms reminiscent of late Gothic architecture. Consequently, all exterior surfaces, including gables and dormers, were treated sculpturally. Architectural elements like grilles and ornaments attained a three-dimensional quality. This approach also yielded novel window and door forms, such as hexagonal windows, and extended to the design of Cubist furniture by Czech architects.

input: Raleigh is also served by Triangle Transit (known formerly as the Triangle Transit Authority, or TTA). Triangle Transit offers scheduled, fixed-route regional and commuter bus service between Raleigh and the region's other principal cities of Durham, Cary and Chapel Hill, as well as to and from the Raleigh-Durham International Airport, Research Triangle Park and several of the region's larger suburban communities. Triangle Transit also coordinates an extensive vanpool and rideshare program that serves the region's larger employers and commute destinations.
rewrite: Raleigh is additionally served by Triangle Transit, previously designated the Triangle Transit Authority (TTA). This agency provides scheduled regional and commuter bus routes connecting Raleigh to Durham, Cary, Chapel Hill, Raleigh-Durham International Airport, Research Triangle Park, and major suburban areas. Furthermore, Triangle Transit administers a comprehensive vanpool and rideshare program, coordinating with the region's larger employers and primary commute destinations.

input: He invited a Roman Catholic priest, Father Anselm Strittmatter, O.S.B., to visit him for consultation. Von Neumann reportedly said in explanation that Pascal had a point, referring to Pascal's Wager. Father Strittmatter administered the last sacraments to him. Some of von Neumann's friends (such as Abraham Pais and Oskar Morgenstern) said they had always believed him to be "completely agnostic." "Of this deathbed conversion, Morgenstern told Heims, "He was of course completely agnostic all his life, and then he suddenly turned Catholic—it doesn't agree with anything whatsoever in his attitude, outlook and thinking when he was healthy." Father Strittmatter recalled that von Neumann did not receive much peace or comfort from it, as he still remained terrified of death.
rewrite: John von Neumann summoned the Roman Catholic priest Father Anselm Strittmatter, O.S.B., for consultation, reportedly invoking Pascal’s Wager as justification by stating that “Pascal had a point.” Father Strittmatter subsequently administered the last rites. This deathbed conversion surprised associates such as Abraham Pais and Oskar Morgenstern, who had consistently regarded von Neumann as entirely agnostic. Morgenstern later remarked to Heims that the conversion aligned with nothing in von Neumann’s prior attitudes or intellectual framework. According to Father Strittmatter’s account, the sacrament provided minimal solace, as von Neumann remained profoundly fearful of death.

input: A more elaborate form of urban AC is the rhythmic oldies format, which focuses primarily on "old school" R&B and soul hits from the 1960s to the 1990s, including Motown and disco hits. The format includes soul or disco artists such as ABBA, The Village People, The Jackson 5, Donna Summer, Tina Charles, Gloria Gaynor and the Bee Gees. Rhythmic oldies stations still exist today, but target African-Americans as opposed to a mass audience.
rewrite: A more sophisticated variant of urban adult contemporary radio is the rhythmic oldies format, which concentrates principally on "old school" R&B and soul music from the 1960s through the 1990s, encompassing Motown and disco genres. It features artists such as ABBA, The Village People, The Jackson 5, Donna Summer, Tina Charles, Gloria Gaynor, and the Bee Gees. While these stations persist, they now primarily target an African-American demographic rather than a broad, general audience.

input: His opponents learned from Napoleon's innovations. The increased importance of artillery after 1807 stemmed from his creation of a highly mobile artillery force, the growth in artillery numbers, and changes in artillery practices. As a result of these factors, Napoleon, rather than relying on infantry to wear away the enemy's defenses, now could use massed artillery as a spearhead to pound a break in the enemy's line that was then exploited by supporting infantry and cavalry. McConachy rejects the alternative theory that growing reliance on artillery by the French army beginning in 1807 was an outgrowth of the declining quality of the French infantry and, later, France's inferiority in cavalry numbers. Weapons and other kinds of military technology remained largely static through the Revolutionary and Napoleonic eras, but 18th-century operational mobility underwent significant change.
rewrite: Napoleon's adversaries adapted to his military innovations. Following 1807, artillery gained prominence due to his development of a highly mobile artillery corps, its numerical expansion, and shifts in tactical employment. Consequently, Napoleon could deploy concentrated artillery as a primary assault force to breach enemy lines, rather than depending solely on infantry to attritionally degrade defenses. These breaches were then exploited by coordinated infantry and cavalry. McConachy disputes the alternative thesis that increasing French artillery reliance from 1807 originated from deteriorating infantry quality or subsequent cavalry shortages. While weapons technology remained relatively static throughout the Revolutionary and Napoleonic periods, the operational mobility characteristic of the preceding century was substantially transformed.

input: Balansiyya had a rebirth of sorts with the beginning of the Taifa of Valencia kingdom in the 11th century. The town grew, and during the reign of Abd al-Aziz a new city wall was built, remains of which are preserved throughout the Old City (Ciutat Vella) today. The Castilian nobleman Rodrigo Diaz de Vivar, known as El Cid, who was intent on possessing his own principality on the Mediterranean, entered the province in command of a combined Christian and Moorish army and besieged the city beginning in 1092. By the time the siege ended in May 1094, he had carved out his own fiefdom—which he ruled from 15 June 1094 to July 1099. This victory was immortalised in the Lay of the Cid. During his rule, he converted nine mosques into churches and installed the French monk Jérôme as bishop of the See of Valencia. El Cid was killed in July 1099 while defending the city from an Almoravid siege, whereupon his wife Ximena Díaz ruled in his place for two years.
rewrite: The city of Balansiyya experienced a significant revival following the establishment of the Taifa kingdom of Valencia in the eleventh century. This period of growth, particularly under the rule of Abd al-Aziz, saw the construction of a new defensive wall, fragments of which endure within the contemporary Ciutat Vella. In 1092, the Castilian nobleman Rodrigo Díaz de Vivar, El Cid, entered the region leading a mixed Christian and Moorish force, initiating a siege with the aim of securing a Mediterranean principality. The city fell in May 1094, after which he governed his newly acquired territory until July 1099. His conquest is celebrated in the epic *Cantar de Mio Cid*. El Cid’s administration involved the consecration of nine mosques as churches and the appointment of the French cleric Jérôme as Bishop of Valencia. He perished in July 1099 defending the city from an Almoravid assault, after which his wife, Ximena Díaz, maintained control for a further two years.

input: A local pioneer of folk song collection in the first half of the 19th century was Shakespearean scholar James Orchard Halliwell, but it was not until the second folk revival in the 20th century that the full range of song from the county, including industrial folk song, began to gain attention. The county produced one of the major figures of the revival in Ewan MacColl, but also a local champion in Harry Boardman, who from 1965 onwards probably did more than anyone to popularise and record the folk song of the county. Perhaps the most influential folk artists to emerge from the region in the late 20th century were Liverpool folk group The Spinners, and from Manchester folk troubadour Roy Harper and musician, comedian and broadcaster Mike Harding. The region is home to numerous folk clubs, many of them catering to Irish and Scottish folk music. Regular folk festivals include the Fylde Folk Festival at Fleetwood.
rewrite: The systematic collection of folk songs in the region during the early nineteenth century was initiated by the Shakespearean scholar James Orchard Halliwell. However, comprehensive scholarly and popular attention to the county's full repertoire, including its industrial folk song tradition, only materialized during the second folk revival of the twentieth century. This period yielded significant figures, most notably the prominent revivalist Ewan MacColl. A dedicated local advocate, Harry Boardman, commencing in 1965, played an unparalleled role in popularizing and documenting the county's folk song heritage. The late twentieth century saw the emergence of highly influential artists from the region, such as the Liverpool group The Spinners and, from Manchester, the troubadour Roy Harper and the multifaceted performer Mike Harding. The area sustains numerous folk clubs, many specializing in Irish and Scottish traditions, and hosts regular festivals including the Fylde Folk Festival in Fleetwood.

input: The politics of Zhejiang is structured in a dual party-government system like all other governing institutions in Mainland China. The Governor of Zhejiang is the highest-ranking official in the People's Government of Zhejiang. However, in the province's dual party-government governing system, the Governor is subordinate to the Zhejiang Communist Party of China (CPC) Provincial Committee Secretary, colloquially termed the "Zhejiang CPC Party Chief".
rewrite: The political structure of Zhejiang operates within a dual party-government framework, consistent with governing institutions throughout mainland China. While the Governor serves as the highest-ranking official in the provincial People's Government, within this dual system the Governor is subordinate to the Secretary of the Zhejiang Provincial Committee of the Communist Party of China, commonly referred to as the provincial Party Chief.

input: In modern times, the Javanese are the largest ethnic group in Southeast Asia, with more than 100 million people, mostly concentrated in Java, Indonesia. In Burma, the Burmese account for more than two-thirds of the ethnic stock in this country, while ethnic Thais and Vietnamese account for about four-fifths of the respective populations of those countries. Indonesia is clearly dominated by the Javanese and Sundanese ethnic groups, while Malaysia is split between half Malays and one-quarter Chinese. Within the Philippines, the Tagalog, Cebuano, Ilocano, and Hiligaynon groups are significant.
rewrite: The Javanese constitute the largest ethnic group in Southeast Asia, numbering over 100 million and residing predominantly on the island of Java in Indonesia. In Burma, the Burmese comprise over two-thirds of the population, while ethnic Thais and Vietnamese constitute approximately four-fifths of their respective national populations. Indonesia is demographically dominated by the Javanese and Sundanese, whereas Malaysia's population is divided between ethnic Malays (roughly half) and Chinese (approximately one-quarter). Significant ethnic groups in the Philippines include the Tagalog, Cebuano, Ilocano, and Hiligaynon.

input: With the end of the war with Japan, the Chinese Civil War resumed between the Chinese Communists and the Chinese Nationalists. While the Communists were struggling for supremacy in Manchuria, they were supported by the North Korean government with matériel and manpower. According to Chinese sources, the North Koreans donated 2,000 railway cars worth of matériel while thousands of Koreans served in the Chinese People's Liberation Army (PLA) during the war. North Korea also provided the Chinese Communists in Manchuria with a safe refuge for non-combatants and communications with the rest of China.
rewrite: Following the conclusion of hostilities with Japan, the Chinese Civil War recommenced between the Communist and Nationalist factions. During the Communist campaign for control of Manchuria, the North Korean government provided substantial material and personnel support. Archival sources indicate this included a donation of matériel equivalent to 2,000 railway freight cars, alongside the service of thousands of Korean personnel within the People’s Liberation Army. Furthermore, North Korea afforded the Manchurian Communists a secure sanctuary for non-combatants and a vital communications link to other regions of China.

input: In vertebrates, the part of the brain that plays the greatest role is the hypothalamus, a small region at the base of the forebrain whose size does not reflect its complexity or the importance of its function. The hypothalamus is a collection of small nuclei, most of which are involved in basic biological functions. Some of these functions relate to arousal or to social interactions such as sexuality, aggression, or maternal behaviors; but many of them relate to homeostasis. Several hypothalamic nuclei receive input from sensors located in the lining of blood vessels, conveying information about temperature, sodium level, glucose level, blood oxygen level, and other parameters. These hypothalamic nuclei send output signals to motor areas that can generate actions to rectify deficiencies. Some of the outputs also go to the pituitary gland, a tiny gland attached to the brain directly underneath the hypothalamus. The pituitary gland secretes hormones into the bloodstream, where they circulate throughout the body and induce changes in cellular activity.
rewrite: Within vertebrate species, the hypothalamus, a diminutive region situated at the base of the forebrain, constitutes the most functionally significant cerebral component. Its limited physical dimensions belie both its intricate organization and its critical physiological role. This structure comprises an aggregation of small nuclei, the majority of which are integral to fundamental biological processes. While certain nuclei mediate arousal and social behaviors—including sexuality, aggression, and maternal responses—a principal function is the maintenance of homeostasis. Numerous hypothalamic nuclei integrate afferent signals from vascular sensors, which monitor parameters such as temperature, sodium concentration, glucose, and blood oxygen levels. In response, these nuclei generate efferent signals to motor areas, initiating corrective actions for any detected imbalances. Additional outputs are directed to the pituitary gland, a minute endocrine organ attached inferiorly to the hypothalamus. The pituitary releases hormones into systemic circulation, where they exert widespread modulatory effects on cellular activities throughout the organism.

input: In the 1940s, Detroit blues artist John Lee Hooker became a long-term resident in the city's southwest Delray neighborhood. Hooker, among other important blues musicians migrated from his home in Mississippi bringing the Delta blues to northern cities like Detroit. Hooker recorded for Fortune Records, the biggest pre-Motown blues/soul label. During the 1950s, the city became a center for jazz, with stars performing in the Black Bottom neighborhood. Prominent emerging Jazz musicians of the 1960s included: trumpet player Donald Byrd who attended Cass Tech and performed with Art Blakey and the Jazz Messengers early in his career and Saxophonist Pepper Adams who enjoyed a solo career and accompanied Byrd on several albums. The Graystone International Jazz Museum documents jazz in Detroit.
rewrite: During the 1940s, Detroit blues musician John Lee Hooker established a lasting residence in the city’s southwest Delray neighborhood. Like other significant blues artists, Hooker migrated from Mississippi, transplanting the Delta blues tradition to northern urban centers such as Detroit. He recorded for Fortune Records, the predominant blues and soul label prior to the rise of Motown. The 1950s saw Detroit emerge as a jazz hub, with notable performances occurring in the Black Bottom area. Prominent jazz figures of the 1960s included trumpeter Donald Byrd, a Cass Technical High School alumnus who performed early with Art Blakey and the Jazz Messengers, and saxophonist Pepper Adams, who maintained a solo career and collaborated with Byrd on multiple recordings. The Graystone International Jazz Museum archives this musical heritage.

input: Red hair varies from a deep burgundy through burnt orange to bright copper. It is characterized by high levels of the reddish pigment pheomelanin (which also accounts for the red color of the lips) and relatively low levels of the dark pigment eumelanin. The term redhead (originally redd hede) has been in use since at least 1510. Cultural reactions have varied from ridicule to admiration; many common stereotypes exist regarding redheads and they are often portrayed as fiery-tempered. (See red hair).
rewrite: Red hair encompasses a spectrum from deep burgundy to bright copper. This coloration results from elevated levels of the reddish pigment pheomelanin—also responsible for lip color—and comparatively low levels of the dark pigment eumelanin. The designation "redhead" dates to at least 1510. Cultural perceptions have ranged from ridicule to admiration, frequently accompanied by stereotypes, such as an association with a fiery temperament. (See red hair).

input: Several Islamic kingdoms (sultanates) under both foreign and, newly converted, Rajput rulers were established across the north western subcontinent (Afghanistan and Pakistan) over a period of a few centuries. From the 10th century, Sindh was ruled by the Rajput Soomra dynasty, and later, in the mid-13th century by the Rajput Samma dynasty. Additionally, Muslim trading communities flourished throughout coastal south India, particularly on the western coast where Muslim traders arrived in small numbers, mainly from the Arabian peninsula. This marked the introduction of a third Abrahamic Middle Eastern religion, following Judaism and Christianity, often in puritanical form. Mahmud of Ghazni in the early 11th century raided mainly the north-western parts of the Indian sub-continent 17 times, but he did not seek to establish "permanent dominion" in those areas.
rewrite: Over several centuries, a number of Islamic sultanates were established across the northwestern regions of the Indian subcontinent, encompassing parts of present-day Afghanistan and Pakistan. These polities were ruled by both foreign dynasties and newly Islamized Rajput lineages. From the 10th century, Sindh was governed by the Rajput Soomra dynasty, succeeded by the Samma dynasty in the mid-13th century. Concurrently, Muslim mercantile communities prospered in coastal South India, especially along the western seaboard, where traders primarily from the Arabian Peninsula arrived. This represented the introduction of Islam, the third Abrahamic faith from the Middle East, often in a puritanical form. Notably, Mahmud of Ghazni's seventeen early 11th-century expeditions targeted northwestern areas but did not aim for permanent territorial control.

input: The devotio was the most extreme offering a Roman general could make, promising to offer his own life in battle along with the enemy as an offering to the underworld gods. Livy offers a detailed account of the devotio carried out by Decius Mus; family tradition maintained that his son and grandson, all bearing the same name, also devoted themselves. Before the battle, Decius is granted a prescient dream that reveals his fate. When he offers sacrifice, the victim's liver appears "damaged where it refers to his own fortunes". Otherwise, the haruspex tells him, the sacrifice is entirely acceptable to the gods. In a prayer recorded by Livy, Decius commits himself and the enemy to the dii Manes and Tellus, charges alone and headlong into the enemy ranks, and is killed; his action cleanses the sacrificial offering. Had he failed to die, his sacrificial offering would have been tainted and therefore void, with possibly disastrous consequences. The act of devotio is a link between military ethics and those of the Roman gladiator.
rewrite: The ritual of *devotio* constituted the most extreme votive offering available to a Roman general, involving a pledge to surrender his own life in battle, along with the enemy, as a collective sacrifice to the chthonic deities. Livy provides a detailed narrative of the *devotio* performed by Decius Mus; familial tradition further asserted that his son and grandson, each bearing the identical name, subsequently performed the same rite. Prior to the engagement, Decius experiences a prescient dream foretelling his destiny. During the sacrificial preliminaries, the victim's liver is observed to be "flawed in the portion pertaining to his own fortunes." The haruspex nevertheless confirms the sacrifice is otherwise wholly acceptable to the gods. Through a prayer recorded by Livy, Decius consecrates both himself and the enemy to the *dii Manes* and Tellus, then deliberately charges alone into the enemy ranks to meet his death, thereby purifying the offering. Had he survived, the sacrifice would have been rendered ritually polluted and invalid, potentially incurring catastrophic repercussions. The practice of *devotio* thus establishes a conceptual connection between military and gladiatorial ethics in Roman culture.

input: A bare proton, H+, cannot exist in solution or in ionic crystals, because of its unstoppable attraction to other atoms or molecules with electrons. Except at the high temperatures associated with plasmas, such protons cannot be removed from the electron clouds of atoms and molecules, and will remain attached to them. However, the term 'proton' is sometimes used loosely and metaphorically to refer to positively charged or cationic hydrogen attached to other species in this fashion, and as such is denoted "H+" without any implication that any single protons exist freely as a species.
rewrite: The isolated proton, H+, cannot persist in solution or ionic crystals due to its potent attraction to any electron-donating atoms or molecules. Outside of high-temperature plasma conditions, protons remain bound within atomic or molecular electron clouds and cannot be extracted. Nevertheless, the term "proton" is often employed loosely and metaphorically to describe cationic hydrogen attached to other species. This usage, denoted as "H+," does not imply the actual existence of free, solitary protons.

input: The city's National Basketball Association teams are the Brooklyn Nets and the New York Knicks, while the New York Liberty is the city's Women's National Basketball Association. The first national college-level basketball championship, the National Invitation Tournament, was held in New York in 1938 and remains in the city. The city is well known for its links to basketball, which is played in nearly every park in the city by local youth, many of whom have gone on to play for major college programs and in the NBA.
rewrite: New York City hosts two National Basketball Association franchises, the Brooklyn Nets and the New York Knicks, alongside the Women's National Basketball Association's New York Liberty. The city also holds a foundational place in collegiate basketball history, having hosted the inaugural National Invitation Tournament in 1938, an event that remains there. Basketball is deeply embedded in the urban culture, with pervasive play in public parks fostering local talent that frequently advances to prominent university teams and the professional ranks.

input: Another who contributed significantly to the spirituality of the order is Albertus Magnus, the only person of the period to be given the appellation "Great". His influence on the brotherhood permeated nearly every aspect of Dominican life. Albert was a scientist, philosopher, astrologer, theologian, spiritual writer, ecumenist, and diplomat. Under the auspices of Humbert of Romans, Albert molded the curriculum of studies for all Dominican students, introduced Aristotle to the classroom and probed the work of Neoplatonists, such as Plotinus. Indeed, it was the thirty years of work done by Thomas Aquinas and himself (1245–1274) that allowed for the inclusion of Aristotelian study in the curriculum of Dominican schools.
rewrite: A further significant contributor to the order's spirituality was Albertus Magnus, the sole figure of his era accorded the honorific "Great." His influence permeated nearly all dimensions of Dominican life. A polymath—encompassing science, philosophy, astrology, theology, spiritual writing, ecumenism, and diplomacy—Albert, under the guidance of Humbert of Romans, fundamentally shaped the order's educational curriculum. He introduced Aristotelian philosophy into Dominican studies and engaged with Neoplatonist thinkers like Plotinus. The collaborative work of Albert and Thomas Aquinas from 1245 to 1274 was instrumental in securing a permanent place for Aristotelian thought within the Dominican scholastic tradition.

input: The competition formed as the FA Premier League on 20 February 1992 following the decision of clubs in the Football League First Division to break away from the Football League, which was originally founded in 1888, and take advantage of a lucrative television rights deal. The deal was worth £1 billion a year domestically as of 2013–14, with BSkyB and BT Group securing the domestic rights to broadcast 116 and 38 games respectively. The league generates €2.2 billion per year in domestic and international television rights. In 2014/15, teams were apportioned revenues of £1.6 billion.
rewrite: The FA Premier League was established on 20 February 1992 after First Division clubs elected to secede from the Football League, founded in 1888, to capitalize on a profitable television rights agreement. By the 2013–14 season, domestic rights were valued at approximately £1 billion annually, with BSkyB and BT Group broadcasting 116 and 38 matches respectively. Annual revenue from global television rights reaches €2.2 billion. For the 2014/15 season, clubs shared £1.6 billion in allocated revenues.

input: After the Seleucid defeat at the Battle of Magnesia in 190 BC, the kings of Sophene and Greater Armenia revolted and declared their independence, with Artaxias becoming the first king of the Artaxiad dynasty of Armenia in 188. During the reign of the Artaxiads, Armenia went through a period of hellenization. Numismatic evidence shows Greek artistic styles and the use of the Greek language. Some coins describe the Armenian kings as "Philhellenes". During the reign of Tigranes the Great (95–55 BC), the kingdom of Armenia reached its greatest extent, containing many Greek cities including the entire Syrian tetrapolis. Cleopatra, the wife of Tigranes the Great, invited Greeks such as the rhetor Amphicrates and the historian Metrodorus of Scepsis to the Armenian court, and - according to Plutarch - when the Roman general Lucullus seized the Armenian capital Tigranocerta, he found a troupe of Greek actors who had arrived to perform plays for Tigranes. Tigranes' successor Artavasdes II even composed Greek tragedies himself.
rewrite: Following the Seleucid defeat at the Battle of Magnesia in 190 BC, the rulers of Sophene and Greater Armenia rebelled, establishing independent kingdoms. Artaxias I, founding the Artaxiad dynasty in 188 BC, assumed the Armenian throne. The subsequent Artaxiad period was characterized by significant Hellenistic influence. Numismatic analysis reveals the adoption of Greek artistic conventions and language on royal coinage, with certain issues explicitly labeling Armenian monarchs as "Philhellenes." Under Tigranes the Great (95–55 BC), the Armenian kingdom attained its maximum territorial expanse, incorporating numerous Hellenistic cities, notably the entire Syrian Tetrapolis. His consort, Queen Cleopatra, is recorded as having invited Greek intellectuals, including the rhetorician Amphicrates and the historian Metrodorus of Scepsis, to the court. Plutarch further notes that during the Roman capture of Tigranocerta in 69 BC, Lucullus discovered a company of Greek actors awaiting a performance. This cultural engagement extended to Tigranes’ successor, Artavasdes II, who is reputed to have authored Greek tragedies.

input: While most artists became established in other formats before moving to adult contemporary, Michael Bublé and Josh Groban started out as AC artists. Throughout this decade, artists such as Nick Lachey, James Blunt, John Mayer, Bruno Mars, Jason Mraz, Kelly Clarkson, Adele, Clay Aiken and Susan Boyle have become successful thanks to a ballad heavy sound. Much as some hot AC and modern rock artists have crossed over into each other, so too has soft AC crossed with country music in this decade. Country musicians such as Faith Hill, Shania Twain, LeAnn Rimes and Carrie Underwood have had success on both charts.
rewrite: In contrast to the typical trajectory of artists establishing themselves in other genres prior to transitioning to adult contemporary (AC), Michael Bublé and Josh Groban emerged initially as AC artists. During this decade, numerous performers—including Nick Lachey, James Blunt, John Mayer, Bruno Mars, Jason Mraz, Kelly Clarkson, Adele, Clay Aiken, and Susan Boyle—achieved commercial success primarily through a ballad-centric repertoire. Furthermore, a notable crossover occurred between soft AC and country music, paralleling the interchange observed between hot AC and modern rock. Consequently, country artists such as Faith Hill, Shania Twain, LeAnn Rimes, and Carrie Underwood attained chart success within both formats.

input: Miami has one of the largest television markets in the nation and the second largest in the state of Florida. Miami has several major newspapers, the main and largest newspaper being The Miami Herald. El Nuevo Herald is the major and largest Spanish-language newspaper. The Miami Herald and El Nuevo Herald are Miami's and South Florida's main, major and largest newspapers. The papers left their longtime home in downtown Miami in 2013. The newspapers are now headquartered at the former home of U.S. Southern Command in Doral.
rewrite: Miami possesses one of the largest television markets in the United States and the second largest within Florida. Its principal newspapers are The Miami Herald and its Spanish-language counterpart, El Nuevo Herald, which together serve as the region's dominant print publications. In 2013, these newspapers relocated from their historic downtown Miami offices. Their current headquarters are now situated in Doral, occupying the former site of the U.S. Southern Command.

input: Former members Heather and Gary Botting compare the cultural paradigms of the religion to George Orwell's Nineteen Eighty-four, and Alan Rogerson describes the religion's leadership as totalitarian. Other critics charge that by disparaging individual decision-making, the religion's leaders cultivate a system of unquestioning obedience in which Witnesses abrogate all responsibility and rights over their personal lives. Critics also accuse the religion's leaders of exercising "intellectual dominance" over Witnesses, controlling information and creating "mental isolation", which former Governing Body member Raymond Franz argued were all elements of mind control.
rewrite: Scholars Heather and Gary Botting liken the religion's cultural paradigms to the dystopian society depicted in George Orwell's *Nineteen Eighty-four*, while Alan Rogerson characterizes its leadership as totalitarian. Critics further contend that by devaluing individual judgment, the leadership fosters a system of uncritical compliance, wherein adherents surrender autonomy over their personal lives. Additional accusations include the exertion of "intellectual dominance" through information control, creating a state of "mental isolation" that former Governing Body member Raymond Franz identified as components of mind control.

input:
The movie industry was born in Paris when Auguste and Louis Lumière projected the first motion picture for a paying audience at the Grand Café on 28 December 1895. Many of Paris' concert/dance halls were transformed into movie theatres when the media became popular beginning in the 1930s. Later, most of the largest cinemas were divided into multiple, smaller rooms. Paris' largest cinema room today is in Le Grand Rex theatre with 2,700 seats.
Big multiplex movie theaters have been built since the 1990s. UGC Ciné Cité Les Halles with 27 screens, MK2 Bibliothèque with 20 screens and UGC Ciné Cité Bercy with 18 screens are among the largest.
rewrite: The cinematic industry originated in Paris with the Lumière brothers' inaugural public screening of a motion picture at the Grand Café on December 28, 1895. As the medium gained popularity from the 1930s onward, numerous Parisian music and dance halls were converted into cinemas. Subsequently, many large-scale venues were subdivided into smaller auditoria. Presently, the city's largest single screen, seating 2,700, is located in Le Grand Rex. Since the 1990s, expansive multiplexes have been constructed, including major complexes such as UGC Ciné Cité Les Halles (27 screens), MK2 Bibliothèque (20 screens), and UGC Ciné Cité Bercy (18 screens).

input: Since the 1988 Education Reform Act, parents have a right to choose which school their child should go to or whether to not send them to school at all and to home educate them instead. The concept of "school choice" introduces the idea of competition between state schools, a fundamental change to the original "neighbourhood comprehensive" model, and is partly intended as a means by which schools that are perceived to be inferior are forced either to improve or, if hardly anyone wants to go there, to close down. Government policy is currently promoting 'specialisation' whereby parents choose a secondary school appropriate for their child's interests and skills. Most initiatives focus on parental choice and information, implementing a pseudo-market incentive to encourage better schools. This logic has underpinned the controversial league tables of school performance.
rewrite: Since the enactment of the 1988 Education Reform Act, parents have been granted the right to select their child's school or to opt for home education. This policy of "school choice" introduces competitive dynamics among state schools, representing a significant departure from the traditional neighbourhood comprehensive model. A key objective is to compel underperforming institutions to either enhance their standards or face closure due to insufficient enrolment. Contemporary government policy further emphasises 'specialisation,' encouraging the selection of secondary schools based on a child's aptitudes and interests. These initiatives predominantly centre on expanding parental choice and access to information, thereby establishing a quasi-market mechanism intended to incentivise school improvement. This rationale has also provided the foundation for the contentious publication of school performance league tables.

input: The Partyja BPF (Belarusian Popular Front) was established in 1988 as a political party and cultural movement for democracy and independence, à la the Baltic republics’ popular fronts. The discovery of mass graves in Kurapaty outside Minsk by historian Zianon Pazniak, the Belarusian Popular Front’s first leader, gave additional momentum to the pro-democracy and pro-independence movement in Belarus. It claimed that the NKVD performed secret killings in Kurapaty. Initially the Front had significant visibility because its numerous public actions almost always ended in clashes with the police and the KGB.
rewrite: Founded in 1988, the Partyja BPF (Belarusian Popular Front) emerged as both a political party and a cultural movement advocating for democracy and national independence, modeled on analogous popular fronts in the Baltic republics. Its pro-democracy campaign gained substantial impetus from the discovery of Kurapaty mass graves near Minsk by historian Zianon Pazniak, the Front's inaugural leader, who attributed the secret executions to the NKVD. The movement initially maintained high visibility through frequent public demonstrations, which typically culminated in confrontations with police and KGB forces.

input: Plymouth is home to Plymouth Argyle F.C., who play in the fourth tier of English football league known as Football League Two. The team's home ground is called Home Park and is located in Central Park. It links itself with the group of English non-conformists that left Plymouth for the New World in 1620: its nickname is "The Pilgrims". The city also has four Non-League football clubs; Plymouth Parkway F.C. who play at Bolitho Park, Elburton Villa F.C. who play at Haye Road, Vospers Oak Villa F.C. who play at Weston Mill and Plymstock United F.C. who play at Deans Cross. All four clubs play in the South West Peninsula League.
rewrite: The city of Plymouth is the home of Plymouth Argyle Football Club, which competes in Football League Two, the fourth tier of the English football league system. The club plays its home matches at Home Park, situated within Central Park. Reflecting the city's historical association with the group of English non-conformists who departed for the New World in 1620, the club bears the nickname "The Pilgrims." Additionally, Plymouth hosts four Non-League football clubs: Plymouth Parkway F.C. (Bolitho Park), Elburton Villa F.C. (Haye Road), Vospers Oak Villa F.C. (Weston Mill), and Plymstock United F.C. (Deans Cross). All four compete within the South West Peninsula League.

input: The Appalachian belt includes, with the ranges enumerated above, the plateaus sloping southward to the Atlantic Ocean in New England, and south-eastward to the border of the coastal plain through the central and southern Atlantic states; and on the north-west, the Allegheny and Cumberland plateaus declining toward the Great Lakes and the interior plains. A remarkable feature of the belt is the longitudinal chain of broad valleys, including The Great Appalachian Valley, which in the southerly sections divides the mountain system into two unequal portions, but in the northernmost lies west of all the ranges possessing typical Appalachian features, and separates them from the Adirondack group. The mountain system has no axis of dominating altitudes, but in every portion the summits rise to rather uniform heights, and, especially in the central section, the various ridges and intermontane valleys have the same trend as the system itself. None of the summits reaches the region of perpetual snow.
rewrite: The Appalachian belt encompasses not only the aforementioned ranges but also the plateaus that descend southward toward the Atlantic Ocean in New England, and southeastward to the coastal plain boundary through the central and southern Atlantic states. To the northwest, it includes the Allegheny and Cumberland plateaus, which slope toward the Great Lakes and the interior plains. A distinctive characteristic of this belt is its longitudinal series of broad valleys, most notably the Great Appalachian Valley. In southern sections, this valley divides the mountain system into two unequal parts, while in the far north it lies west of all ranges with typical Appalachian traits, thereby separating them from the Adirondack group. The system lacks a dominant axial crest of peak elevations; instead, summit heights are relatively consistent throughout. Particularly in the central region, the ridges and intermontane valleys align with the overall trend of the system. No summit attains an elevation sufficient for permanent snow cover.

input: In a speech before the Organization of American States in November 2013, Kerry remarked that the era of the Monroe Doctrine was over. He went on to explain, "The relationship that we seek and that we have worked hard to foster is not about a United States declaration about how and when it will intervene in the affairs of other American states. It's about all of our countries viewing one another as equals, sharing responsibilities, cooperating on security issues, and adhering not to doctrine, but to the decisions that we make as partners to advance the values and the interests that we share."
rewrite: In a November 2013 address to the Organization of American States, Secretary of State John Kerry declared the conclusion of the Monroe Doctrine era. He elaborated that the policy the United States seeks to cultivate is not defined by unilateral declarations regarding intervention. Instead, it is founded upon a collective vision of hemispheric relations as a partnership of equals. This framework emphasizes shared responsibility, cooperative security, and adherence to joint decisions made to advance common values and interests, moving beyond doctrinal unilateralism.

input: There is a strong relationship between the properties of wood and the properties of the particular tree that yielded it. The density of wood varies with species. The density of a wood correlates with its strength (mechanical properties). For example, mahogany is a medium-dense hardwood that is excellent for fine furniture crafting, whereas balsa is light, making it useful for model building. One of the densest woods is black ironwood.
rewrite: A significant correlation exists between the physical properties of wood and those of its source tree. Wood density, which varies by species, is directly correlated with its mechanical strength. For instance, mahogany, a medium-density hardwood, is well-suited for fine furniture, while lightweight balsa is ideal for model construction. Among the densest woods is black ironwood, exemplifying this relationship between density and material characteristics.

input: The hypnotic electronic dance song "On and On", produced in 1984 by Chicago DJ Jesse Saunders and co-written by Vince Lawrence, had elements that became staples of the early house sound, such as the Roland TB-303 bass synthesizer and minimal vocals as well as a Roland (specifically TR-808) drum machine and Korg (specifically Poly-61) synthesizer. It also utilized the bassline from Player One's disco record "Space Invaders" (1979). "On and On" is sometimes cited as the 'first house record', though other examples from around that time, such as J.M. Silk's "Music is the Key" (1985), have also been cited.
rewrite: Released in 1984, the hypnotic electronic dance track "On and On," produced by Chicago DJ Jesse Saunders and co-written by Vince Lawrence, incorporated foundational elements of the early house genre. These included the Roland TB-303 bass synthesizer, a Roland TR-808 drum machine, a Korg Poly-61 synthesizer, and minimal vocals. The composition also integrated the bassline from Player One's 1979 disco record "Space Invaders." While frequently cited as the inaugural house record, contemporaneous works like J.M. Silk's "Music is the Key" (1985) also hold this distinction.

input: Rufinus relates a story that as Bishop Alexander stood by a window, he watched boys playing on the seashore below, imitating the ritual of Christian baptism. He sent for the children and discovered that one of the boys (Athanasius) had acted as bishop. After questioning Athanasius, Bishop Alexander informed him that the baptisms were genuine, as both the form and matter of the sacrament had been performed through the recitation of the correct words and the administration of water, and that he must not continue to do this as those baptized had not been properly catechized. He invited Athanasius and his playfellows to prepare for clerical careers.
rewrite: According to Rufinus, Bishop Alexander observed from his window a group of boys on the shore imitating Christian baptism. Upon summoning them, he learned one child, Athanasius, had performed the role of bishop. After interrogation, Alexander declared the baptisms valid, as the requisite form (the correct words) and matter (water) of the sacrament were present. However, he admonished Athanasius to cease, noting the recipients lacked proper catechesis. Subsequently, Alexander invited Athanasius and his companions to undertake formal preparation for ecclesiastical vocations.

input: Tensions between John and the barons had been growing for several years, as demonstrated by the 1212 plot against the king. Many of the disaffected barons came from the north of England; that faction was often labelled by contemporaries and historians as "the Northerners". The northern barons rarely had any personal stake in the conflict in France, and many of them owed large sums of money to John; the revolt has been characterised as "a rebellion of the king's debtors". Many of John's military household joined the rebels, particularly amongst those that John had appointed to administrative roles across England; their local links and loyalties outweighed their personal loyalty to John. Tension also grew across North Wales, where opposition to the 1211 treaty between John and Llywelyn was turning into open conflict. For some the appointment of Peter des Roches as justiciar was an important factor, as he was considered an "abrasive foreigner" by many of the barons. The failure of John's French military campaign in 1214 was probably the final straw that precipitated the baronial uprising during John's final years as king; James Holt describes the path to civil war as "direct, short and unavoidable" following the defeat at Bouvines.
rewrite: Tensions between King John and the baronial class escalated over several years, as evidenced by the conspiracy against him in 1212. A significant contingent of these disaffected barons originated from northern England, a faction commonly designated by both contemporary observers and subsequent historians as "the Northerners." These northern barons frequently possessed little personal interest in the ongoing conflict in France, and a substantial number were heavily indebted to the crown; consequently, the revolt has been characterized as a rebellion of the king's debtors. Notably, many members of John's own military household defected to the rebel cause, particularly those appointed to administrative posts throughout the realm, whose regional affiliations ultimately superseded their personal allegiance to the monarch. Concurrently, unrest intensified in North Wales, where resistance to the 1211 treaty between John and Llywelyn ap Iorwerth escalated into open warfare. For certain barons, the appointment of Peter des Roches as justiciar proved a further provocation, as he was widely perceived as an abrasive foreigner. The failure of John's military campaign in France during 1214 likely served as the decisive catalyst for the baronial uprising in the king's final years. As historian James Holt concludes, following the defeat at Bouvines, the path to civil war became "direct, short and unavoidable."

input: Incandescent light bulbs come in a range of shapes and sizes. The names of the shapes may be slightly different in some regions. Many of these shapes have a designation consisting of one or more letters followed by one or more numbers, e.g. A55 or PAR38. The letters represent the shape of the bulb. The numbers represent the maximum diameter, either in 1⁄8 of an inch, or in millimeters, depending on the shape and the region. For example, 63 mm reflectors are designated R63, but in the US, they are known as R20 (2.5 in). However, in both regions, a PAR38 reflector is known as PAR38.
rewrite: Incandescent light bulbs are produced in various shapes and sizes, with nomenclature that can vary regionally. Many shapes are identified by a code comprising one or more letters followed by numbers, such as A55 or PAR38. The letters indicate the bulb's shape, while the numbers denote the maximum diameter. This measurement is expressed either in eighths of an inch or in millimeters, contingent upon the specific shape and geographic market. For instance, a 63 mm reflector is labeled R63 in many areas but as R20 in the United States. Notably, the designation PAR38 remains consistent across both regions.

input: Between October 14–16, 1964, Leonid Brezhnev and a small cadre of high-ranking Communist Party officials, deposed Khrushchev as Soviet government leader a day after Voskhod 1 landed, in what was called the "Wednesday conspiracy". The new political leaders, along with Korolev, ended the technologically troublesome Voskhod program, cancelling Voskhod 3 and 4, which were in the planning stages, and started concentrating on the race to the Moon. Voskhod 2 would end up being Korolev's final achievement before his death on January 14, 1966, as it would become the last of the many space firsts that demonstrated the USSR's domination in spacecraft technology during the early 1960s. According to historian Asif Siddiqi, Korolev's accomplishments marked "the absolute zenith of the Soviet space program, one never, ever attained since." There would be a two-year pause in Soviet piloted space flights while Voskhod's replacement, the Soyuz spacecraft, was designed and developed.
rewrite: Between October 14 and 16, 1964, Leonid Brezhnev and a select group of senior Communist Party officials removed Nikita Khrushchev from leadership in an event subsequently termed the "Wednesday conspiracy," occurring shortly after the Voskhod 1 mission. The incoming leadership, in consultation with chief designer Sergei Korolev, terminated the technically problematic Voskhod program. Planned missions Voskhod 3 and 4 were cancelled to refocus efforts on the lunar race. Voskhod 2, which included the first spacewalk, proved to be Korolev's final success before his death in January 1966, representing the last in a series of pioneering Soviet space achievements that demonstrated technological dominance in the early 1960s. Historian Asif Siddiqi identifies this period as "the absolute zenith of the Soviet space program." A subsequent two-year hiatus in crewed flights ensued during the development of the Soyuz spacecraft, intended to succeed Voskhod.

input: In comparison to the other regions of Spain, the major economic benefit of Galicia is its fishing Industry. Galicia is a land of economic contrast. While the western coast, with its major population centers and its fishing and manufacturing industries, is prosperous and increasing in population, the rural hinterland — the provinces of Ourense and Lugo — is economically dependent on traditional agriculture, based on small landholdings called minifundios. However, the rise of tourism, sustainable forestry and organic and traditional agriculture are bringing other possibilities to the Galician economy without compromising the preservation of the natural resources and the local culture.
rewrite: Galicia’s economy is distinguished within Spain by its reliance on the fishing industry. The region exhibits significant internal contrasts: the populous western coast, centered on fishing and manufacturing, is prosperous and growing, whereas the rural interior—comprising Ourense and Lugo—remains dependent on traditional agriculture organized around smallholdings, or *minifundios*. Emerging sectors such as tourism, sustainable forestry, and organic farming are now diversifying the economic base, offering development that aligns with the conservation of natural resources and local cultural heritage.

input: Florida's nickname is the "Sunshine State", but severe weather is a common occurrence in the state. Central Florida is known as the lightning capital of the United States, as it experiences more lightning strikes than anywhere else in the country. Florida has one of the highest average precipitation levels of any state, in large part because afternoon thunderstorms are common in much of the state from late spring until early autumn. A narrow eastern part of the state including Orlando and Jacksonville receives between 2,400 and 2,800 hours of sunshine annually. The rest of the state, including Miami, receives between 2,800 and 3,200 hours annually.
rewrite: Despite its designation as the "Sunshine State," Florida is frequently subject to severe weather. Central Florida, recognized as the national lightning capital, sustains more lightning strikes than any other U.S. region. The state also records among the highest average precipitation levels nationally, attributable to prevalent afternoon thunderstorms from late spring through early autumn. Annually, a narrow eastern zone encompassing Orlando and Jacksonville receives 2,400 to 2,800 hours of sunshine. The remainder of the state, including Miami, experiences a higher range of 2,800 to 3,200 hours.

input: By the 1860s the Kingdom of Prussia and the Austrian Empire were the two most powerful nations dominated by German-speaking elites. Both sought to expand their influence and territory. The Austrian Empire – like the Holy Roman Empire – was a multi-ethnic state, but German-speaking people there did not have an absolute numerical majority; the creation of the Austro-Hungarian Empire was one result of the growing nationalism of other ethnicities especially the Hungarians. Prussia under Otto von Bismarck would ride on the coat-tails of nationalism to unite all of modern-day Germany. The German Empire ("Second Reich") was created in 1871 following the proclamation of Wilhelm I as head of a union of German-speaking states, while disregarding millions of its non-German subjects who desired self-determination from German rule.
rewrite: By the 1860s, the German-speaking elites of the Kingdom of Prussia and the Austrian Empire presided over the two most powerful German states, each pursuing territorial and political expansion. The Austrian Empire, a multi-ethnic polity akin to its predecessor the Holy Roman Empire, lacked an absolute German demographic majority; rising nationalist sentiments among other ethnicities, notably the Hungarians, subsequently contributed to the formation of the Austro-Hungarian Empire. Conversely, Prussia, directed by Otto von Bismarck, strategically harnessed nationalist fervor to unify modern Germany. The resultant German Empire, or "Second Reich," was proclaimed in 1871 under Kaiser Wilhelm I. This unification explicitly consolidated German-speaking states while simultaneously excluding and subjugating millions of non-German subjects who sought self-determination.

input: The Atlantic coast of the United States is low, with minor exceptions. The Appalachian Highland owes its oblique northeast-southwest trend to crustal deformations which in very early geological time gave a beginning to what later came to be the Appalachian mountain system. This system had its climax of deformation so long ago (probably in Permian time) that it has since then been very generally reduced to moderate or low relief. It owes its present-day altitude either to renewed elevations along the earlier lines or to the survival of the most resistant rocks as residual mountains. The oblique trend of this coast would be even more pronounced but for a comparatively modern crustal movement, causing a depression in the northeast resulting in an encroachment of the sea upon the land. Additionally, the southeastern section has undergone an elevation resulting in the advance of the land upon the sea.
rewrite: The Atlantic coastline of the United States is predominantly low-lying, with few significant deviations. The Appalachian Highland exhibits an oblique northeast-southwest orientation, a trend established by ancient crustal deformations that initiated the formation of the Appalachian system. This mountain system reached its primary orogenic climax in the distant geologic past, likely during the Permian period, and has subsequently been eroded to a state of moderate or low relief. Its contemporary elevation is attributable either to renewed uplift along pre-existing structural lines or to the persistence of the most resilient rock formations as residual mountains. The oblique coastal trend would be more pronounced were it not for relatively recent tectonic activity. This includes subsidence in the northeastern region, leading to marine transgression, and uplift in the southeastern section, resulting in progradation of the land.

input: Each of these four dialects was associated with an independent kingdom on the island. Of these, Northumbria south of the Tyne, and most of Mercia, were overrun by the Vikings during the 9th century. The portion of Mercia that was successfully defended, and all of Kent, were then integrated into Wessex under Alfred the Great. From that time on, the West Saxon dialect (then in the form now known as Early West Saxon) became standardised as the language of government, and as the basis for the many works of literature and religious materials produced or translated from Latin in that period.
rewrite: Each of these four dialects corresponded to a distinct kingdom on the island. During the ninth century, the regions of Northumbria south of the Tyne and much of Mercia were conquered by Viking forces. The remaining defended portion of Mercia, along with all of Kent, were subsequently incorporated into the kingdom of Wessex under Alfred the Great. Consequently, the West Saxon dialect, specifically in its Early West Saxon form, was standardized for administrative use. It also served as the foundational language for the numerous literary and religious works composed or translated from Latin during this era.

input: Noted 19th-century mosaics include those by Edward Burne-Jones at St Pauls within the Walls in Rome. Another modern mosaic of note is the world's largest mosaic installation located at the Cathedral Basilica of St. Louis, located in St. Louis, Missouri. A modern example of mosaic is the Museum of Natural History station of the New York City Subway (there are many such works of art scattered throughout the New York City subway system, though many IND stations are usually designed with bland mosaics.) Another example of mosaics in ordinary surroundings is the use of locally themed mosaics in some restrooms in the rest areas along some Texas interstate highways.
rewrite: Prominent nineteenth-century mosaics include those designed by Edward Burne-Jones for St. Paul's Within the Walls in Rome. A significant modern installation, the world's largest, adorns the Cathedral Basilica of St. Louis in Missouri. Contemporary applications also feature in public infrastructure, such as the art-filled stations of the New York City Subway, exemplified by the Museum of Natural History stop, though many IND stations employ more utilitarian designs. Similarly, regionally themed mosaics appear in mundane settings like rest area facilities along certain Texas interstate highways.

input: British Somaliland became independent on 26 June 1960 as the State of Somaliland, and the Trust Territory of Somalia (the former Italian Somaliland) followed suit five days later. On 1 July 1960, the two territories united to form the Somali Republic, albeit within boundaries drawn up by Italy and Britain. A government was formed by Abdullahi Issa Mohamud and Muhammad Haji Ibrahim Egal other members of the trusteeship and protectorate governments, with Haji Bashir Ismail Yusuf as President of the Somali National Assembly, Aden Abdullah Osman Daar as the President of the Somali Republic and Abdirashid Ali Shermarke as Prime Minister (later to become President from 1967 to 1969). On 20 July 1961 and through a popular referendum, the people of Somalia ratified a new constitution, which was first drafted in 1960. In 1967, Muhammad Haji Ibrahim Egal became Prime Minister, a position to which he was appointed by Shermarke. Egal would later become the President of the autonomous Somaliland region in northwestern Somalia.
rewrite: On 26 June 1960, British Somaliland attained independence as the State of Somaliland. This was followed, five days later, by the independence of the Trust Territory of Somalia, formerly Italian Somaliland. The two territories unified on 1 July 1960 to establish the Somali Republic, though within borders originally demarcated by the Italian and British colonial administrations. An inaugural government was formed, incorporating members from both predecessor administrations. Key leadership positions included Haji Bashir Ismail Yusuf as President of the Somali National Assembly, Aden Abdullah Osman Daar as President of the Republic, and Abdirashid Ali Shermarke as Prime Minister. A new constitution, initially drafted in 1960, was ratified by popular referendum on 20 July 1961. Shermarke, who later served as President from 1967 to 1969, appointed Muhammad Haji Ibrahim Egal as Prime Minister in 1967. Egal would subsequently assume the presidency of the autonomous Somaliland region in northwestern Somalia.

input: Feathers are a feature characteristic of birds (though also present in some dinosaurs not currently considered to be true birds). They facilitate flight, provide insulation that aids in thermoregulation, and are used in display, camouflage, and signaling. There are several types of feathers, each serving its own set of purposes. Feathers are epidermal growths attached to the skin and arise only in specific tracts of skin called pterylae. The distribution pattern of these feather tracts (pterylosis) is used in taxonomy and systematics. The arrangement and appearance of feathers on the body, called plumage, may vary within species by age, social status, and sex.
rewrite: Feathers represent a defining trait of birds, also present in certain non-avian dinosaurs. These complex epidermal structures, which grow from specific skin tracts known as pterylae, serve multiple functions. These include enabling flight, providing insulation for thermoregulation, and facilitating display, camouflage, and signaling. The pattern of these tracts, termed pterylosis, is taxonomically significant. Furthermore, the overall arrangement and appearance of feathers, or plumage, can vary within a species according to age, sex, and social status.

input: Once the elevator arrives at the floor, it will park with its doors open and the car buttons will be disabled to prevent a passenger from taking control of the elevator. Medical personnel must then activate the code-blue key switch inside the car, select their floor and close the doors with the door close button. The elevator will then travel non-stop to the selected floor, and will remain in code-blue service until switched off in the car. Some hospital elevators will feature a 'hold' position on the code-blue key switch (similar to fire service) which allows the elevator to remain at a floor locked out of service until code blue is deactivated.
rewrite: Upon arrival at the designated floor, the elevator will park with open doors and deactivate its interior controls to prevent passenger operation. Medical staff must then engage the code-blue key switch within the car, select the desired floor, and initiate door closure via the dedicated button. The elevator will subsequently travel directly to that floor without interruption, maintaining code-blue priority until the switch is disengaged internally. Certain hospital elevator systems include a 'hold' function on the key switch, analogous to fire service operation, which retains the elevator at a floor and out of general service until the code-blue status is terminated.

input: Myanmar's armed forces are known as the Tatmadaw, which numbers 488,000. The Tatmadaw comprises the Army, the Navy, and the Air Force. The country ranked twelfth in the world for its number of active troops in service. The military is very influential in Myanmar, with all top cabinet and ministry posts usually held by military officials. Official figures for military spending are not available. Estimates vary widely because of uncertain exchange rates, but Myanmar's military forces' expenses are high. Myanmar imports most of its weapons from Russia, Ukraine, China and India.
rewrite: The Myanmar Armed Forces, known as the Tatmadaw, maintain an active personnel strength of approximately 488,000 across its Army, Navy, and Air Force, ranking twelfth globally. The institution holds considerable political influence, with senior cabinet and ministerial positions typically occupied by military officials. While official defense expenditure data is unavailable, estimates indicate substantial spending, complicated by volatile currency exchange rates. Myanmar's primary sources for arms imports are Russia, Ukraine, China, and India.

input: The Anglo-French hostilities were ended in 1763 by the Treaty of Paris, which involved a complex series of land exchanges, the most important being France's cession to Spain of Louisiana, and to Great Britain the rest of New France except for the islands of St. Pierre and Miquelon. Faced with the choice of retrieving either New France or its Caribbean island colonies of Guadeloupe and Martinique, France chose the latter to retain these lucrative sources of sugar, writing off New France as an unproductive, costly territory. France also returned Minorca to the British. Spain lost control of Florida to Great Britain, but it received from the French the Île d'Orléans and all of the former French holdings west of the Mississippi River. The exchanges suited the British as well, as their own Caribbean islands already supplied ample sugar, and, with the acquisition of New France and Florida, they now controlled all of North America east of the Mississippi.
rewrite: The Anglo-French conflict was formally concluded in 1763 with the Treaty of Paris. This agreement entailed a multifaceted territorial reorganization, most notably France's cession of Louisiana to Spain and of the remainder of New France (excluding St. Pierre and Miquelon) to Great Britain. Confronted with the option of regaining either New France or its valuable Caribbean sugar colonies, Guadeloupe and Martinique, France prioritized the latter for their economic profitability, effectively abandoning New France as a burdensome and unremunerative possession. France additionally restored Minorca to British control. While Spain relinquished Florida to Great Britain, it acquired from France the Île d'Orléans and all former French territories west of the Mississippi River. These arrangements aligned with British interests, as their existing Caribbean holdings provided sufficient sugar, and the gains of New France and Florida secured their dominance over all North American territories east of the Mississippi.

input: The city had surrendered without a fight to the invading Moors (Berbers and Arabs) by 714 AD, and the cathedral of Saint Vincent was turned into a mosque. Abd al-Rahman I, the first emir of Cordoba, ordered the city destroyed in 755 during his wars against other nobility, but several years later his son, Abdullah, had a form of autonomous rule over the province of Valencia. Among his administrative acts he ordered the building of a luxurious palace, the Russafa, on the outskirts of the city in the neighbourhood of the same name. So far no remains have been found. Also at this time Valencia received the name Medina al-Turab (City of Sand). When Islamic culture settled in, Valencia, then called Balansiyya, prospered from the 10th century, due to a booming trade in paper, silk, leather, ceramics, glass and silver-work. The architectural legacy of this period is abundant in Valencia and can still be appreciated today in the remnants of the old walls, the Baños del Almirante bath house, Portal de Valldigna street and even the Cathedral and the tower, El Micalet (El Miguelete), which was the minaret of the old mosque.
rewrite: By 714 AD, the city had capitulated without resistance to the invading Moorish forces, comprising Berbers and Arabs, leading to the conversion of the Cathedral of Saint Vincent into a mosque. In 755, during his conflicts with rival nobility, Abd al-Rahman I, the first Emir of Córdoba, commanded the city's destruction. However, several years later, his son Abdullah established a degree of autonomous governance over the province of Valencia. Among his administrative initiatives was the construction of a luxurious palace, the Russafa, located on the city's outskirts within the identically named district; to date, no archaeological remains of this structure have been discovered. During this era, Valencia also acquired the name Medina al-Turab (City of Sand). As Islamic culture became entrenched, the city, then known as Balansiyya, entered a period of prosperity from the 10th century onward, fueled by a flourishing trade in paper, silk, leather, ceramics, glass, and silverwork. The architectural legacy from this Islamic period remains abundant in Valencia, evident in surviving segments of the old city walls, the Baños del Almirante bathhouse, Portal de Valldigna street, and even integrated into later structures such as the Cathedral and its tower, El Micalet (El Miguelete), which originated as the minaret of the former mosque.

input: Whereas SCIMs cannot turn a shaft faster than allowed by the power line frequency, universal motors can run at much higher speeds. This makes them useful for appliances such as blenders, vacuum cleaners, and hair dryers where high speed and light weight are desirable. They are also commonly used in portable power tools, such as drills, sanders, circular and jig saws, where the motor's characteristics work well. Many vacuum cleaner and weed trimmer motors exceed 10,000 rpm, while many similar miniature grinders exceed 30,000 rpm.
rewrite: Unlike single-phase induction motors (SCIMs), which are limited by line frequency, universal motors can achieve substantially higher rotational speeds. This capability renders them suitable for applications demanding high speed and low weight, including household appliances such as blenders, vacuum cleaners, and hair dryers. They are also prevalent in portable power tools like drills and saws. Speeds often exceed 10,000 rpm in vacuum cleaners and can surpass 30,000 rpm in miniature grinders.

input: To counter the trend towards low-density suburban residential growth, the government began a series of controversial public housing projects in the inner city by the Housing Commission of Victoria, which resulted in demolition of many neighbourhoods and a proliferation of high-rise towers.
