Two of these, a car ferry service and a fast catamaran passenger ferry service, provide links to East Cowes and Cowes respectively on the Isle of Wight and are operated by Red Funnel. The third ferry is the Hythe Ferry, providing a passenger service to Hythe on the other side of Southampton Water.
rewrite: Although Southampton no longer serves as a departure point for cross-channel ferries, it remains the terminus for three domestic ferry services, all operating from Town Quay. Two services, a car ferry and a fast passenger catamaran, connect to East Cowes and Cowes on the Isle of Wight, operated by Red Funnel. The third is the Hythe Ferry, a passenger service to Hythe across Southampton Water.

input: On release, Twilight Princess was considered to be the greatest Zelda game ever made by many critics including writers for 1UP.com, Computer and Video Games, Electronic Gaming Monthly, Game Informer, GamesRadar, IGN and The Washington Post. Game Informer called it "so creative that it rivals the best that Hollywood has to offer". GamesRadar praised Twilight Princess as "a game that deserves nothing but the absolute highest recommendation". Cubed3 hailed Twilight Princess as "the single greatest videogame experience". Twilight Princess's graphics were praised for the art style and animation, although the game was designed for the GameCube, which is technically lacking compared to the next generation consoles. Both IGN and GameSpy pointed out the existence of blurry textures and low-resolution characters. Despite these complaints, Computer and Video Games felt the game's atmosphere was superior to that of any previous Zelda game, and regarded Twilight Princess's Hyrule as the best version ever created. PALGN praised the game's cinematics, noting that "the cutscenes are the best ever in Zelda games". Regarding the Wii version, GameSpot's Jeff Gerstmann said the Wii controls felt "tacked-on", although 1UP.com said the remote-swinging sword attacks were "the most impressive in the entire series". Gaming Nexus considered Twilight Princess's soundtrack to be the best of this generation, though IGN criticized its MIDI-formatted songs for lacking "the punch and crispness" of their orchestrated counterparts. Hyper's Javier Glickman commended the game for its "very long quests, superb Wii controls and being able to save anytime". However, he criticised it for "no voice acting, no orchestral score and slightly outdated graphics".
rewrite:
Upon its initial release, *The Legend of Zelda: Twilight Princess* was widely acclaimed by critics as the pinnacle of the franchise. Numerous publications, including 1UP.com, *Computer and Video Games*, *Electronic Gaming Monthly*, *Game Informer*, GamesRadar, IGN, and *The Washington Post*, lauded the title. *Game Informer* described its creativity as rivaling "the best that Hollywood has to offer," while GamesRadar offered it "the absolute highest recommendation." Cubed3 declared it "the single greatest videogame experience." The game's art style and animation were frequently praised, though reviewers acknowledged technical limitations stemming from its original GameCube design, with IGN and GameSpy noting blurry textures and low-resolution character models.

Nevertheless, *Computer and Video Games* contended that the game's atmospheric depth surpassed all prior series entries, considering its rendition of Hyrule the finest to date. PALGN highlighted the cinematics, asserting the cutscenes were "the best ever in Zelda games." Assessments of the Wii port were mixed; GameSpot's Jeff Gerstmann found its motion controls "tacked-on," whereas 1UP.com celebrated the remote-swinging sword attacks as "the most impressive in the entire series." Critical opinion on the audio was also divided. Gaming Nexus deemed the soundtrack the best of its generation, yet IGN criticized the MIDI-formatted songs for lacking "the punch and crispness" of a full orchestra. Hyper's Javier Glickman commended the lengthy quests, refined Wii controls, and flexible save system, but cited the absence of voice acting, an orchestral score, and somewhat dated graphics as notable shortcomings.

input: Some multiracial individuals feel marginalized by U.S. society. For example, when applying to schools or for a job, or when taking standardized tests, Americans are sometimes asked to check boxes corresponding to race or ethnicity. Typically, about five race choices are given, with the instruction to "check only one." While some surveys offer an "other" box, this choice groups together individuals of many different multiracial types (ex: European Americans/African-Americans are grouped with Asian/Native American Indians).
rewrite: Certain multiracial individuals experience marginalization within U.S. societal structures, particularly during institutional processes such as educational admissions, employment applications, or standardized testing. These contexts often require selecting a single racial or ethnic category from a limited set, typically around five options. Although some instruments include an "other" designation, it aggregates diverse multiracial backgrounds—for instance, combining European American/African American heritage with Asian/Native American Indian ancestry—into a single, undifferentiated group.

input: One of the central problems in the anthropology of art concerns the universality of 'art' as a cultural phenomenon. Several anthropologists have noted that the Western categories of 'painting', 'sculpture', or 'literature', conceived as independent artistic activities, do not exist, or exist in a significantly different form, in most non-Western contexts. To surmount this difficulty, anthropologists of art have focused on formal features in objects which, without exclusively being 'artistic', have certain evident 'aesthetic' qualities. Boas' Primitive Art, Claude Lévi-Strauss' The Way of the Masks (1982) or Geertz's 'Art as Cultural System' (1983) are some examples in this trend to transform the anthropology of 'art' into an anthropology of culturally specific 'aesthetics'.
rewrite: A principal challenge within the anthropology of art involves the question of whether 'art' constitutes a universal cultural category. Scholars have observed that Western classifications such as 'painting' or 'sculpture,' understood as autonomous artistic domains, are either absent or manifest in markedly different forms across numerous non-Western societies. To address this analytical impasse, the discipline has shifted focus toward examining formal properties of objects that, while not exclusively artistic, possess discernible aesthetic attributes. Foundational works, including Boas’s *Primitive Art*, Lévi-Strauss’s *The Way of the Masks* (1982), and Geertz’s “Art as Cultural System” (1983), exemplify this trajectory, which reorients the field from an anthropology of 'art' to an anthropology of culturally situated aesthetics.

input: Presbyterianism first officially arrived in Colonial America in 1703 with the establishment of the first Presbytery in Philadelphia. In time, the presbytery would be joined by two more to form a synod (1717) and would eventually evolve into the Presbyterian Church in the United States of America in 1789. The nation's largest Presbyterian denomination, the Presbyterian Church (U.S.A.) – PC (USA) – can trace their heritage back to the original PCUSA, as can the Presbyterian Church in America (PCA), the Orthodox Presbyterian Church (OPC), the Bible Presbyterian Church (BPC), the Cumberland Presbyterian Church (CPC), the Cumberland Presbyterian Church in America the Evangelical Presbyterian Church (EPC) and the Evangelical Covenant Order of Presbyterians (ECO).
rewrite: Presbyterianism was formally established in Colonial America in 1703 with the founding of the first Presbytery in Philadelphia. This initial body was later joined by two additional presbyteries to constitute a synod in 1717, which ultimately developed into the Presbyterian Church in the United States of America (PCUSA) in 1789. The lineage of this original denomination extends to several major contemporary bodies. These include the largest, the Presbyterian Church (U.S.A.), as well as the Presbyterian Church in America, the Orthodox Presbyterian Church, the Bible Presbyterian Church, the Cumberland Presbyterian Church, the Cumberland Presbyterian Church in America, the Evangelical Presbyterian Church, and the Evangelical Covenant Order of Presbyterians.

input: In London Chopin took lodgings at Dover Street, where the firm of Broadwood provided him with a grand piano. At his first engagement, on 15 May at Stafford House, the audience included Queen Victoria and Prince Albert. The Prince, who was himself a talented musician, moved close to the keyboard to view Chopin's technique. Broadwood also arranged concerts for him; among those attending were Thackeray and the singer Jenny Lind. Chopin was also sought after for piano lessons, for which he charged the high fee of one guinea (£1.05 in present British currency) per hour, and for private recitals for which the fee was 20 guineas. At a concert on 7 July he shared the platform with Viardot, who sang arrangements of some of his mazurkas to Spanish texts.
rewrite: Upon his arrival in London, Frédéric Chopin secured accommodations on Dover Street, where the Broadwood firm supplied him with a grand piano. His inaugural performance occurred on 15 May at Stafford House, attended by Queen Victoria and Prince Albert. The Prince, a skilled musician in his own right, positioned himself near the keyboard to observe Chopin’s technique closely. Broadwood further facilitated concerts for the composer, with notable attendees including William Thackeray and the soprano Jenny Lind. Chopin was also in high demand for piano instruction, commanding a substantial fee of one guinea per hour, and for private recitals, for which he charged twenty guineas. At a subsequent concert on 7 July, he performed alongside Pauline Viardot, who sang adaptations of his mazurkas set to Spanish texts.

input: The materialist view is perhaps best understood in its opposition to the doctrines of immaterial substance applied to the mind historically, famously by René Descartes. However, by itself materialism says nothing about how material substance should be characterized. In practice, it is frequently assimilated to one variety of physicalism or another.
rewrite: Materialism is best defined in contrast to historical doctrines of immaterial mental substance, notably Cartesian dualism. Yet, materialism itself does not specify the nature of material substance and is often equated with one form of physicalism or another.

input: Sony's PlayStation 3 has extensive HD compatibility because of its built in Blu-ray disc based player, so does Microsoft's Xbox 360 with the addition of Netflix and Windows Media Center HTPC streaming capabilities, and the Zune marketplace where users can rent or purchase digital HD content. Recently, Nintendo released a next generation high definition gaming platform, The Wii U, which includes TV remote control features in addition to IPTV streaming features like Netflix. The HD capabilities of the consoles has influenced some developers to port games from past consoles onto the PS3, Xbox 360 and Wii U, often with remastered or upscaled graphics.
rewrite: The PlayStation 3 offers extensive high-definition compatibility through its integrated Blu-ray player. Similarly, the Xbox 360 provides HD functionality via Netflix, Windows Media Center streaming, and the Zune marketplace for digital content. Nintendo's subsequent high-definition platform, the Wii U, incorporates IPTV services such as Netflix alongside television control features. These consolidated HD capabilities have prompted developers to port and visually enhance titles from prior console generations for release on the PS3, Xbox 360, and Wii U.

input: Between 1892, when Harvard and Yale met in one of the first intercollegiate debates, and 1909, the year of the first Triangular Debate of Harvard, Yale, and Princeton, the rhetoric, symbolism, and metaphors used in athletics were used to frame these early debates. Debates were covered on front pages of college newspapers and emphasized in yearbooks, and team members even received the equivalent of athletic letters for their jackets. There even were rallies sending off the debating teams to matches. Yet, the debates never attained the broad appeal that athletics enjoyed. One reason may be that debates do not have a clear winner, as is the case in sports, and that scoring is subjective. In addition, with late 19th-century concerns about the impact of modern life on the human body, athletics offered hope that neither the individual nor the society was coming apart.
rewrite: Between 1892, when Harvard and Yale participated in an early intercollegiate debate, and 1909, which marked the inaugural Triangular Debate among Harvard, Yale, and Princeton, the language and imagery of athletics were employed to structure these forensic contests. Debates received prominent coverage on the front pages of college newspapers and in yearbooks, while team members were awarded letters analogous to those given to athletes. Rallies were even held to send the debating teams to competitions. Despite this parallel treatment, debates failed to achieve the widespread popularity of athletics. This disparity may be attributed, in part, to the absence of a definitive, objectively scored winner in debate, unlike in sporting events. Furthermore, within the late nineteenth-century context of anxieties regarding modernity’s impact on the human body, athletics provided a narrative of physical and social cohesion that intellectual competition could not match.

input: In towns, which expanded greatly during the period, landowners turned into property developers, and rows of identical terraced houses became the norm. Even the wealthy were persuaded to live in these in town, especially if provided with a square of garden in front of the house. There was an enormous amount of building in the period, all over the English-speaking world, and the standards of construction were generally high. Where they have not been demolished, large numbers of Georgian buildings have survived two centuries or more, and they still form large parts of the core of cities such as London, Edinburgh, Dublin and Bristol.
rewrite: During the era of significant urban expansion, landowners transitioned into property developers, establishing rows of uniform terraced housing as the standard. Even affluent residents were encouraged to reside in such townhouses, particularly when afforded a small garden square. This period witnessed extensive construction across the Anglophone world, characterized by generally high building standards. Consequently, where not demolished, a substantial quantity of Georgian structures has endured for over two centuries, continuing to constitute major segments of the urban cores in cities including London, Edinburgh, Dublin, and Bristol.

input: The offices of elder and ministerial servant were restored to Witness congregations in 1972, with appointments made from headquarters (and later, also by branch committees). It was announced that, starting in September 2014, appointments would be made by traveling overseers. In a major organizational overhaul in 1976, the power of the Watch Tower Society president was diminished, with authority for doctrinal and organizational decisions passed to the Governing Body. Since Knorr's death in 1977, the position of president has been occupied by Frederick Franz (1977–1992) and Milton Henschel (1992–2000), both members of the Governing Body, and since 2000 by Don A. Adams, not a member of the Governing Body. In 1995, Jehovah's Witnesses abandoned the idea that Armageddon must occur during the lives of the generation that was alive in 1914 and in 2013 changed their teaching on the "generation".
rewrite: In 1972, the offices of elder and ministerial servant were reinstated within Witness congregations, with appointments initially issued from headquarters and subsequently also by branch committees. It was later declared that, commencing in September 2014, such appointments would be made by traveling overseers. A significant restructuring in 1976 reduced the authority of the Watch Tower Society president, transferring doctrinal and organizational decision-making power to the Governing Body. Following Nathan Knorr's death in 1977, the presidency was held by Governing Body members Frederick Franz (1977–1992) and Milton Henschel (1992–2000). Since 2000, the role has been occupied by Don A. Adams, who is not a Governing Body member. Doctrinally, in 1995, Jehovah's Witnesses discontinued the teaching that Armageddon must transpire within the lifespan of the generation alive in 1914, revising this concept of the "generation" again in 2013.

input: Compared to children, adolescents are more likely to question others' assertions, and less likely to accept facts as absolute truths. Through experience outside the family circle, they learn that rules they were taught as absolute are in fact relativistic. They begin to differentiate between rules instituted out of common sense—not touching a hot stove—and those that are based on culturally-relative standards (codes of etiquette, not dating until a certain age), a delineation that younger children do not make. This can lead to a period of questioning authority in all domains.
rewrite: Adolescents exhibit a greater propensity than children to critically evaluate assertions and are less inclined to accept information as unequivocally true. Exposure to contexts beyond the family unit reveals that many rules presented as absolute are instead relativistic. They develop the capacity to distinguish between norms grounded in universal pragmatism, such as avoiding physical harm, and those derived from culturally specific conventions, like etiquette or courtship customs—a distinction typically absent in younger children. This cognitive shift often precipitates a broader phase of challenging authority across various domains.

input: Different cultures have evolved various ways of creating clothes out of cloth. One approach simply involves draping the cloth. Many people wore, and still wear, garments consisting of rectangles of cloth wrapped to fit – for example, the dhoti for men and the sari for women in the Indian subcontinent, the Scottish kilt or the Javanese sarong. The clothes may simply be tied up, as is the case of the first two garments; or pins or belts hold the garments in place, as in the case of the latter two. The precious cloth remains uncut, and people of various sizes or the same person at different sizes can wear the garment.
rewrite: Various cultures have developed distinct methods of garment construction from woven textiles. One fundamental technique involves the direct draping of uncut cloth. This practice remains prevalent in garments such as the Indian dhoti and sari, the Scottish kilt, and the Javanese sarong, each formed by wrapping rectangular fabric panels to conform to the body. These draped garments are secured either through knotting and tucking or with the aid of fasteners like pins and belts. This approach conserves the textile intact, allowing for adjustable wearability across different body sizes and over time for a single individual.

input: The biggest change in this year's census was in racial classification. Enumerators were instructed to no longer use the "Mulatto" classification. Instead, they were given special instructions for reporting the race of interracial persons. A person with both white and black ancestry (termed "blood") was to be recorded as "Negro," no matter the fraction of that lineage (the "one-drop rule"). A person of mixed black and American Indian ancestry was also to be recorded as "Neg" (for "Negro") unless he was considered to be "predominantly" American Indian and accepted as such within the community. A person with both White and American Indian ancestry was to be recorded as an Indian, unless his American Indian ancestry was small, and he was accepted as white within the community. In all situations in which a person had White and some other racial ancestry, he was to be reported as that other race. Persons who had minority interracial ancestry were to be reported as the race of their father.
rewrite: The most significant modification in the current year’s census pertained to racial categorization. Enumerators received directives to discontinue use of the “Mulatto” classification. Specific protocols were instituted for recording the race of individuals of mixed ancestry. Individuals with both White and Black ancestry, described in the instructions as sharing “blood,” were to be designated as “Negro,” irrespective of the proportional lineage—an application of the “one-drop rule.” Those of mixed Black and American Indian ancestry were similarly to be recorded as “Neg” (for “Negro”), unless deemed predominantly American Indian and accepted as such within their community. For persons of White and American Indian ancestry, the designation was to be Indian, except in cases where the American Indian lineage was minimal and the individual was socially accepted as White. In all instances involving White and any other racial ancestry, the individual was to be reported as that other race. For persons with mixed ancestry not involving White, the racial designation of the father was to be recorded.

input: When it comes to civil and criminal cases, the Bundesgerichtshof is at the top of the hierarchy of courts. The other branches of the German judicial system each have their own appellate systems, each topped by a high court; these are the Bundessozialgericht for matters of social security, the Bundesarbeitsgericht for employment and labour, the Bundesfinanzhof for taxation and financial issues, and the Bundesverwaltungsgericht for administrative law. The so-called Gemeinsamer Senat der Obersten Gerichtshöfe (Joint Senate of the Supreme Courts) is not a supreme court in itself, but an ad-hoc body that is convened in only when one supreme court intends to diverge from another supreme court's legal opinion or when a certain case exceeds the authority of one court. As the courts have well-defined areas of responsibility, situations like these are rather rare and so, the Joint Senate gathers very infrequently, and only to consider matters which are mostly definitory.
rewrite: The Bundesgerichtshof occupies the apex of the judicial hierarchy for civil and criminal matters in Germany. The remaining specialized branches of the judiciary possess independent appellate structures, each culminating in a respective high court: the Bundessozialgericht for social security law, the Bundesarbeitsgericht for labor and employment law, the Bundesfinanzhof for tax and financial law, and the Bundesverwaltungsgericht for administrative law. The Gemeinsamer Senat der Obersten Gerichtshöfe (Joint Senate of the Supreme Courts) does not constitute a separate supreme court, but rather an ad-hoc body. It is convened exclusively when one supreme court intends to depart from the legal doctrine of another, or when a case transcends the jurisdictional boundaries of a single court. Given the courts' precisely delineated domains, such circumstances are uncommon. Consequently, the Joint Senate assembles infrequently and solely to adjudicate primarily definitional matters.

input: The modern Standard Chinese exonym for the ethnic Tibetan region is Zangqu (Chinese: 藏区; pinyin: Zàngqū), which derives by metonymy from the Tsang region around Shigatse plus the addition of a Chinese suffix, 区 qū, which means "area, district, region, ward". Tibetan people, language, and culture, regardless of where they are from, are referred to as Zang (Chinese: 藏; pinyin: Zàng) although the geographical term Xīzàng is often limited to the Tibet Autonomous Region. The term Xīzàng was coined during the Qing dynasty in the reign of the Jiaqing Emperor (1796–1820) through the addition of a prefix meaning "west" (西 xī) to Zang.
rewrite: The contemporary Standard Chinese exonym for the ethnically Tibetan region is Zangqu (藏区; Zàngqū). This term originates metonymically from the Tsang area surrounding Shigatse, combined with the Chinese suffix *qū* (区), denoting an administrative district or region. The ethnonym Zang (藏; Zàng) refers comprehensively to Tibetan people, language, and culture. In contrast, the geographical designation Xīzàng (西藏), meaning "Western Zang," is frequently applied specifically to the Tibet Autonomous Region. This latter term was formulated during the Qing dynasty under the Jiaqing Emperor (1796–1820) by prefixing Zang with *xī* (西), signifying "west."

input: The Christian population of the empire, owing to their higher educational levels, started to pull ahead of the Muslim majority, leading to much resentment on the part of the latter. In 1861, there were 571 primary and 94 secondary schools for Ottoman Christians with 140,000 pupils in total, a figure that vastly exceeded the number of Muslim children in school at the same time, who were further hindered by the amount of time spent learning Arabic and Islamic theology. In turn, the higher educational levels of the Christians allowed them to play a large role in the economy. In 1911, of the 654 wholesale companies in Istanbul, 528 were owned by ethnic Greeks. Of course, it would be a mistake to ignore the geopolitical dimensions of this dynamic. The preponderance of Christian merchants owed not to any innate business sense on their part, although plenty of European observers were keen on making this point. In fact, in many cases, Christians and also Jews were able to gain protection from European consuls and citizenship, meaning they were protected from Ottoman law and not subject to the same economic regulations as their Muslim comrades.
rewrite: The elevated educational attainment among the Christian subjects of the Ottoman Empire facilitated their socioeconomic advancement relative to the Muslim majority, engendering significant resentment. By 1861, Ottoman Christians were served by 571 primary and 94 secondary schools, collectively educating approximately 140,000 pupils. This figure substantially surpassed the number of Muslim students, whose educational progress was further impeded by curricular requirements in Arabic and Islamic theology. Consequently, the Christians' superior education translated into pronounced economic influence. For instance, in 1911, ethnic Greeks owned 528 of the 654 wholesale companies in Istanbul. However, attributing this commercial preponderance to an innate Christian aptitude for business, as some contemporary European commentators did, is erroneous. A critical geopolitical factor was the ability of many Christians, and also Jews, to secure foreign protection through European consuls or citizenship. This status exempted them from Ottoman jurisprudence and various economic regulations that continued to bind their Muslim counterparts, thereby conferring a significant competitive advantage.

input: The direct object of the verb appears either in the accusative (for total objects) or in the partitive (for partial objects). The accusative coincides with the genitive in the singular and with nominative in the plural. Accusative vs. partitive case opposition of the object used with transitive verbs creates a telicity contrast, just as in Finnish. This is a rough equivalent of the perfective vs. imperfective aspect opposition.
rewrite: The direct object of a verb is marked either by the accusative case, indicating a total object, or by the partitive case, denoting a partial object. The accusative form aligns with the genitive in the singular and the nominative in the plural. This accusative-partitive opposition with transitive verbs generates a telicity contrast, analogous to Finnish, roughly corresponding to a perfective-imperfective aspect distinction.

input: Wove paper does not exhibit "laidlines", which are small regular lines left behind on paper when it was handmade in a mould made from rows of metal wires or bamboo. Laidlines are very close together. They run perpendicular to the "chainlines", which are further apart. Handmade paper similarly exhibits "deckle edges", or rough and feathery borders.
rewrite: Wove paper lacks the closely spaced "laidlines" found in handmade paper, which are formed by parallel wires in the mould and run perpendicular to the wider "chainlines." Unlike laid paper, it also does not display the characteristic rough, feathery "deckle edges" of handmade sheets.

input: Iranian scientists outside Iran have also made some major contributions to science. In 1960, Ali Javan co-invented the first gas laser, and fuzzy set theory was introduced by Lotfi Zadeh. Iranian cardiologist, Tofy Mussivand invented and developed the first artificial cardiac pump, the precursor of the artificial heart. Furthering research and treatment of diabetes, HbA1c was discovered by Samuel Rahbar. Iranian physics is especially strong in string theory, with many papers being published in Iran. Iranian-American string theorist Kamran Vafa proposed the Vafa-Witten theorem together with Edward Witten. In August 2014, Maryam Mirzakhani became the first-ever woman, as well as the first-ever Iranian, to receive the Fields Medal, the highest prize in mathematics.
rewrite: Iranian scientists abroad have made significant contributions to global science. In 1960, Ali Javan co-invented the first gas laser, while Lotfi Zadeh introduced fuzzy set theory. The pioneering artificial cardiac pump, a precursor to the artificial heart, was invented and developed by cardiologist Tofy Mussivand. Samuel Rahbar advanced diabetes research through his discovery of HbA1c. Theoretical physics, particularly string theory, is notably robust within Iran, as evidenced by substantial domestic publication. Iranian-American string theorist Kamran Vafa co-proposed the Vafa-Witten theorem with Edward Witten. In 2014, Maryam Mirzakhani became the first woman and first Iranian to receive the Fields Medal, mathematics' highest honor.

input: The only cosmetic difference between an RLV disc and a regular factory-pressed LaserDiscs is their reflective purple-violet (or blue with some RLV discs) color resulting from the dye embedded in the reflective layer of the disc to make it recordable, as opposed to the silver mirror appearance of regular LDs. The purplish color of RLVs is very similar to DVD-R and DVD+R discs. RLVs were popular for making short-run quantities of LaserDiscs for specialized applications such as interactive kiosks and flight simulators.
rewrite: The sole cosmetic distinction between a Recordable LaserVision (RLV) disc and a standard factory-pressed LaserDisc is its reflective purple-violet or blue hue. This results from a dye within the reflective layer enabling recordability, contrasting with the silver mirror finish of conventional discs. The coloration closely resembles that of DVD-R and DVD+R media. RLVs were commonly employed for producing limited quantities of LaserDiscs for specialized uses, including interactive kiosks and flight simulators.

input: It was imperative for Japanese commanders to hold Saipan. The only way to do this was to destroy the U.S. Fifth Fleet, which had 15 fleet carriers and 956 planes, 7 battleships, 28 submarines, and 69 destroyers, as well as several light and heavy cruisers. Vice Admiral Jisaburo Ozawa attacked with nine-tenths of Japan's fighting fleet, which included nine carriers with 473 planes, 5 battleships, several cruisers, and 28 destroyers. Ozawa's pilots were outnumbered 2:1 and their aircraft were becoming or were already obsolete. The Japanese had considerable antiaircraft defenses but lacked proximity fuzes or good radar. With the odds against him, Ozawa devised an appropriate strategy. His planes had greater range because they were not weighed down with protective armor; they could attack at about 480 km (300 mi)[citation needed], and could search a radius of 900 km[citation needed] (560 mi). U.S. Navy Hellcat fighters could only attack within 200 miles (320 km) and only search within a 325-mile (523 km)[citation needed] radius. Ozawa planned to use this advantage by positioning his fleet 300 miles (480 km)[citation needed] out. The Japanese planes would hit the U.S. carriers, land at Guam to refuel, then hit the enemy again when returning to their carriers. Ozawa also counted on about 500 land-based planes at Guam and other islands.
rewrite:
For Japanese military leadership, the retention of Saipan was an imperative strategic objective. This necessitated the destruction of the opposing U.S. Fifth Fleet, a formidable force comprising fifteen fleet carriers with 956 aircraft, seven battleships, twenty-eight submarines, sixty-nine destroyers, and numerous cruisers. Vice Admiral Jisaburo Ozawa committed approximately ninety percent of Japan’s operational naval strength to this engagement, including nine carriers with 473 aircraft, five battleships, several cruisers, and twenty-eight destroyers. Despite this commitment, Ozawa’s forces faced significant disadvantages: his aviators were outnumbered two-to-one, and their aircraft were largely obsolete. While Japanese vessels possessed considerable antiaircraft artillery, they lacked proximity fuzes and effective radar systems.

Confronted with these asymmetries, Ozawa formulated a strategy predicated on the superior operational range of his carrier aircraft, which, unburdened by protective armor, could strike at approximately 480 kilometers and conduct searches within a 900-kilometer radius. This contrasted with the U.S. Navy’s Hellcat fighters, which were limited to a combat radius of roughly 320 kilometers and a search radius of approximately 523 kilometers. Ozawa intended to exploit this advantage by positioning his fleet beyond 480 kilometers from the American task forces. His aircraft would attack U.S. carriers, proceed to airfields on Guam for refueling and rearming, and then execute a second attack upon returning to their carriers. This plan was further augmented by the anticipated support of some 500 land-based aircraft stationed on Guam and surrounding islands.

input: Corey Clark was disqualified during the finals for having an undisclosed police record; however, he later alleged that he and Paula Abdul had an affair while on the show and that this contributed to his expulsion. input: Furthermore, despite the novel's thematic focus on racial injustice, its black characters are not fully examined. In its use of racial epithets, stereotyped depictions of superstitious blacks, and Calpurnia, who to some critics is an updated version of the "contented slave" motif and to others simply unexplored, the book is viewed as marginalizing black characters. One writer asserts that the use of Scout's narration serves as a convenient mechanism for readers to be innocent and detached from the racial conflict. Scout's voice "functions as the not-me which allows the rest of us—black and white, male and female—to find our relative position in society". A teaching guide for the novel published by The English Journal cautions, "what seems wonderful or powerful to one group of students may seem degrading to another". A Canadian language arts consultant found that the novel resonated well with white students, but that black students found it "demoralizing". Another criticism, articulated by Michael Lind, is that the novel indulges in classist stereotyping and demonization of poor rural "white trash".
rewrite: Moreover, notwithstanding the novel’s thematic engagement with racial injustice, its African American characters remain insufficiently developed. Through its employment of racial epithets, stereotypical portrayals of superstitious Black individuals, and the character of Calpurnia—interpreted by some critics as a modern iteration of the “contented slave” trope and by others as merely underexplored—the text is perceived as marginalizing Black perspectives. One scholar contends that Scout’s narrative voice operates as a convenient device, enabling readers to maintain innocence and detachment from racial tensions. Scout’s perspective “functions as the not-me which allows the rest of us—black and white, male and female—to find our relative position in society.” A pedagogical guide for the novel in *The English Journal* warns that “what seems wonderful or powerful to one group of students may seem degrading to another.” Research by a Canadian language arts consultant indicated that while the novel resonated strongly with white students, Black students often found it “demoralizing.” Further critique, articulated by Michael Lind, posits that the novel engages in classist stereotyping through its demonization of impoverished rural whites.

input: With the death of Zhengde and ascension of Jiajing, the politics at court shifted in favor of the Neo-Confucian establishment which not only rejected the Portuguese embassy of Fernão Pires de Andrade (d. 1523), but had a predisposed animosity towards Tibetan Buddhism and lamas. Evelyn S. Rawski, a professor in the Department of History of the University of Pittsburgh, writes that the Ming's unique relationship with Tibetan prelates essentially ended with Jiajing's reign while Ming influence in the Amdo region was supplanted by the Mongols.
rewrite: Following the demise of Emperor Zhengde and the accession of Jiajing, court politics realigned with Neo-Confucian orthodoxy. This establishment not only repudiated the Portuguese embassy led by Fernão Pires de Andrade (d. 1523) but also held a deep-seated antipathy toward Tibetan Buddhism. As historian Evelyn S. Rawski notes, the Ming dynasty's distinctive patronage of Tibetan prelates effectively concluded under Jiajing, concurrent with Mongol ascendancy supplanting Ming influence in the Amdo region.

input: St. John's served as the capital city of the Colony of Newfoundland and the Dominion of Newfoundland before Newfoundland became Canada's tenth province in 1949. The city now serves as the capital of Newfoundland and Labrador, therefore the provincial legislature is located in the city. The Confederation Building, located on Confederation Hill, is home to the House of Assembly along with the offices for the Members of the House of Assembly (MHAs) and Ministers. The city is represented by ten MHAs, four who are members of the governing Progressive Conservative Party, three that belong to the New Democratic Party (NDP), and three that belong to the Liberal Party. Lorraine Michael, leader of the NDP since 2006, represents the district of Signal Hill-Quidi Vidi.
rewrite: St. John’s functioned as the capital of both the Colony and Dominion of Newfoundland prior to the province’s accession to Canada in 1949. It remains the capital of Newfoundland and Labrador, hosting the provincial legislature. The House of Assembly, along with offices for Members of the House of Assembly (MHAs) and Ministers, is situated in the Confederation Building on Confederation Hill. The city is represented by ten MHAs: four from the governing Progressive Conservative Party, three from the New Democratic Party (NDP), and three from the Liberal Party. Since 2006, NDP leader Lorraine Michael has represented the district of Signal Hill-Quidi Vidi.

input: The Crimean War was a military conflict fought between October 1853 – March 1856 in which Russia lost to an alliance of France, the United Kingdom, the Ottoman Empire, and Sardinia. The immediate cause involved the rights of Christian minorities in the Holy Land, which was controlled by the Ottoman Empire. The French promoted the rights of Catholics, while Russia promoted those of the Eastern Orthodox Christians. The longer-term causes involved the decline of the Ottoman Empire and the unwillingness of the United Kingdom and France to allow Russia to gain territory and power at Ottoman expense. It has widely been noted that the causes, in one case involving an argument over a key, have never revealed a "greater confusion of purpose", yet led to a war noted for its "notoriously incompetent international butchery."
rewrite: The Crimean War, waged from October 1853 to March 1856, culminated in the defeat of Russia by an alliance comprising France, the United Kingdom, the Ottoman Empire, and Sardinia. The proximate cause centered on disputes over privileges for Christian minorities within the Ottoman-controlled Holy Land, with France advocating for Catholic rights and Russia for those of the Eastern Orthodox Church. Underlying this were longer-term geopolitical tensions stemming from the Ottoman Empire’s decline and the determination of Britain and France to prevent Russian territorial expansion at Ottoman expense. Historians have frequently observed that the conflict’s origins, at times descending into trivial disputes, reflect a profound confusion of political objectives, yet resulted in a war infamous for its military mismanagement and catastrophic casualties.

input: Private CBC affiliates are not as common as they were in the past, as many such stations have been purchased either by the CBC itself or by Canwest Global or CHUM Limited, respectively becoming E! or A-Channel (later A, now CTV Two) stations. One private CBC affiliate, CHBC-TV in Kelowna, joined E! (then known as CH) on February 27, 2006. When a private CBC affiliate reaffiliates with another network, the CBC has normally added a retransmitter of its nearest O&O station to ensure that CBC service is continued. However, due to an agreement between CHBC and CFJC-TV in Kamloops, CFJC also disaffiliated from the CBC on February 27, 2006, but no retransmitters were installed in the licence area. Former private CBC affiliates CKPG-TV Prince George and CHAT-TV Medicine Hat disaffiliated on August 31, 2008 and joined E!, but the CBC announced it will not add new retransmitters to these areas. Incidentally, CFJC, CKPG and CHAT are all owned by an independent media company, Jim Pattison Group. With the closure of E! and other changes in the media landscape, several former CBC affiliates have since joined City or Global, or closed altogether.
rewrite: The prevalence of privately-owned affiliates of the Canadian Broadcasting Corporation (CBC) has diminished over time, with many such stations having been acquired either by the CBC directly or by major broadcasters such as Canwest Global or CHUM Limited. These acquisitions typically resulted in their conversion into E! or A-Channel stations (subsequently rebranded as A and now CTV Two). Historically, when a private affiliate disaffiliated from the CBC to join another network, the CBC would routinely establish a retransmitter of its nearest owned-and-operated (O&O) station to maintain service continuity. This pattern, however, has seen notable exceptions. For instance, following the reaffiliation of CHBC-TV in Kelowna to E! (then known as CH) on February 27, 2006, and the concurrent disaffiliation of CFJC-TV in Kamloops due to a shared agreement, no retransmitters were installed within the relevant licence area. Similarly, upon the disaffiliation of CKPG-TV in Prince George and CHAT-TV in Medicine Hat on August 31, 2008—both of which subsequently joined E!—the CBC explicitly announced it would not deploy new retransmitters. These three stations are all held by the independent Jim Pattison Group. Subsequent to the discontinuation of E! and broader industry shifts, several former CBC affiliates have since aligned with City or Global networks, or ceased operations entirely.

input: Available web browsers range in features from minimal, text-based user interfaces with bare-bones support for HTML to rich user interfaces supporting a wide variety of file formats and protocols. Browsers which include additional components to support e-mail, Usenet news, and Internet Relay Chat (IRC), are sometimes referred to as "Internet suites" rather than merely "web browsers".
rewrite: Web browsers vary from basic, text-based interfaces with limited HTML support to advanced graphical interfaces accommodating diverse file formats and protocols. Those integrating additional functionalities such as email, Usenet news, and Internet Relay Chat (IRC) are often termed "Internet suites" rather than simply "web browsers."

input: While West had encountered controversy a year prior when he stormed out of the American Music Awards of 2004 after losing Best New Artist, the rapper's first large-scale controversy came just days following Late Registration's release, during a benefit concert for Hurricane Katrina victims. In September 2005, NBC broadcast A Concert for Hurricane Relief, and West was a featured speaker. When West was presenting alongside actor Mike Myers, he deviated from the prepared script. Myers spoke next and continued to read the script. Once it was West's turn to speak again, he said, "George Bush doesn't care about black people." West's comment reached much of the United States, leading to mixed reactions; President Bush would later call it one of the most "disgusting moments" of his presidency. West raised further controversy in January 2006 when he posed on the cover of Rolling Stone wearing a crown of thorns.
rewrite: The initial significant controversy involving the rapper occurred shortly after the release of *Late Registration*, during a televised benefit for Hurricane Katrina relief in September 2005. This followed a comparatively minor incident at the 2004 American Music Awards. As a featured speaker on NBC's *A Concert for Hurricane Relief*, West deviated from the prepared script while presenting with actor Mike Myers. After Myers continued reading his lines, West returned to the microphone and declared, "George Bush doesn't care about black people." The remark, broadcast nationally, elicited polarized responses, with President George W. Bush later denouncing it as a profoundly "disgusting" moment of his administration. West subsequently provoked additional debate in January 2006 by appearing on the cover of *Rolling Stone* magazine wearing a crown of thorns.

input: Where old disc recordings are considered to be of artistic or historic interest, from before the era of tape or where no tape master exists, archivists play back the disc on suitable equipment and record the result, typically onto a digital format, which can be copied and manipulated to remove analog flaws without any further damage to the source recording. For example, Nimbus Records uses a specially built horn record player to transfer 78s. Anyone can do this using a standard record player with a suitable pickup, a phono-preamp (pre-amplifier) and a typical personal computer. However, for accurate transfer, professional archivists carefully choose the correct stylus shape and diameter, tracking weight, equalisation curve and other playback parameters and use high-quality analogue-to-digital converters.
rewrite: When disc recordings from the pre-tape era, or instances where no tape master survives, possess artistic or historical significance, archivists undertake a playback transfer using appropriate equipment. The output is recorded, generally to a digital format, enabling subsequent copying and processing to mitigate analog imperfections without additional harm to the original source. As an illustration, Nimbus Records employs a custom-built horn gramophone for 78 rpm transfers. While a standard turntable with a suitable cartridge, phono preamplifier, and personal computer permits basic transfer, professional archival practice demands meticulous selection of stylus profile and size, tracking force, equalization, and other playback parameters, alongside high-quality analog-to-digital conversion, to ensure an accurate reproduction.

input: During her childhood, Madonna was inspired by actors, later saying, "I loved Carole Lombard and Judy Holliday and Marilyn Monroe. They were all incredibly funny ... and I saw myself in them ... my girlishness, my knowingness and my innocence." Her "Material Girl" music video recreated Monroe's look in the song "Diamonds Are a Girl's Best Friend", from the film Gentlemen Prefer Blondes (1953). She studied the screwball comedies of the 1930s, particularly those of Lombard, in preparation for the film Who's That Girl. The video for "Express Yourself" (1989) was inspired by Fritz Lang's silent film Metropolis (1927). The video for "Vogue" recreated the style of Hollywood glamour photographs, in particular those by Horst P. Horst, and imitated the poses of Marlene Dietrich, Carole Lombard, and Rita Hayworth, while the lyrics referred to many of the stars who had inspired her, including Bette Davis, described by Madonna as an idol. However, Madonna's film career has been largely received negatively by the film critic community. Stephanie Zacharek, critic for Time magazine, stated that, "[Madonna] seems wooden and unnatural as an actress, and it's tough to watch, because she's clearly trying her damnedest." According to biographer Andrew Morton, "Madonna puts a brave face on the criticism, but privately she is deeply hurt." After the box office bomb Swept Away (2002), Madonna vowed that she would never again act in a film, hoping her repertoire as a bad actress would never be discussed again.
rewrite:
Throughout her formative years, Madonna drew significant inspiration from cinematic figures, later reflecting, “I loved Carole Lombard and Judy Holliday and Marilyn Monroe. They were all incredibly funny ... and I saw myself in them ... my girlishness, my knowingness and my innocence.” This influence manifested directly in her artistic output. Her 1985 “Material Girl” music video deliberately recreated Monroe’s performance aesthetic from “Diamonds Are a Girl’s Best Friend” in the film *Gentlemen Prefer Blondes* (1953). Furthermore, she studied 1930s screwball comedies, particularly those featuring Carole Lombard, as preparation for her role in *Who’s That Girl* (1987). Her visual references extended beyond Hollywood, with the video for “Express Yourself” (1989) drawing inspiration from Fritz Lang’s silent film *Metropolis* (1927). The “Vogue” (1990) video emulated the style of Hollywood glamour photography, notably the work of Horst P. Horst, and replicated poses associated with Marlene Dietrich, Carole Lombard, and Rita Hayworth, while its lyrics paid homage to other inspirations like Bette Davis, whom Madonna identified as an idol.

Despite these deliberate cinematic engagements, Madonna’s film career has been predominantly criticized by film critics. Stephanie Zacharek of *Time* magazine observed that Madonna “seems wooden and unnatural as an actress, and it’s tough to watch, because she’s clearly trying her damnedest.” Biographer Andrew Morton noted that while “Madonna puts a brave face on the criticism, privately she is deeply hurt.” Following the commercial and critical failure of *Swept Away* (2002), Madonna resolved to cease acting in films, expressing a hope that her reputation as a poor actress would subsequently fade from discussion.

input: Another common application is the control of the throttle of an internal combustion engine in conjunction with an electronic governor. In this usage, the motor works against a return spring to move the throttle in accordance with the output of the governor. The latter monitors engine speed by counting electrical pulses from the ignition system or from a magnetic pickup and, depending on the speed, makes small adjustments to the amount of current applied to the motor. If the engine starts to slow down relative to the desired speed, the current will be increased, the motor will develop more torque, pulling against the return spring and opening the throttle. Should the engine run too fast, the governor will reduce the current being applied to the motor, causing the return spring to pull back and close the throttle.
rewrite: A further prevalent application involves the regulation of an internal combustion engine's throttle via an electronic governor. In this configuration, an electric motor operates against a return spring to adjust the throttle position based on the governor's signal. The governor tracks rotational speed by processing electrical pulses from either the ignition system or a magnetic sensor. It then modulates the current supplied to the motor to maintain the desired setpoint. Should engine speed decrease below the target, current is increased, enhancing motor torque to open the throttle against the spring force. Conversely, if speed exceeds the setpoint, current is reduced, allowing the return spring to close the throttle and decelerate the engine.

input: Sometimes people of mixed African-American and Native American descent report having had elder family members withholding pertinent genealogical information. Tracing the genealogy of African Americans can be a very difficult process, as censuses did not identify slaves by name before the American Civil War, meaning that most African Americans did not appear by name in those records. In addition, many white fathers who used slave women sexually, even those in long-term relationships like Thomas Jefferson's with Sally Hemings, did not acknowledge their mixed-race slave children in records, so paternity was lost.
rewrite: Genealogical research among African Americans is often impeded by historical record-keeping practices. Prior to the Civil War, censuses omitted the names of enslaved individuals, creating a significant documentary void. Furthermore, paternal lines are frequently obscured because white fathers, including those in sustained relationships with enslaved women, typically did not legally acknowledge their mixed-race children. Some individuals of African-American and Native American descent also report that elder family members have withheld pertinent familial information, compounding these archival challenges.

input: Minute Maid Park (home of the Astros) and Toyota Center (home of the Rockets), are located in downtown Houston. Houston has the NFL's first retractable-roof stadium with natural grass, NRG Stadium (home of the Texans). Minute Maid Park is also a retractable-roof stadium. Toyota Center also has the largest screen for an indoor arena in the United States built to coincide with the arena's hosting of the 2013 NBA All-Star Game. BBVA Compass Stadium is a soccer-specific stadium for the Dynamo, the Texas Southern University football team, and Dash, located in East Downtown. In addition, NRG Astrodome was the first indoor stadium in the world, built in 1965. Other sports facilities include Hofheinz Pavilion (Houston Cougars basketball), Rice Stadium (Rice Owls football), and Reliant Arena. TDECU Stadium is where the University of Houston Houston Cougars football team plays. Houston has hosted several major sports events: the 1968, 1986 and 2004 Major League Baseball All-Star Games; the 1989, 2006 and 2013 NBA All-Star Games; Super Bowl VIII and Super Bowl XXXVIII, as well as hosting the 2005 World Series and 1981, 1986, 1994 and 1995 NBA Finals, winning the latter two. Super Bowl LI is currently slated to be hosted in NRG Stadium in 2017.
rewrite:
Houston's downtown area hosts several major sporting venues, including Minute Maid Park, home to Major League Baseball's Houston Astros, and the Toyota Center, home to the National Basketball Association's Houston Rockets. Both facilities feature retractable roofs, with the Toyota Center also containing the largest video display in any United States indoor arena, an installation that coincided with its hosting of the 2013 NBA All-Star Game. The city is also notable for NRG Stadium, home of the National Football League's Houston Texans, which was the NFL's first retractable-roof stadium to utilize a natural grass playing surface. Further contributing to Houston's sporting infrastructure is BBVA Compass Stadium, a soccer-specific venue in East Downtown that hosts the Houston Dynamo (MLS), the Houston Dash (NWSL), and the Texas Southern University football team.

Historically, the NRG Astrodome, constructed in 1965, is recognized as the world's first fully enclosed, air-conditioned stadium. Other significant facilities include TDECU Stadium (University of Houston football), Hofheinz Pavilion (University of Houston basketball), Rice Stadium (Rice University football), and Reliant Arena. The metropolitan area has served as host for numerous premier events, such as the MLB All-Star Games in 1968, 1986, and 2004; the NBA All-Star Games in 1989, 2006, and 2013; Super Bowls VIII and XXXVIII; the 2005 World Series; and the NBA Finals in 1981, 1986, 1994, and 1995, with the Houston Rockets winning the latter two championships. Super Bowl LI is scheduled for NRG Stadium in 2017.

input: Numerous major American cultural movements began in the city, such as the Harlem Renaissance, which established the African-American literary canon in the United States. The city was a center of jazz in the 1940s, abstract expressionism in the 1950s, and the birthplace of hip hop in the 1970s. The city's punk and hardcore scenes were influential in the 1970s and 1980s. New York has long had a flourishing scene for Jewish American literature.
rewrite: The city has served as a foundational site for numerous pivotal American cultural movements. These include the Harlem Renaissance, which established the African-American literary canon, and the emergence of hip hop in the 1970s. It was also a central hub for jazz in the 1940s, abstract expressionism in the 1950s, and influential punk and hardcore scenes from the 1970s-80s, alongside a longstanding tradition of Jewish American literature.

input: Richard Phillips Feynman was born on May 11, 1918, in Queens, New York City, the son of Lucille (née Phillips), a homemaker, and Melville Arthur Feynman, a sales manager. His family originated from Russia and Poland; both of his parents were Ashkenazi Jews. They were not religious, and by his youth Feynman described himself as an "avowed atheist". He also stated "To select, for approbation the peculiar elements that come from some supposedly Jewish heredity is to open the door to all kinds of nonsense on racial theory," and adding "... at thirteen I was not only converted to other religious views, but I also stopped believing that the Jewish people are in any way 'the chosen people'." Later in his life, during a visit to the Jewish Theological Seminary, he encountered the Talmud for the first time, and remarked that he found it a "wonderful book" and "valuable".
rewrite: Richard Phillips Feynman was born on May 11, 1918, in Queens, New York City. His parents were Lucille (née Phillips), a homemaker, and Melville Arthur Feynman, a sales manager. The family had origins in Russia and Poland, and both parents were of Ashkenazi Jewish heritage. While raised in a secular household, Feynman explicitly identified as an "avowed atheist" from his youth. He rejected notions of ethnic or religious superiority, criticizing the selection of "peculiar elements from some supposedly Jewish heredity" as opening "the door to all kinds of nonsense on racial theory." He further noted that by age thirteen he had ceased to believe in the concept of Jews as "the chosen people." In later life, however, during a visit to the Jewish Theological Seminary, he encountered the Talmud for the first time and described it as both a "wonderful" and a "valuable" book.

input: In 118 BC, King Micipsa of Numidia (current-day Algeria and Tunisia) died. He was succeeded by two legitimate sons, Adherbal and Hiempsal, and an illegitimate son, Jugurtha. Micipsa divided his kingdom between these three sons. Jugurtha, however, turned on his brothers, killing Hiempsal and driving Adherbal out of Numidia. Adherbal fled to Rome for assistance, and initially Rome mediated a division of the country between the two brothers. Eventually, Jugurtha renewed his offensive, leading to a long and inconclusive war with Rome. He also bribed several Roman commanders, and at least two tribunes, before and during the war. His nemesis, Gaius Marius, a legate from a virtually unknown provincial family, returned from the war in Numidia and was elected consul in 107 BC over the objections of the aristocratic senators. Marius invaded Numidia and brought the war to a quick end, capturing Jugurtha in the process. The apparent incompetence of the Senate, and the brilliance of Marius, had been put on full display. The populares party took full advantage of this opportunity by allying itself with Marius.
rewrite: Upon the death of King Micipsa of Numidia in 118 BC, his kingdom, located in the region of present-day Algeria and Tunisia, was divided among his two legitimate heirs, Adherbal and Hiempsal, and his illegitimate son, Jugurtha. Jugurtha subsequently initiated a violent usurpation, murdering Hiempsal and forcibly expelling Adherbal from the territory. Adherbal sought refuge and intervention from Rome, which initially brokered a partition of Numidia between the surviving claimants. Jugurtha, however, resumed hostilities, instigating a protracted and indecisive conflict with the Roman Republic. His strategies included the corruption of multiple Roman military commanders and at least two tribunes, both prior to and during the hostilities. The war was ultimately concluded by Gaius Marius, a legate from an obscure provincial background who returned from Numidia to be elected consul in 107 BC despite senatorial opposition. Marius’s swift invasion culminated in the capture of Jugurtha. This outcome starkly contrasted the perceived inefficacy of the Senatorial aristocracy with the demonstrated competence of Marius, a disparity effectively exploited by the *populares* faction through their political alliance with the victorious general.

input: The sixty-one year reign of the Kangxi Emperor was the longest of any Chinese emperor. Kangxi's reign is also celebrated as the beginning of an era known as the "High Qing", during which the dynasty reached the zenith of its social, economic and military power. Kangxi's long reign started when he was eight years old upon the untimely demise of his father. To prevent a repeat of Dorgon's dictatorial monopolizing of power during the regency, the Shunzhi Emperor, on his deathbed, hastily appointed four senior cabinet ministers to govern on behalf of his young son. The four ministers — Sonin, Ebilun, Suksaha, and Oboi — were chosen for their long service, but also to counteract each other's influences. Most important, the four were not closely related to the imperial family and laid no claim to the throne. However, as time passed, through chance and machination, Oboi, the most junior of the four, achieved such political dominance as to be a potential threat. Even though Oboi's loyalty was never an issue, his personal arrogance and political conservatism led him into an escalating conflict with the young emperor. In 1669 Kangxi, through trickery, disarmed and imprisoned Oboi — a significant victory for a fifteen-year-old emperor over a wily politician and experienced commander.
rewrite: The sixty-one-year reign of the Kangxi Emperor represents the lengthiest tenure of any sovereign in Chinese history. This period is widely regarded as inaugurating the "High Qing" era, characterized by the dynasty's apex in social, economic, and military authority. Kangxi ascended the throne at the age of eight following the premature death of his father, the Shunzhi Emperor. To avert a recurrence of the dictatorial regency exercised earlier by Dorgon, the dying emperor hastily appointed four senior cabinet ministers—Sonin, Ebilun, Suksaha, and Oboi—to govern as a regency council. Selected for their extensive service and mutual counterbalance, these ministers were deliberately not members of the imperial clan and thus posed no direct threat to the dynastic succession. Over time, however, Oboi, initially the most junior among them, consolidated singular political dominance through circumstance and intrigue, emerging as a potential threat. Although his loyalty remained ostensibly intact, Oboi's personal arrogance and political conservatism engendered escalating friction with the adolescent emperor. In 1669, Kangxi, then fifteen, orchestrated Oboi's arrest and imprisonment through a calculated stratagem, a decisive victory that demonstrated the young monarch's political acumen over a seasoned and formidable opponent.

input: The FAA gradually assumed additional functions. The hijacking epidemic of the 1960s had already brought the agency into the field of civil aviation security. In response to the hijackings on September 11, 2001, this responsibility is now primarily taken by the Department of Homeland Security. The FAA became more involved with the environmental aspects of aviation in 1968 when it received the power to set aircraft noise standards. Legislation in 1970 gave the agency management of a new airport aid program and certain added responsibilities for airport safety. During the 1960s and 1970s, the FAA also started to regulate high altitude (over 500 feet) kite and balloon flying.
rewrite: The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) progressively expanded its operational scope. The agency initially entered the domain of civil aviation security during the hijacking epidemic of the 1960s, though this primary responsibility was later transferred to the Department of Homeland Security following the events of September 11, 2001. In 1968, the FAA engaged with environmental considerations by acquiring authority to establish aircraft noise standards. Subsequent legislation in 1970 granted it management of a new airport aid program and further airport safety duties. Additionally, throughout the 1960s and 1970s, the FAA began regulating high-altitude (exceeding 500 feet) kite and balloon operations.

input: In 1654, Otto von Guericke invented the first vacuum pump and conducted his famous Magdeburg hemispheres experiment, showing that teams of horses could not separate two hemispheres from which the air had been partially evacuated. Robert Boyle improved Guericke's design and with the help of Robert Hooke further developed vacuum pump technology. Thereafter, research into the partial vacuum lapsed until 1850 when August Toepler invented the Toepler Pump and Heinrich Geissler invented the mercury displacement pump in 1855, achieving a partial vacuum of about 10 Pa (0.1 Torr). A number of electrical properties become observable at this vacuum level, which renewed interest in further research.
rewrite: In 1654, Otto von Guericke invented the initial vacuum pump and demonstrated its power through the Magdeburg hemispheres experiment, proving that teams of horses could not pull apart two hemispheres from which air had been partially removed. Robert Boyle subsequently enhanced this design, and with Robert Hooke, advanced vacuum technology. Investigation into partial vacuums then diminished until 1850, when August Toepler invented the Toepler Pump, followed by Heinrich Geissler's mercury displacement pump in 1855, achieving a partial vacuum of approximately 10 Pa (0.1 Torr). This degree of vacuum rendered various electrical properties observable, thereby reinvigorating scientific interest in further research.

input: The Han-era family was patrilineal and typically had four to five nuclear family members living in one household. Multiple generations of extended family members did not occupy the same house, unlike families of later dynasties. According to Confucian family norms, various family members were treated with different levels of respect and intimacy. For example, there were different accepted time frames for mourning the death of a father versus a paternal uncle. Arranged marriages were normal, with the father's input on his offspring's spouse being considered more important than the mother's. Monogamous marriages were also normal, although nobles and high officials were wealthy enough to afford and support concubines as additional lovers. Under certain conditions dictated by custom, not law, both men and women were able to divorce their spouses and remarry.
rewrite: The Han dynasty family structure was patrilineal, with households typically comprising four to five nuclear family members. Contrary to patterns in subsequent dynasties, co-residence of multiple extended generations was uncommon. Confucian principles dictated a hierarchical framework of respect and intimacy among relatives, exemplified by prescribed variations in mourning periods, such as those for a father compared to a paternal uncle. Marital unions were predominantly arranged, with paternal authority outweighing maternal influence in spouse selection. While monogamy was the standard practice, elite males often maintained concubines. Furthermore, both genders possessed the customary, though not legally codified, capacity to initiate divorce and subsequently remarry.

input: Part of the Russian resistance was credited[by whom?] to the deployment of newly invented blockade mines. Perhaps the most influential contributor to the development of naval mining was a Swede resident in Russia, the inventor and civil engineer Immanuel Nobel (the father of Alfred Nobel). Immanuel Nobel helped the Russian war effort by applying his knowledge of industrial explosives, such as nitroglycerin and gunpowder. One account dates modern naval mining from the Crimean War: "Torpedo mines, if I may use this name given by Fulton to self-acting mines underwater, were among the novelties attempted by the Russians in their defences about Cronstadt and Sevastopol", as one American officer put it in 1860.
rewrite: A portion of Russian defensive success has been attributed to the implementation of newly developed blockade mines. A pivotal figure in advancing naval mining technology was the Swedish-born inventor and civil engineer Immanuel Nobel, resident in Russia and father of Alfred Nobel. He supported the Russian military by applying his expertise in industrial explosives, including nitroglycerin and gunpowder. Modern naval mining is frequently dated to the Crimean War, as noted in an 1860 account by an American officer: "Torpedo mines...were among the novelties attempted by the Russians in their defences about Cronstadt and Sevastopol."

input: In 1838, Claridge obtained patents in Scotland on 27 March, and Ireland on 23 April, and in 1851 extensions were sought for all three patents, by the trustees of a company previously formed by Claridge. This was Claridge's Patent Asphalte Company, formed in 1838 for the purpose of introducing to Britain "Asphalte in its natural state from the mine at Pyrimont Seysell in France", and "laid one of the first asphalt pavements in Whitehall". Trials were made of the pavement in 1838 on the footway in Whitehall, the stable at Knightsbridge Barracks, "and subsequently on the space at the bottom of the steps leading from Waterloo Place to St. James Park". "The formation in 1838 of Claridge's Patent Asphalte Company (with a distinguished list of aristocratic patrons, and Marc and Isambard Brunel as, respectively, a trustee and consulting engineer), gave an enormous impetus to the development of a British asphalt industry". "By the end of 1838, at least two other companies, Robinson's and the Bastenne company, were in production", with asphalt being laid as paving at Brighton, Herne Bay, Canterbury, Kensington, the Strand, and a large floor area in Bunhill-row, while meantime Claridge's Whitehall paving "continue(d) in good order".
rewrite: In March and April of 1838, John Claridge secured patents in Scotland and Ireland, respectively. Extensions for these patents, along with a third, were later pursued in 1851 by the trustees of a company he had previously established. This entity, Claridge’s Patent Asphalte Company, was incorporated in 1838 with the objective of importing natural asphalt from the Pyrimont Seysell mine in France to Britain. The company was instrumental in laying one of the nation’s earliest asphalt pavements in Whitehall. Initial trials took place that same year on a Whitehall footway, the stable at Knightsbridge Barracks, and subsequently on the area at the base of the steps from Waterloo Place into St. James’s Park. The company’s formation, supported by a distinguished roster of aristocratic patrons and with Marc and Isambard Brunel serving as trustee and consulting engineer, provided significant momentum for the British asphalt industry. By the close of 1838, at least two additional firms, Robinson’s and the Bastenne company, were also operational. Their asphalt was deployed for paving in locations including Brighton, Herne Bay, Canterbury, Kensington, the Strand, and a substantial floor in Bunhill Row, while Claridge’s original Whitehall pavement reportedly remained in good condition.

input: In South Australia, initially a Liberal and Country Party affiliated party, the Liberal and Country League (LCL), mostly led by Premier of South Australia Tom Playford, was in power from the 1933 election to the 1965 election, though with assistance from an electoral malapportionment, or gerrymander, known as the Playmander. The LCL's Steele Hall governed for one term from the 1968 election to the 1970 election and during this time began the process of dismantling the Playmander. David Tonkin, as leader of the South Australian Division of the Liberal Party of Australia, became Premier at the 1979 election for one term, losing office at the 1982 election. The Liberals returned to power at the 1993 election, led by Premiers Dean Brown, John Olsen and Rob Kerin through two terms, until their defeat at the 2002 election. They have since remained in opposition under a record five Opposition Leaders.
rewrite: In South Australia, political dominance was maintained by the Liberal and Country League (LCL)—initially affiliated with the Liberal and Country Party—from the 1933 election until 1965, primarily under Premier Tom Playford. This prolonged tenure was facilitated by a significant electoral malapportionment, colloquially termed the Playmander. Following this period, the LCL's Steele Hall governed from 1968 to 1970, initiating the dismantling of the Playmander. Subsequently, David Tonkin, leading the South Australian Division of the Liberal Party of Australia, secured a single term as Premier following the 1979 election, departing office after the 1982 election. The Liberal Party regained power at the 1993 election, with Premiers Dean Brown, John Olsen, and Rob Kerin serving across two terms until defeat in 2002. Since that time, the party has remained in opposition under a record five consecutive Opposition Leaders.

input: The phrase "in whole or in part" has been subject to much discussion by scholars of international humanitarian law. The International Criminal Tribunal for the Former Yugoslavia found in Prosecutor v. Radislav Krstic – Trial Chamber I – Judgment – IT-98-33 (2001) ICTY8 (2 August 2001) that Genocide had been committed. In Prosecutor v. Radislav Krstic – Appeals Chamber – Judgment – IT-98-33 (2004) ICTY 7 (19 April 2004) paragraphs 8, 9, 10, and 11 addressed the issue of in part and found that "the part must be a substantial part of that group. The aim of the Genocide Convention is to prevent the intentional destruction of entire human groups, and the part targeted must be significant enough to have an impact on the group as a whole." The Appeals Chamber goes into details of other cases and the opinions of respected commentators on the Genocide Convention to explain how they came to this conclusion.
rewrite: The phrase "in whole or in part" within the context of genocide has been extensively analyzed within international humanitarian law scholarship. Judicial interpretation was notably provided by the International Criminal Tribunal for the Former Yugoslavia. In *Prosecutor v. Radislav Krstić*, the Trial Chamber initially found genocide to have been committed (Judgment, IT-98-33, 2001). Subsequently, the Appeals Chamber (Judgment, IT-98-33, 2004) elaborated on the meaning of "in part" in paragraphs 8-11. It determined that the targeted "part" must constitute a substantial portion of the protected group. This interpretation aligns with the Genocide Convention's object and purpose of preventing the intentional destruction of entire human groups, requiring that the targeted segment be significant enough to impact the group's overall viability. The Appeals Chamber substantiated this conclusion through a detailed examination of relevant jurisprudence and the commentaries of respected authorities on the Convention.

input: Iran received access to the Internet in 1993. According to 2014 census, around 40% of the population of Iran are Internet users. Iran ranks 24th among countries by number of Internet users. According to the statistics provided by the web information company of Alexa, Google Search and Yahoo! are the most used search engines in Iran. Over 80% of the users of Telegram, a cloud-based instant messaging service, are from Iran. Instagram is the most popular online social networking service in Iran. Direct access to Facebook has been blocked in Iran since the 2009 Iranian presidential election protests, due to organization of the opposition movements on the website; but however, Facebook has around 12 to 17 million users in Iran who are using virtual private networks and proxy servers to access the website. Around 90% of Iran's e-commerce takes place on the Iranian online store of Digikala, which has around 750,000 visitors per day and more than 2.3 million subscribers. Digikala is the most visited online store in the Middle East, and ranks 4th among the most visited websites in Iran.
rewrite: Iran obtained internet connectivity in 1993. As of a 2014 census, approximately 40% of the national population were internet users, positioning Iran 24th globally by this metric. Statistical data from the web analytics firm Alexa indicate that Google Search and Yahoo! are the most utilized search engines within the country. The cloud-based messaging application Telegram reports that over 80% of its user base originates from Iran, while Instagram is the predominant social networking platform. Direct access to Facebook has been prohibited since the 2009 presidential election protests, owing to its use by opposition movements for organization. Nevertheless, an estimated 12 to 17 million Iranian users circumvent this restriction via virtual private networks and proxy servers. Approximately 90% of national e-commerce is conducted through the domestic online retailer Digikala, which attracts around 750,000 daily visitors and maintains over 2.3 million subscribers. This platform is the most frequented online store in the Middle East and ranks as the fourth most visited website in Iran.

input: A large number of Bell's writings, personal correspondence, notebooks, papers and other documents reside at both the United States Library of Congress Manuscript Division (as the Alexander Graham Bell Family Papers), and at the Alexander Graham Bell Institute, Cape Breton University, Nova Scotia; major portions of which are available for online viewing.
